Customer Account Self-Service

Account Statement Generation and Delivery

1. Re-sequence transactions by card numberdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

A scheduled step that puts every transaction in order by card number, then by transaction ID, so statements can be built one card at a time. The statement operations team runs it before statements are produced. It must never lose, duplicate or reorder transactions, and if the step fails it must not leave a partial work copy behind.

As a statement operations team, I want the transaction master re-sorted by card number and transaction ID into a work copy, so that statements can be built card by card.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#1

Open questions

  • SME-030 When producing statements, if the customer or account for a card cannot be found, should that statement be skipped, the run stopped, or an exception recorded? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-031 On statements, should address line 3, state, country and ZIP each be cut off at their first space, even when the value has more than one word? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-032 Statement production assumes card cross-references are processed in ascending card number order, matching the sorted transactions. Must the new system guarantee that order? (Data architecture team)
  • DEF-101 Is this intended? The reformatting copies only 50 bytes from position 279 of the transaction record, while the two timestamps there take 52 bytes, so the last 2 bytes of the processed timestamp are dropped from the work copy. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Produce a card-ordered extract of all transactions, sorted ascending by card number (16 characters) and then by transaction ID. Store it as a staging data set or a query or view that later steps read in that order. The new application does not have to copy the card number to the front of each record or use 350-byte fixed records. What matters is the sort order and that every transaction is included. Re-sequence transactions by card number
2. Load and group card-ordered transactionsdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 5 criteria

Loads the card-ordered transactions into a store keyed by card number and transaction ID, and groups them by card. This lets each statement list only that card's transactions, in transaction-ID order. It must never put a transaction under the wrong card, and it must not silently drop transactions when the legacy limits (51 cards, 10 transactions per card) are exceeded.

As a statement operations team, I want the card-ordered transactions loaded into a keyed file and grouped by card, so that each card's statement lists exactly that card's transactions in transaction-ID order.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-004design noteWhen every earlier step of the statement job ended with return code 0, the system shall copy every record of the card-ordered work copy (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRXFL.SEQ) into the keyed transaction file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRXFL.VSAM.KSDS), keyed on card number followed by transaction ID.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-005design noteWhile loading the card-and-transaction-ID-sorted transaction extract, the system shall add each transaction to the current card's slot while the card number is unchanged, and on a new card number shall close the previous card's transaction count and open a new card slot with a count of 1.AC-03
REQ-N-001design noteThe system shall hold at most 51 distinct cards for the whole transaction file and at most 10 transactions per card in memory, with no check when either limit is exceeded.AC-04, AC-05

Decision tables

Open questions

  • SME-030 When producing statements, if the customer or account for a card cannot be found, should that statement be skipped, the run stopped, or an exception recorded? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-031 On statements, should address line 3, state, country and ZIP each be cut off at their first space, even when the value has more than one word? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-032 Statement production assumes card cross-references are processed in ascending card number order, matching the sorted transactions. Must the new system guarantee that order? (Data architecture team)
  • DEF-174 Is this intended? Loading never checks the 51-card or 10-transaction limit, so larger files overrun the table instead of being rejected or handled. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Make card-ordered transactions available by the composite key (card number, transaction ID). An indexed table or a keyed staging store works. Load it only after every earlier step of the statement job has succeeded. Copy every record, and run the load as a gated step in the scheduled job. Load card-ordered transactions into keyed file
  • Group the sorted transactions by card number: a control break opens a new group with a count of 1 when the card number changes and adds to the current group while it stays the same. In the new application this is a group-by on card number that keeps transaction-ID order within each card. Group transactions by card in table
  • The legacy program holds at most 51 cards and 10 transactions per card in memory and does not check either limit. The new application should not have these fixed limits. It can stream or query per card, or size its collections dynamically. If a limit has to stay, exceeding it must be reported, not ignored. The business has to confirm whether to keep the legacy truncation. In-memory capacity limit of 51 cards x 10 transactions per card
3. Produce one statement per carddraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 7 rules · 9 criteria

The scheduled statement run produces one statement for every card in the card cross-reference, in plain text and in HTML. Each statement combines the cardholder's customer and account details with that card's transactions. It must produce exactly one statement per card, and if the run fails it must keep no statements from that run.

As a cardholder, I want a monthly statement in plain text and HTML for each of my cards, so that I can see my account details and transactions.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#3

Decision tables

Open questions

  • SME-030 When producing statements, if the customer or account for a card cannot be found, should that statement be skipped, the run stopped, or an exception recorded? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-031 On statements, should address line 3, state, country and ZIP each be cut off at their first space, even when the value has more than one word? (Statement operations business owner)
  • SME-032 Statement production assumes card cross-references are processed in ascending card number order, matching the sorted transactions. Must the new system guarantee that order? (Data architecture team)
  • SME-033 Should there be one statement per card, or one per account covering all its cards? (Card servicing business owner)

Design notes

  • A scheduled statement job that runs only after the earlier steps succeed. It reads card-ordered transactions, the card cross-reference, accounts and customers, and writes two new outputs per run: a plain-text statement report and an HTML statement report. The 80- and 100-character line widths only matter if the text output must match the legacy layout exactly. Produce text and HTML card statements
  • Fixed order for the run: open both outputs, load the card transactions, open the cross-reference, customer and account sources, build every statement, then release all inputs and close the outputs. In the new application, make the transactions available before statement building starts, and finalise the outputs only after every statement is built. Fixed processing sequence: load transactions, open masters, then produce statements
  • Every data source has the lifecycle open, read one or more times, close. The new application can do this with scoped resources such as connections or readers that are always released, including on failure. File status passed back to the caller as the outcome code
  • For each cross-reference record, look up the customer by its customer ID and the account by its account ID, then write the header and details, the transactions, the total and the footer. Both lookups use the primary key of their record. Produce one statement per card
4. Show statement header and holder detailsdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 6 criteria

The top of each statement tells the cardholder whose account it covers: the cardholder's name and address, the account ID, current balance and FICO score. The HTML version also shows the issuer, Bank of XYZ. Names, addresses and the balance must come from the right customer and account records, formatted exactly as specified, with negative balances clearly marked.

As a cardholder, I want my statement to show the issuer, my name, address and basic account details, so that I know whose account the statement covers and its current position.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#4

5. List card transactions and totaldraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 9 criteria

Each statement lists every transaction on that card, in transaction-ID order, with its ID, description and amount. The text statement ends with a total of the amounts. The statement must never miss one of the card's transactions or include another card's, and the total must be the exact signed sum of the listed amounts.

As a cardholder, I want my statement to list each transaction on my card with a total, so that I can check what was charged to my account.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#5

REQ-F-020formattingWhen a statement is produced for a card, the system shall list every transaction held for that card number on both the text and HTML statements, one line each showing transaction ID, description (first 49 characters) and amount with a trailing minus sign for negative amounts.AC-06

6. Stop the statement run on file errorsdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 7 criteria · 2 gaps

If any statement data cannot be opened, read or closed, the run stops with a clear message naming the file and the return code, and no statements from that run are issued. Its main audience is the statement operations team. It must never issue a statement built from missing customer or account data, and it must never carry on after a file error.

As a statement operations team, I want the statement run to stop with a clear message when a file cannot be opened, read or closed, so that no incomplete statements are issued.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#6

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-026error handlingIf the customer record for a cross-reference card cannot be read (any result other than '00'), then the system shall display 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' with the return code and abend, producing no further statements.AC-02
REQ-F-027error handlingIf the account record for a cross-reference card cannot be read (any result other than '00'), then the system shall display 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' with the return code and abend.AC-03

REQ-F-030error handlingIf opening, closing or making the first read of the transaction file, or opening or closing the cross-reference, customer or account file, returns anything other than '00' or '04', then the system shall display 'ERROR OPENING <file>', 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE' or 'ERROR CLOSING <file>' with the return code and abend.AC-06
REQ-F-031error handlingIf a later read of the transaction file during loading returns anything other than '00' or end of file '10', then the system shall display 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE' with the return code and abend.AC-07

7. Read-only statement data accessdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 8 criteria

Statement data is read only through a data-access layer that reads files and reports each outcome. Producing statements therefore never changes customer, account, card or transaction records. The layer must never write, change or delete data, and it must report not-found and end-of-data outcomes accurately so the run can stop or continue correctly.

As a statement operations team, I want statement data read through a routine that only reads files and returns each file outcome, so that producing statements never changes customer, account, card or transaction records.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data, security. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#7

Open questions

  • SME-035 Does the caller always pass a key length of 9 for customer lookups and 11 for account lookups? Should the new system check the key length, and check that the account key is numeric, before looking it up? (Application architect)
  • DEF-175 Is this intended? An operation a file does not support (for example 'R' on CUSTFILE, or 'W' or 'Z' on any file) does nothing but still returns that file's last status, often '00', so the caller would take it as success; an unknown file name returns without setting any outcome code. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Look up a customer directly by primary key (customer ID) and return the record, or a 'not found' result that the caller can tell apart from other failures. The legacy program passes the key length in from the caller. The new application should use a typed customer ID instead. Keyed customer/account lookup uses caller-supplied key length
  • Look up an account directly by its 11-digit account ID (primary key) and return the record or a clear 'not found' result. Validate the ID as 11 digits rather than relying on a key length the caller supplies. Keyed customer/account lookup uses caller-supplied key length
  • Every data source the statement job uses follows the lifecycle open, read one or more times, close. Use scoped resources that are always released, including when the run fails. File status passed back to the caller as the outcome code
  • Transactions must be readable in order of (card number, transaction ID), and the card cross-reference in card-number order. These are ordered sequential reads, such as streams or cursors over a sorted query, with a clear end-of-data signal. Statement data access: allowed operations per file
  • Customers and accounts are needed only for keyed point lookups. No scans or ordered reads are needed for them. Statement data access: allowed operations per file
  • The statement job's data access must be read-only. Use read-only connections or a read replica with credentials that cannot write. Expose no write or update operations, even though the legacy routine defines 'W' and 'Z' operation codes. Statement data access: allowed operations per file
8. Publish statements as PDFdraft · scheduled job · 1 requirements · 1 rules · 1 criterion

Once statements have been created, the text statements are converted to PDF so cardholders can view and keep them in a standard format. The PDF must contain exactly the statements from the completed run, and it must never be published from a failed or partial run.

As a cardholder, I want my account statement delivered as a PDF, so that I can view and keep it in a standard format.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/AccountStatementGenerationandDelivery#8

Open questions

  • SME-298 What should the modernized statement PDF output be called, and where should it be stored? Today it is known only by the legacy dataset name AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS.PDF. (Statement operations team)
  • SME-299 The statement PDF conversion only runs if every earlier step ended with return code 0, yet it is the job's only business step. Which earlier steps does this cover, and should the modernized system keep this check? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-300 If the statement PDF conversion fails or is rerun, should a rerun overwrite the existing PDF, and is a partial PDF acceptable after a failure? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-301 The browse option (BROWSE Y) is described only as making the statement PDF viewable. Which PDF properties must the modernized conversion keep to meet this intent? (Statement operations team)
  • DEF-102 Is this intended? The step carries COND=(0,NE), which looks meant to skip conversion after a failure, but as the first and only step it has nothing to test, so the PDF is produced even if the statement job's output is incomplete. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A scheduled follow-on step that starts when statement creation completes. It renders the plain-text statement report to PDF and stores the result as the published statement document (legacy name AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.STATEMNT.PS.PDF), for example in document storage. Any text-to-PDF renderer works. The legacy job uses the TXT2PDF utility with BROWSE Y. Convert account statements to PDF

Daily Transaction Processing and Reporting

1. Extract account data to output filesfinal · scheduled job · 12 requirements · 13 rules · 15 criteria

A scheduled extract that reads every account on the account master and writes it out in four formats for downstream processes: a flat account record, a balance array record, and two variable-length records (one with status, one with financial details). It serves operations analysts and the systems that consume these extracts. It must never skip or duplicate an account, so N accounts always give N, N and 2N records. It must also stop the run on any read or write error rather than produce a partial extract.

As an operations analyst, I want each account on the account master file extracted to the account output, balance array and variable-length files, so that downstream processes receive the account details in the formats they expect.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001design noteWhen an account record is read successfully, the system shall copy the account ID, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiration date, current cycle credit and group ID to the account output record.AC-11
REQ-F-002design noteWhen an account record is read successfully, the system shall convert the account reissue date from YYYY-MM-DD to YYYYMMDD and write it as the output reissue date.AC-12
REQ-F-003business ruleWhen the account's current cycle debit equals zero, the system shall set the output current cycle debit to 2525.00.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-004business ruleThe system shall not copy a non-zero current cycle debit to the account output record.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-005historical artifactWhen an account record is read successfully, the system shall write a balance array record holding the account identifier and the current balance in cycle slots 1 and 2 with cycle debits 1005.00 and 1525.00, and slot 3 with balance -1025.00 and cycle debit -2500.00.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-006design noteWhen an account record is read successfully, the system shall write a 12-byte variable-length status record holding the 11-digit account ID followed by the account active status.AC-13
REQ-F-007design noteWhen an account record is read successfully, the system shall then write a 39-byte variable-length financial record holding the account ID, current balance, credit limit and the four-digit year of the reissue date.AC-14
REQ-F-008design noteWhen an account is read successfully from the account master file, the system shall write one account output record, one balance array record and two variable-length records and then read the next account, so that N accounts give N, N and 2N records.AC-07
REQ-F-009error handlingWhen a write to any of the three output files returns file status '00' or '10', the system shall treat the write as successful and continue processing.AC-08
REQ-F-010error handlingIf a write to the account output file, the balance array file or either variable-length record write returns a file status other than '00' or '10', then the system shall display 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' with the status, 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the four-digit status and 'ABENDING PROGRAM', and abend with code 999.AC-09
REQ-F-011design noteWhen reading the account master file returns status '10', the system shall treat it as end of file, stop reading, close the account file and end normally with 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT01C'.AC-10
REQ-F-012error handlingIf reading the account master file returns a status other than '00' or '10', then the system shall display 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' with the file status and abend with code 999.AC-15

Open questions

  • SME-006 The account extract replaces a zero cycle debit with 2,525.00, and the balance array record is filled with fixed amounts (cycle debits 1,005.00, 1,525.00 and -2,500.00; a balance of -1,025.00). Are these real business values or test data to be replaced? And when an account has a non-zero cycle debit, should its own value be carried through to the extract? (Business analyst)
  • SME-007 The extract accepts a write result of '10' as well as '00' as success. Should accepting '10' be kept in the new system? (Technical lead)
  • SME-008 Do downstream consumers depend on the exact fixed record layouts of the account extracts (including the different status and financial record lengths), so they must be kept? (Integration team)
  • SME-009 Does anything downstream use the balance array file, or is it a demo/test file that can be dropped or replaced with real data? (Downstream data owner)
  • DEF-031 Is this intended? Every write failure, including those on the array and variable-record files, is reported with the same text 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:', so the message does not say which file failed; status '10' (end of file) is also accepted on a write, where it has no meaning. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-070 Is this intended? At the end of the run only the account master file is closed; the three output files are never explicitly closed and rely on the runtime closing them at GOBACK. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-108 Is this intended? The current cycle debit is only set (to the fixed 2525.00) when the account's value is zero; a non-zero cycle debit is never copied, so the output carries whatever was left in the record area. COBDATFT's 'INVALID INPUT' error result is also never checked. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Map each account straight onto the flat account extract record: ID, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiration date, current cycle credit and group ID, with no changes to the values. Define the extract layout as a versioned contract that its downstream consumers agree to. Build account output record with reformatted reissue date
  • Parse the reissue date once from its stored YYYY-MM-DD form. Use it both for the YYYYMMDD output date and for the four-digit reissue year in the financial record, so the two can never disagree. Stage account reissue date
  • Use a standard date library to reformat the reissue date from YYYY-MM-DD to YYYYMMDD instead of a separate shared date-conversion routine. Decide and test how an invalid or blank reissue date is handled. Build account output record with reformatted reissue date
  • Produce a fixed 12-character status record per account: the account ID zero-padded to 11 digits, then the one-character active status. Downstream readers depend on the exact width. Populate account status and financial records
  • After each account's status record, produce a 39-byte financial record (account ID, current balance, credit limit, reissue year) in the same output stream. Keep the order status-then-financial for each account, and give the numeric fields an agreed fixed encoding. Populate account status and financial records
  • Process accounts as a sequential stream over the whole account master. Each account produces exactly one account record, one balance array record and two variable-length records, so the record counts can be reconciled (N, N, 2N) at the end of the run. Process successfully read account
  • Treat running out of accounts as normal completion: close the source and log the completion message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT01C' (or an agreed equivalent) with a success exit status for the scheduler. Sequential extract run lifecycle and end-of-file handling
2. Validate daily transactionsfinal · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 11 rules · 20 criteria

Checks each daily card transaction before it is posted. The card must be on the card cross-reference, its account must exist, the account must not go over its credit limit, and the transaction must not be dated after the account expires. It serves the card issuer and decides which transactions are posted and which are rejected. It must never post a transaction for an unknown card, a missing account, an over-limit cycle or an expired account, and it must assign the correct reason code (100, 101, 102 or 103), with expiry (103) taking precedence over over-limit (102).

As a card issuer, I want each daily transaction checked against the card cross-reference and the linked account, so that only transactions for known cards on valid, in-limit, unexpired accounts are posted.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#2

Open questions

  • SME-039 How should the over-credit-limit check measure exposure? Today it uses cycle credits minus cycle debits plus the transaction amount, and because debits are stored as negative amounts this effectively adds payments. Is that intended, or should the check use the current balance plus the transaction amount? Should cash transactions also be checked against the cash credit limit? (Credit risk / card product owner)
  • DEF-018 Is this intended? Negative amounts are stored in the cycle debit total as negative values (2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC), so 'credit minus debit' adds their magnitude back and raises the projection instead of lowering it. The check also ignores the current balance and any earlier cycles, and reason 103 silently overwrites reason 102. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

3. Post validated transactionsfinal · scheduled job · 13 requirements · 14 rules · 17 criteria

Posts each validated daily transaction: it adds the amount to the matching category balance, updates the account's current balance and cycle credit or debit totals, and writes the posted transaction, stamped with the run time, to the transaction master. It serves the card issuer and keeps balances in line with the day's activity. It must never post in the wrong order (category balance, then account, then transaction), lose an amount, or let a storage failure pass unnoticed; any read or write error on these files stops the run.

As a card issuer, I want each validated daily transaction posted to its category balance, its account and the transaction master file, so that balances and cycle totals reflect the day's activity.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#3

Open questions

  • SME-040 When posting a transaction and the account record cannot be saved (failure reason 109), should the run stop, should the transaction go to the daily rejects file, or should the posted transaction still be written? (Card business rules team)
  • SME-041 Posting one transaction updates the category balance, then the account, then writes the posted transaction. If a later step fails, must the earlier updates be reversed, so that all three succeed or fail together? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-042 Each posting run replaces the contents of the posted-transaction master. Is that intended, or should posted transactions accumulate across days? (Card operations / batch operations owner)
  • DEF-003 Is this intended? When the account rewrite fails, reason 109 is set after the posting decision has been made. The transaction is still written, nothing goes to the rejects file, the reject count is unchanged, and the run does not abend. Rewrite failures other than INVALID KEY are not checked at all, so the account and transaction files can disagree. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-009 Is this intended? Posting is not all-or-nothing: the category balance is saved before the account update, and if the account rewrite fails (reason 109 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND') the batch neither abends nor rejects; it still writes the transaction, leaving the category balance and transaction file out of step with the account. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-073 Is this intended? The category balance and the account are updated before the transaction is written. If the write then fails (for example a duplicate transaction ID), the run abends after those updates were already made. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Look up the category balance by a composite key of account ID, transaction type and transaction category; a unique key or index on these three columns. 'Not found' must be told apart from other errors, because 'not found' leads to creating the record. Locate category balance for transaction
  • Save the account's new balance and cycle totals before writing the posted transaction. Ideally both happen in one database transaction, so an account is never updated without its transaction record, or the reverse. Post transaction to account balances
  • Map the posted transaction field for field from the daily transaction: ID, type, category, source, description, amount, merchant ID, name, city, ZIP, card number and original timestamp. Only the processed timestamp is added by posting. Assemble posted transaction record
  • Take the processed timestamp from the run's clock and store it as a proper timestamp. Where it is exported or compared with legacy data, render it as YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000 (hundredths of a second followed by '0000'). Assemble posted transaction record
4. Run daily posting and handle rejectsfinal · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 7 criteria

Runs the daily posting over the whole daily transaction file: it validates and posts each transaction, writes each rejected one with its 4-digit reason code and description, and reports how many were processed and rejected. It serves operations analysts, who follow up on rejects. It must never lose a rejected transaction or miscount, and it must end with return code 4 whenever anything was rejected so the schedule can react.

As an operations analyst, I want every daily transaction read, rejected ones written with their reason, and run counts reported, so that I can see what was posted and follow up on rejected transactions.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches audit, card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-033business ruleWhile daily transactions remain in the daily transaction file, the system shall read the next one, add it to the processed count, clear its failure reason to 0, validate it and, when the failure reason stays 0, post it.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-034side effectWhen a daily transaction fails validation, the system shall add one to the reject count and write a reject record holding the original 350-byte transaction followed by an 80-byte trailer of the 4-digit reason code and 76-character reason description.AC-03
REQ-F-035error handlingIf writing a reject record to the daily rejects file returns a file status other than '00', then the system shall display 'ERROR WRITING TO REJECTS FILE' with the file status and abend the job with code 999.AC-04
REQ-F-036formattingWhen all daily transactions have been read, the system shall display 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' with the count of all transactions read and 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED :' with the reject count.AC-07
REQ-F-037error handlingWhen the run finishes with a reject count greater than 0, the system shall end with job return code 4, otherwise leaving the return code unchanged.AC-05, AC-06

None.

5. Calculate and post monthly interestfinal · scheduled job · 14 requirements · 13 rules · 17 criteria · 1 gap

Calculates monthly interest on each category balance (balance × rate ÷ 1200) at the rate for the account's disclosure group, falling back to the 'DEFAULT' group's rate when the group has none. It writes each interest charge as a system transaction, then adds the account's total interest to its balance and resets its cycle totals to zero. It serves the card issuer, who must charge customers the right interest. It must never use the wrong rate, charge interest at a rate of 0, or carry on when an account or card cross-reference is missing.

As a card issuer, I want monthly interest calculated on each category balance at the account group's rate and posted to the account, so that customers are charged the correct interest.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#5

Open questions

  • SME-012 Interest transaction IDs are made from the run date plus a sequence number. What type and length must the ID and the sequence part have, and what should happen if the sequence runs out of digits? (Data architecture team)
  • SME-013 If the interest run fails, the interest transactions are discarded but accounts already updated with interest are not rolled back. Should account updates and interest transactions be saved together as one unit, and how should a restart avoid charging interest twice? (Batch operations)
  • SME-015 Is the interest run the official cycle-close event that resets each account's cycle credit and debit totals, and should accounts with no category balances also have their cycle totals reset? (Card product / finance owner)
  • DEF-032 Is this intended? An abend part-way through leaves earlier accounts' balances already rewritten with interest, but the job's TRANSACT output is catalogued with abnormal disposition DELETE, so the interest transactions for those accounts are discarded; a rerun would post interest to them again. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-103 Is this intended? The final posting at end of file runs even when the category balance file is empty, so no account has been read and the program tries to rewrite an empty account record, which fails and abends the run with 'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-180 Confirm this is deliberate: Fees are never assessed although the job describes itself as computing interest and fees; the fee step is an empty stub. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Read all category balances in key order (account ID, then type, then category) as one sorted stream, so each account's balances come together. The per-account interest total and the account rewrite depend on that grouping. Iterate category balances and post final account
6. Produce daily transaction reportfinal · online and scheduled job · 5 requirements · 4 rules · 8 criteria

Produces the Daily Transaction Report for a date range. It lists the transactions in range by card, with the transaction type and category descriptions, totals per account, and page totals every 20 lines. It serves operations analysts reviewing the day's activity. It must never print a transaction without its reference data (it stops instead), and it must put the right date range in the heading.

As an operations analyst, I want a paginated daily transaction report with reference descriptions and account totals, so that I can review the day's transactions by card and account.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#6

Open questions

  • SME-043 The transaction report extract selects transactions using fixed dates (2022-01-01 to 2022-07-06), but the report itself takes its start and end dates from the run's date parameter. Should the extract period come from the same run parameter, and what should happen if the two periods differ? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-044 When the transaction report meets a transaction outside the reporting period, the program stops reading entirely, so later in-range transactions and the grand total are lost (the input is sorted by card, not date). Should out-of-range transactions just be skipped instead? Is it acceptable to rely only on the earlier sort step's date filter? (Reporting owner / batch operations lead)
  • SME-045 At the end of the transaction report, the last transaction's amount is added to the page, account and grand totals a second time, which overstates them. Is this double-counting intended, or should it be corrected? How critical are these totals? (Finance reporting owner)
  • SME-046 Should the transaction report print an 'Account Total' line for the last card at the end of the report? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-047 What page size does the transaction report need? Is 20 lines per page a business requirement, and should a page break happen whenever that size is reached, rather than only on exact multiples? (Reporting owner)
  • DEF-182 Is this intended? Account-total and page-total blocks add 2 lines at once, so the counter can skip over a multiple of 20 and a page runs on to the next multiple. Page length is therefore irregular, at up to about 40 lines. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • For each in-range transaction, look up the card's cross-reference (giving the account) by card number, the type description by type code, and the category description by type and category code. A missing reference record must fail the report run rather than print a blank. The type and category tables are small and can be cached for the run. Enrich transaction with reference data
7. Post daily transactions and record rejectsfinal · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria

The scheduled daily posting job. It takes the day's card transactions, posts accepted ones to the transaction master, the account records and the category balances, and keeps rejected ones in a new daily rejects file of 430-byte records (the 350-byte transaction plus an 80-byte reason trailer). It serves the card operations team. It must never leave a partial rejects file behind when the job fails; the rejects file is kept only when the job ends normally.

As a card operations team, I want each day's card transactions posted to the transaction master and account records, with rejected transactions kept separately, so that balances reflect the day's activity and rejects can be investigated.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#7

8. Calculate monthly interest as system transactionsfinal · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 3 rules · 4 criteria

The scheduled monthly interest job, run at billing-cycle close for a supplied processing date. It turns interest on category balances into system transactions and writes them to a new system transaction file of 350-byte records. It serves the card operations team. It must run before transactions are combined, and it must never leave a partial system transaction file when it fails.

As a card operations team, I want monthly interest calculated at billing-cycle close and produced as system transactions, so that interest charges are added to the transaction history before transactions are combined.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#8

  • Run a scheduled monthly job that takes the processing date as a run parameter (the delivered job used '2022071800') rather than the system clock, so a run can be repeated or backdated. It reads category balances, the card cross-reference by card and by account, accounts and disclosure groups without locking out other readers. Run interest step producing system transactions
  • Write the generated interest transactions as one new, versioned batch output (a new file version or a batch-tagged table load) in the 350-byte transaction layout. Publish it only if the job succeeds and discard it on failure, so the combine step never picks up a partial batch. Run interest step producing system transactions
9. Consolidate transactions into the transaction masterfinal · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Combines the latest transaction backup with the latest system-generated (interest) transactions into one set sorted by transaction ID, then loads that set into the transaction master. It serves the card operations team, so the master holds all activity including interest. It must never publish a combined set from a failed sort, and it must keep the transaction ID order.

As a card operations team, I want backed-up and system-generated transactions combined in transaction ID order and loaded into the transaction master, so that the master holds all activity including interest.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#9

10. Back up the transaction masterfinal · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 5 criteria

Copies the whole transaction master into a new backup version of 350-byte records, giving a point-in-time copy for consolidation, extracts and recovery. It serves the card operations team. It must copy every record, must not block other jobs reading the master, and must keep the new backup only when the copy succeeds.

As a card operations team, I want the transaction master copied into a new backup generation, so that a point-in-time copy of transaction history is available for consolidation, extracts and recovery.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#10

11. Set up the transaction master and its timestamp indexfinal · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

A setup job that recreates the transaction master empty, loads it from the initial daily transaction file, and builds an index on the processed timestamp, so transactions can be found by ID or by when they were processed. It serves the card operations team. It must load every record, and the timestamp index must allow many transactions with the same timestamp.

As a card operations team, I want the transaction master loaded from the initial daily transaction file and indexed by processed timestamp, so that transactions can be accessed both by ID and by when they were processed.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#11

  • DEF-105 Is this intended? No step has a condition code check, so the load and index build still run after a failed definition in STEP10. STEP05 also resets delete errors up to 8 to 0. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Provide a setup or seeding job that empties the transaction store (drop and recreate, or truncate) and bulk-loads every record from the initial daily transaction file. It is for environment setup only and must never be part of the regular daily schedule. Load transaction master from daily file
  • Add a secondary, non-unique index on the transaction's processed timestamp, the 26-character value at offset 304 in the legacy record, alongside the primary key on transaction ID. In a relational store this is an ordinary database index kept up to date automatically rather than rebuilt after loading. Build alternate index over transactions
12. Load disclosure group and category balance mastersfinal · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 3 rules · 5 criteria

Loads the disclosure group master (interest rates by group, type and category) and the transaction category balance file from their flat files. The disclosure master is fully replaced on each load. It serves the card operations team, so interest and posting work from current data. It must replace the disclosure groups completely rather than merge them, it must not fail when there is no previous master, and nothing else may write to these files during the load.

As a card operations team, I want the disclosure group master and the transaction category balance file loaded from their flat files, so that interest calculation and posting work from current reference and balance data.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#12

Design notes

  • Make the disclosure group load a full replace: clear or recreate the store, keyed on the 16-character key of group ID, type and category over 50-byte records, before loading. Treat an absent previous store as normal, not an error. Load disclosure group master from flat file
  • Bulk-load every record of the disclosure group feed into the keyed disclosure group store. Load it as one unit (in a single transaction, or by swapping in a staging table) so the interest job never sees a partly loaded rate table. Load disclosure group master from flat file
  • Bulk-load every category balance record from the flat feed into the category balance store, keyed on account ID, type and category. Hold exclusive write access during the load, and schedule it so it never overlaps the posting or interest jobs. Load category balances into keyed file
13. Print the transaction category balance reportfinal · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Produces a printed report of every transaction category balance so card operations analysts can review balances by account, transaction type and category. Each run takes a fresh snapshot of the category balances and lists them in ascending order of account id, then transaction type, then category code. It must never mix in a stale earlier report or keep a partial report when the run fails.

As a card operations analyst, I want a sorted report of transaction category balances, so that I can review balances by account, transaction type and category.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#13

14. Produce account extracts from the account masterfinal · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Produces fresh extracts of the account master in three layouts (fixed account records, account array records and variable-length records) so downstream processes can use account data without reading the master directly. The account master is only read, never changed. Every run must replace the extracts completely, and the run must never leave behind extracts from a failed run.

As a card operations team, I want fresh extracts of the account master in fixed, array and variable-record formats, so that downstream processes can use account data without accessing the master directly.

15. Extract transactions for a reporting periodfinal · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 11 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Takes a fresh backup of all transactions and extracts those whose processing date falls in the reporting period, sorted by card number, as input to the transaction report. The period is the fixed range 2022-01-01 to 2022-07-06 when the standalone job is run, or the start and end dates the analyst entered when it is requested online. It must never include a transaction outside the inclusive date range, and it must never keep an extract or backup from a failed step.

As a card operations analyst, I want transactions for a chosen date range extracted from a fresh backup and sorted by card number, so that the transaction report covers exactly the period I need.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#15

Open questions

  • SME-043 The transaction report extract selects transactions using fixed dates (2022-01-01 to 2022-07-06), but the report itself takes its start and end dates from the run's date parameter. Should the extract period come from the same run parameter, and what should happen if the two periods differ? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-044 When the transaction report meets a transaction outside the reporting period, the program stops reading entirely, so later in-range transactions and the grand total are lost (the input is sorted by card, not date). Should out-of-range transactions just be skipped instead? Is it acceptable to rely only on the earlier sort step's date filter? (Reporting owner / batch operations lead)
  • SME-045 At the end of the transaction report, the last transaction's amount is added to the page, account and grand totals a second time, which overstates them. Is this double-counting intended, or should it be corrected? How critical are these totals? (Finance reporting owner)
  • SME-046 Should the transaction report print an 'Account Total' line for the last card at the end of the report? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-047 What page size does the transaction report need? Is 20 lines per page a business requirement, and should a page break happen whenever that size is reached, rather than only on exact multiples? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-280 The one-day transaction extract uses a fixed run date of 2022-06-02. Should the run date come from a run parameter or from the business date? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-281 What should the one-day transaction extract do when no current version of the transaction backup file exists? (Batch operations team)
  • DEF-104 Confirm this is deliberate: The selection date is hard-coded as '2022-06-02' rather than taken from the run date, so every run extracts the same day's transactions. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-107 Confirm this is deliberate: The standalone job and the cataloged procedure have the date range hard-coded to 2022-01-01 through 2022-07-06, so a scheduled run never reports current transactions unless someone edits the JCL. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Start each reporting run by copying every transaction record into a new numbered backup version, a point-in-time snapshot. Keep the version only if the copy completes, and discard it on failure so later steps never read a partial backup. Back up the transaction master
  • The sort test job needs a sorted extract: the selected transactions, in ascending card number order and with the same record layout as the backup, written as a new numbered version of the daily transaction file. Keep the version when the step succeeds and delete it when the step fails. Extract one day's transactions by card
16. Run the transaction report jobfinal · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria · 1 screen

Runs the transaction report over the period extract, looking up each card's account and the transaction type and category descriptions, and produces a new version of the formatted transaction report. When the analyst requests the report online, the dates they entered must be used instead of the stored date parameters. A failed run must never leave a partial report in place.

As a card operations analyst, I want the transaction report produced from the period extract, using the dates I entered when I request it online, so that I receive a formatted report for the period I asked for.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#16

Design notes

  • Run the report as a job step that starts only after the period extract exists. It reads the extract and does keyed lookups on the card cross-reference (card to account), transaction types and transaction categories, plus the report date parameters. It writes a new numbered version of the transaction report as 133-character print lines. Produce the formatted transaction report
17. Print the daily transaction report with totalsfinal · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 7 criteria · 1 gap

Prints the daily transaction report for card operations analysts. Each in-period transaction gets a line with its ID, account, type, category, source and signed amount, followed by page totals, account totals and a grand total for reconciliation. The totals must add up exactly as the rules state, including the last transaction being counted a second time at end of file. Reporting must stop without any final totals as soon as a transaction outside the period is read.

As a card operations analyst, I want each in-period transaction listed with its account, type, category, source and amount, with page, account and grand totals, so that I can review and reconcile the period's activity.

Final: signed off by Pat (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/DailyTransactionProcessingandReporting#17

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-082business ruleThe system shall take the reporting period from the date parameter record, with the start date in positions 1-10 and the end date in positions 12-21 (YYYY-MM-DD), and treat a transaction as in range when the date part of its processing timestamp is between them inclusive, compared as text.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-083business ruleWhen an in-range transaction is reported, the system shall add its amount to the current page total and the current card's account total before printing its detail line.AC-03
REQ-F-084formattingThe system shall print each detail line with the transaction ID, the account ID from the card cross-reference, the type code and description joined by '-', the category code and description joined by '-', the source, and the amount, with a minus sign shown only for negatives.AC-04
REQ-F-085business ruleWhen a page is closed, either at a page break or at the end of the transaction file, the system shall print a 'Page Total' line with the page's signed amount (e.g. +1,000.00), add that amount to the grand total, reset the page total to zero and print a dashed separator line.AC-05
REQ-F-086business ruleWhen the end of the transaction file is reached, the system shall add the amount of the last transaction read to the page and account totals a second time, print the final 'Page Total' line, then print a 'Grand Total' line showing the sum of all page totals.AC-06
REQ-F-087business ruleIf a transaction read has a processing date outside the reporting period, then the system shall stop processing at once, skipping that and all later transactions, and close its files without printing the final page total, account total or grand total.AC-07

Open questions

  • SME-043 The transaction report extract selects transactions using fixed dates (2022-01-01 to 2022-07-06), but the report itself takes its start and end dates from the run's date parameter. Should the extract period come from the same run parameter, and what should happen if the two periods differ? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-044 When the transaction report meets a transaction outside the reporting period, the program stops reading entirely, so later in-range transactions and the grand total are lost (the input is sorted by card, not date). Should out-of-range transactions just be skipped instead? Is it acceptable to rely only on the earlier sort step's date filter? (Reporting owner / batch operations lead)
  • SME-045 At the end of the transaction report, the last transaction's amount is added to the page, account and grand totals a second time, which overstates them. Is this double-counting intended, or should it be corrected? How critical are these totals? (Finance reporting owner)
  • SME-046 Should the transaction report print an 'Account Total' line for the last card at the end of the report? (Reporting owner)
  • SME-047 What page size does the transaction report need? Is 20 lines per page a business requirement, and should a page break happen whenever that size is reached, rather than only on exact multiples? (Reporting owner)
  • DEF-010 Is this intended? At end of file the last transaction's amount is added to the page and account totals a second time. The end-of-file read leaves the previous record in place, so the final page total and the grand total are overstated by that amount. The last card's account total is never printed at end of file. If the file is empty, the totals are printed without any heading. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-035 Is this intended? An out-of-range transaction ends the whole report run without totals, when the IF/CONTINUE structure shows the intent was only to skip it. In practice the preceding SORT step filters by the same dates, so this only happens when the DATEPARM record and the SORT dates differ. That can happen in the standalone TRANREPT job, which hard-codes the SORT dates. (Subject-matter expert)

Online Account and Transaction Management

1. Find the account to updatefinal · online · 14 requirements · 14 rules · 15 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Lets an operator enter an account id and fetches the linked card cross-reference, account and customer records so the details can be reviewed and updated. It records what was fetched as the original snapshot that later change detection and the concurrency check compare against. It must never present or update details for an account or customer that was not actually found, and must stop at the first missing record with the right message.

As an operator, I want to enter an account id and have the system fetch the linked card, account and customer records, so that I can review and update the right account and customer details.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#1

Open questions

  • SME-055 When the customer for an account cannot be found during account update, a 'not found' message is shown but the customer is not marked as not found. Should the new system explicitly mark the customer as not found? (Account servicing business owner)
  • DEF-116 Is this intended? When the account is not on the account master, the 'not found' state is never set (that line is commented out), so the check at 3627 never stops processing. The program goes on to read the customer, stores account data it never read, and can show the screen as if details were found. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-117 Is this intended? The 'customer not found' state is never set (that line is commented out), so the program still stores the unread customer record as the original snapshot and in the shared context. The screen stays in 'not fetched' because the customer was not found. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Needs a keyed lookup from account id to its card link (customer id and card number), via an index on account id over the card-account-customer cross-reference; the customer id it returns drives the customer read, and the card number is kept in the session. Resolve customer from card cross-reference
  • Needs a read of the account record by its account id primary key; a successful read sets an 'account found' state that the screen uses to decide whether account fields can be shown. Read account master record
  • Needs a read of the customer record by the customer id taken from the cross-reference; a successful read sets a 'customer found' state used for showing customer fields. Read customer master record
  • Keep account id, customer id, customer names, account status and card number in the operator's server-side session (or a signed request token) so they carry over between screen submissions and to the next screen. Store fetched details as original snapshot
  • Store an immutable snapshot of the fetched account and customer values for the session, with open, expiry, reissue and birth dates held as year, month and day parts; it is the baseline for change detection and for the optimistic check that nobody else changed the record before save (a version or timestamp column can serve the same purpose). Store fetched details as original snapshot
2. View account and customer details for updatefinal · online · 12 requirements · 11 rules · 15 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Shows the operator the fetched or entered account and customer values on the Update account screen, with the right message and only the permitted fields open for editing at each stage of the update. Account number, customer number and country must never be editable, and every field must be locked once changes await confirmation or have been saved.

As an operator, I want the fetched or entered account and customer values shown with the right fields open for editing, so that I can see what is stored and change only what may be changed.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-015formattingThe system shall always show the current information message and the current error or return message in their message lines.AC-01
REQ-F-016formattingWhen the account update screen shows the original values, the system shall clear all field-error flags and set the information message to 'Update account details presented above.'AC-02
REQ-F-017formattingWhen the account update screen is shown after details were fetched and the stage is details shown ('S') or changes not OK ('E'), the system shall set the information message to 'Update account details presented above.'AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-018formattingWhen the original values are shown and either the account or the customer was found, the system shall show the stored account status, the current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit and cycle credit and debit as formatted amounts, the open, expiry and reissue dates as year, month and day, and the account group.AC-05
REQ-F-019formattingWhen the original values are shown and the customer was found, the system shall show the stored customer details, with the SSN split into 3-2-4 digits, both phone numbers split into area code, prefix and line number, and the date of birth split into year, month and day.AC-06
REQ-F-020formattingWhen the account update screen is shown on re-entry, the system shall show the entered account id, but leave it blank when the id is zero and the account search is valid.AC-07
REQ-F-021formattingWhen the screen is shown on re-entry and either no details have been fetched or the account id is zero, the system shall show all account and customer fields blank.AC-08
REQ-F-022formattingWhen the screen is shown on re-entry with details shown ('S'), the system shall show the original fetched values, and when changes have been made ('E', 'N', 'C', 'L', 'F'), the system shall show the values the operator entered.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-023formattingWhile account details are shown for editing (state 'S') or shown again with input errors (state 'E'), the system shall let the operator change status, credit and cash limits, balance, cycle credit and debit, open, expiry and reissue dates, group, SSN, FICO score, date of birth, names, address lines, city, state, ZIP, both phones, government ID, EFT account and primary-holder flag.AC-11
REQ-N-001formattingWhile account details are shown for editing (state 'S' or 'E'), the system shall keep the account number, customer number and country protected so they cannot be changed.AC-12, AC-13
REQ-N-002formattingWhile changes are waiting for confirmation (state 'N') or have been saved (state 'C'), the system shall protect every field.AC-14, AC-15
REQ-F-024formattingWhile no account is fetched yet or the save failed, the system shall leave only the account number open for entry.AC-14, AC-15

3. Capture entered changesfinal · online · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 15 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Captures what the operator typed on the Update account screen as proposed new values, treating any field left blank or entered as '*' as not supplied. Amounts entered in currency form are converted to numbers with two decimals. It must never mistake a blank or '*' for a real value to compare or save.

As an operator, I want the values I type to be captured as proposed changes, with blank or '*' entries treated as not supplied, so that the system knows exactly what I intend to change.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#3

Open questions

  • SME-056 Can the customer identifier be changed on the account update screen, or should it be shown read-only? (Account servicing business owner)
  • DEF-011 Confirm this is deliberate: The amount check accepts any signed currency number, so a negative or zero credit limit, cash credit limit or cycle amount passes validation and can be saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-036 Is this intended? When the date service returns a non-zero severity, the check jumps to the end of the final-check paragraph (EDIT-DATE-LE-EXIT). It then runs on into the statement that marks the whole date valid (WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID). The rejected date's year, month and day flags are therefore reset to valid, the field is not marked as in error, and for Date of Birth the future-date check still runs. The input-error state and the message do stay set. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-037 Is this intended? A date of birth equal to today is rejected with a message saying it is in the future, which it is not. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Input binding for account group: map blank or '*' to an explicit 'not supplied' value (null), otherwise keep the entered text as the proposed group. Stage entered account group
  • Input binding for country code: map blank or '*' to null (not supplied), otherwise keep the entered value as the proposed country code. Stage country code entry
  • Input binding for customer number once details are shown: blank or '*' becomes null; any other value is carried as the proposed value, compared with the snapshot and written to the customer record on save. Stage customer identifier entry
  • Input binding for government-issued ID once details are shown: blank or '*' becomes null; otherwise the entered value is the proposed ID, compared with the snapshot and written to the customer record on save. Stage government identifier entry
  • Input binding for the five amounts (credit limit, cash credit limit, current balance, current cycle credit, current cycle debit): blank or '*' becomes null (not supplied) so validation can report it as missing. Stage entered credit limit amount
  • A currency parser that accepts an optional '$', thousands commas, a sign and decimals, and yields a decimal amount at scale 2 (use a decimal type, not floating point); unparseable text stays as entered for validation to reject. Convert entered credit limit
  • Input binding for open, expiry and reissue dates as separate year, month and day parts: each part that is blank or '*' becomes null, any other entry is kept exactly as typed for the date checks. Stage entered account open date
  • Input binding for date of birth parts (year, month, day): blank or '*' becomes null, otherwise the part is kept as the proposed value. Stage date of birth parts
4. Validate changed account and customer fieldsfinal · online · 13 requirements · 10 rules · 18 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Checks every account and customer field once the operator has changed a fetched account, and only moves the update to awaiting confirmation when all checks pass. Amounts must be present and valid currency numbers but may be negative or zero. It must never let an invalid field through to confirmation, and shows only the first error found.

As an operator, I want every changed account and customer field checked before I can confirm, so that only valid details are saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#4

Open questions

  • SME-057 Please supply the complete, authoritative list of valid general-purpose phone area codes. Today it is described only as running from '201' to '989'. (Data governance team)
  • SME-063 At present, a phone number counts as 'not supplied' when the area code and exchange are blank, even if a line number was entered. Is that intended, or should a phone count as not supplied only when all three parts are blank? (Business analyst)
  • SME-064 Should the second and third parts of a social security number be validated only when the first part is valid, or always? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-011 Confirm this is deliberate: The amount check accepts any signed currency number, so a negative or zero credit limit, cash credit limit or cycle amount passes validation and can be saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-113 Confirm this is deliberate: The SSN middle and last parts, the government id and address line 2 get no content check beyond the SSN edit, and address line 2 is deliberately left optional. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

5. Validate account and customer datesfinal · online · 14 requirements · 14 rules · 18 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Checks the open, expiry, reissue and birth dates part by part and then as real calendar dates whenever the operator changes account details. Each message names the date it concerns and only the first error is shown. Impossible dates such as 31 April, 30 February or 29 February in a non-leap year must never be saved.

As an operator, I want the open, expiry, reissue and birth dates checked part by part and as real calendar dates, so that impossible dates are never saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-045business ruleWhen the entered values differ from the stored account and are not awaiting or past confirmation, the system shall check the 'Open Date', 'Expiry Date', 'Reissue Date' and 'Date of Birth' in that order with the same date check, prefix each message with the date's name, and show only the first error message found.AC-01
REQ-F-046business ruleIf the year of a date is blank, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name> : Year must be supplied.' and still go on to check the month and day.AC-08
REQ-F-047business ruleIf the year of a date is not a four-digit number, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name> must be 4 digit number.'AC-09
REQ-F-048business ruleIf a numeric year does not start with 19 or 20, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name> : Century is not valid.'AC-02
REQ-F-049business ruleIf the month of a date is blank, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name> : Month must be supplied.'AC-10
REQ-F-050business ruleIf the month of a date is not a number from 1 to 12, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name>: Month must be a number between 1 and 12.'AC-11, AC-12
REQ-F-051business ruleIf the day of a date is blank, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name> : Day must be supplied.'AC-13
REQ-F-052business ruleIf the day of a date is not a number or is outside 1 to 31, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name>:day must be a number between 1 and 31.'AC-14, AC-15
REQ-F-053business ruleIf the day is 31 and the month is not 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 or 12, then the system shall reject the date with '<date name>:Cannot have 31 days in this month.' and stop checking that date.AC-16, AC-17
REQ-F-054business ruleIf the date is 30 February, then the system shall reject it with '<date name>:Cannot have 30 days in this month.' and stop checking that date.AC-18
REQ-F-055business ruleIf the date is 29 February and the year is not a leap year (a year ending in 00 must divide by 400, any other year by 4), then the system shall reject it with '<date name>:Not a leap year.Cannot have 29 days in this month.'AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-056business ruleIf any of the year, month or day of a date has failed its check, then the system shall stop checking that date without the final date-service check.AC-05
REQ-F-057business ruleWhen a date passes all the earlier checks, the system shall confirm it with the date service (CSUTLDTC) in format 'YYYYMMDD' and reject it with '<date name> validation error Sev code: <severity> Message code: <message number>' if the service returns a non-zero severity.AC-06
REQ-F-058error handlingWhen the date service rejects a date, the system shall still mark the date's year, month and day as valid, so that only the error message and the screen's input-error state record the failure.AC-07

Open questions

  • SME-059 When the date-checking utility rejects a date, the date is still marked valid even though an input error is raised. Should a rejected date stay invalid, including for later checks such as 'date of birth cannot be in the future'? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-060 Should date validation check that the month is numeric before checking that it is between 1 and 12? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-061 Only years in the 1900s and 2000s are accepted for all four account and customer dates. Should this restriction still apply to card expiry and reissue dates? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-065 When a date's year fails validation, should the whole date check stop, or should the month and day still be checked? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-036 Is this intended? When the date service returns a non-zero severity, the check jumps to the end of the final-check paragraph (EDIT-DATE-LE-EXIT). It then runs on into the statement that marks the whole date valid (WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID). The rejected date's year, month and day flags are therefore reset to valid, the field is not marked as in error, and for Date of Birth the future-date check still runs. The input-error state and the message do stay set. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

6. Confirm and save the account updatefinal · online · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 7 criteria · 1 screen

Lets the operator confirm validated changes and saves them to the account and customer records, but only if nobody else has changed those records since they were fetched. Only the keys allowed at each stage take effect; anything else is treated as Enter. It must never overwrite another user's update, and the legacy save places the account group into the stored ZIP position, which the new design must deliberately decide whether to keep.

As an operator, I want to confirm validated changes and have them saved only if nobody else has changed the record meanwhile, so that I do not overwrite another user's update.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#6

Requirements

REQ-F-059business ruleWhen the operator presses a key that is not Enter, not PF3, not PF5 while changes are pending confirmation ('N'), and not PF12 after the account details are fetched, the system shall reject the requested key operation and treat the request as Enter, while allowed keys keep their requested operation.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-060error handlingIf any stored account or customer value differs from the value fetched when the details were shown, then the system shall flag 'Record changed by some one else. Please review' and stop the save.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06

Open questions

  • SME-062 What should the account update screen do in each of these cases: exit (PF3), first entry before any details are fetched, arriving from the menu, a completed save, a failed save, cancel (PF12), details shown, and answering 'N' to confirmation (PF5)? (Business analyst)
  • SME-066 When account update saves changes, the account record is written before the customer record. Must both be saved together, so that if the customer save fails the account change is rolled back? How critical is this, given it changes balances, limits and regulated customer data? (Account servicing SME / architecture team)
  • DEF-159 Is this intended? The account update record layout leaves out the account ZIP field, so every save shifts the group ID into the ZIP position and overwrites the real group ID with filler. The next read then shows a wrong group ID, and the account ZIP is lost. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The legacy save writes the account from a layout without a ZIP field, so the entered group lands in the stored ZIP position (offsets 103-112) and the group field gets unset filler. The new account store should have distinct group and ZIP columns; whether to reproduce this shift for data compatibility (e.g. while the legacy file is still read by other jobs) or correct it is a decision to record, and any migration must account for existing records with the group in the ZIP position. Persisted record formatting and account record layout
7. Select an account to updatefinal · online · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 11 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Lets the operator enter an 11-digit account number to start an update; until an account is fetched only that number is checked. A valid number triggers the cross-reference, account and customer lookups, and details are shown only when all three are found. A blank, non-numeric or all-zero number must never lead to a lookup.

As an operator, I want to enter an account number and see the account and customer details, so that I can review and update them.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#7

Requirements

REQ-F-063business ruleWhile no account details have been fetched yet, the system shall check only the account number and ignore every other field on the screen.AC-03
REQ-F-064business ruleIf no account details have been fetched yet and the account number is blank or '*', then the system shall show the error 'No input received', set the current account number to zeros and read no account.AC-04, AC-05
