Open questions

  • SME-054 When saving an account update, a failure to lock the customer record is reported as a successful save. Is that intended, or should it be reported as a lock error? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-055 When the customer for an account cannot be found during account update, a 'not found' message is shown but the customer is not marked as not found. Should the new system explicitly mark the customer as not found? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-056 Can the customer identifier be changed on the account update screen, or should it be shown read-only? (Account servicing business owner)
  • DEF-040 Is this intended? For a blank account number, the 'Account number not provided' message set in 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT is always overwritten by 'No input received' in 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS, so the more specific message is never shown on this path. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-074 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch that turns a committed save ('C') back into 'details shown' and clears the account and card number when there is no calling transaction, but it can never run: the main dispatch catches state 'C' first on the next interaction and resets the screen itself. The field edits also skip the 'C' state check for the same reason. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Input binding for the account number: blank or '*' becomes null (not supplied), otherwise the entered text is kept as the search key for the account-number validation. Capture account id entry
8. Detect changes before validatingfinal · online · 5 requirements · 7 rules · 8 criteria · 1 screen

Compares what the operator entered against the values fetched and runs field checks only when something has actually changed and the update is not already awaiting confirmation or saved. Text is compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces; numbers, dates and codes exactly. It must never re-validate or save unchanged details, and shows 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' instead.

As an operator, I want the system to check my entries only when I have actually changed something, so that unchanged details are not re-validated or saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#8

REQ-F-068business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter on an account already shown, the system shall compare every entered value with the value fetched, ignoring upper/lower case and surrounding spaces for text fields (status, group, names, address, state, country, ZIP, government ID, primary-holder flag) and comparing amounts, dates, phone parts, SSN, EFT account and FICO exactly, counting any difference as a change.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-069business ruleWhen no entered value differs from the fetched values, the system shall show 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.', run no field checks, save nothing and leave the details on screen without asking for confirmation.AC-04
REQ-F-070business ruleWhile the update is neither awaiting confirmation ('N') nor completed ('C'), when a change is detected, the system shall mark the changes as not yet accepted ('E'), run every field check, and move the update to awaiting confirmation ('N') if all checks pass.AC-05, AC-06, AC-07

Open questions

  • SME-057 Please supply the complete, authoritative list of valid general-purpose phone area codes. Today it is described only as running from '201' to '989'. (Data governance team)
  • SME-063 At present, a phone number counts as 'not supplied' when the area code and exchange are blank, even if a line number was entered. Is that intended, or should a phone count as not supplied only when all three parts are blank? (Business analyst)
  • SME-064 Should the second and third parts of a social security number be validated only when the first part is valid, or always? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-038 Confirm this is deliberate: The name, city, state and country fields accept only the letters A-Z and a-z and spaces. Real names and places with apostrophes, hyphens or periods ('O'Brien', 'St. Louis') are rejected. Separately, the blank-phone check tests the area-code part twice where it should test the line-number part. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-039 Confirm this is deliberate: Text fields are compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces, so a correction that only changes capitalisation (for example 'smith' to 'Smith') counts as no change and cannot be saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-041 Is this intended? The 'phone not supplied' test checks the area code twice and never checks that the line number is blank-spaces (third condition tests area code = spaces OR line number = low-values). Because the screen input turns blanks into low-values first, this has no visible effect today, but a number arriving with a spaces area code and prefix would be accepted as omitted even with a line number entered. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Validation is a step gated by update state: when no change is detected or the update is awaiting confirmation or completed, reset all per-field error flags and skip the validators entirely, including date checks. Skip edits when nothing changed
9. Validate customer name and addressfinal · online · 9 requirements · 11 rules · 16 criteria · 1 screen

Checks the customer's names, address line 1, city, state, ZIP and country when the operator changes details, including that the state is a valid US state code and matches the ZIP prefix. Middle name and address line 2 are optional. It must never save a missing required name or address part, non-letter characters in names, or a state and ZIP that do not belong together.

As an operator, I want customer names and address details checked when I change them, so that only well-formed and consistent names and addresses are saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#9

Open questions

  • SME-056 Can the customer identifier be changed on the account update screen, or should it be shown read-only? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-057 Please supply the complete, authoritative list of valid general-purpose phone area codes. Today it is described only as running from '201' to '989'. (Data governance team)
  • SME-058 Please supply the complete, authoritative list of valid state and ZIP-prefix combinations. Is this rough check enough, or is a finer-grained address check required? (Data governance team)
  • SME-063 At present, a phone number counts as 'not supplied' when the area code and exchange are blank, even if a line number was entered. Is that intended, or should a phone count as not supplied only when all three parts are blank? (Business analyst)
  • SME-064 Should the second and third parts of a social security number be validated only when the first part is valid, or always? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-038 Confirm this is deliberate: The name, city, state and country fields accept only the letters A-Z and a-z and spaces. Real names and places with apostrophes, hyphens or periods ('O'Brien', 'St. Louis') are rejected. Separately, the blank-phone check tests the area-code part twice where it should test the line-number part. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-043 Confirm this is deliberate: The ZIP check only compares the first two ZIP digits with the state, so a ZIP in the wrong area of a valid prefix is accepted; the code comment calls it a crude edit, so this looks intended. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Input binding for first, middle and last name, address lines 1 and 2, city and EFT account id: blank or '*' becomes null; otherwise the value is the proposed new value. The city maps to the customer's third address line in the stored record. Stage electronic funds transfer account
  • Input binding for state and ZIP: blank or '*' becomes null (empty); otherwise the entered value goes to the state and ZIP validators. Stage state code entry
10. Validate customer phone numbersfinal · online · 13 requirements · 14 rules · 13 criteria · 1 screen

Checks each customer phone number the operator enters as a North American number: area code from the list of general-purpose codes, then a 3-digit prefix and a 4-digit line number, none of them zero. Phones are optional, so a fully blank number is accepted. Every failing part is flagged, but only the first message is shown.

As an operator, I want any phone number I enter checked as a North American number, so that only valid contact numbers are saved while phones stay optional.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#10

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-082design noteWhen the operator enters '*' or leaves blank any part of phone number 1 or phone number 2 (area code, prefix or line number), the system shall treat that part as not supplied before validating it.AC-01
REQ-F-083business ruleWhen the area code, prefix and line number of a phone number are all not supplied, the system shall accept the phone number as omitted and skip all further checks on it.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-084business ruleIf any part of a phone number is supplied but its area code is not, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Area code must be supplied.' and go on to check the prefix.AC-03
REQ-F-085business ruleIf a supplied area code is not all digits, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Area code must be A 3 digit number.' and go on to check the prefix.AC-07
REQ-F-086business ruleIf a supplied area code is 000, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Area code cannot be zero' and go on to check the prefix.AC-08
REQ-F-087business ruleIf a supplied numeric, non-zero area code is not one of the listed North American general-purpose area codes (410 codes between '201' and '989', not every number in that range), then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Not valid North America general purpose area code'.AC-04
REQ-F-088business ruleIf the prefix of a phone number being checked is not supplied, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Prefix code must be supplied.' and go on to check the line number.AC-09
REQ-F-089business ruleIf a supplied prefix is not all digits, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Prefix code must be A 3 digit number.' and go on to check the line number.AC-10
REQ-F-090business ruleIf a supplied prefix is 000, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Prefix code cannot be zero' and go on to check the line number, accepting any other three-digit prefix (for example 555).AC-05
REQ-F-091business ruleIf the line number of a phone number being checked is not supplied, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Line number code must be supplied.'.AC-11
REQ-F-092business ruleIf a supplied line number is not all digits, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Line number code must be A 4 digit number.'.AC-12
REQ-F-093business ruleIf a supplied line number is 0000, then the system shall flag an input error with '<Phone Number 1 or 2>: Line number code cannot be zero', accepting any other four-digit line number.AC-06
REQ-F-094formattingWhen more than one phone number part fails its checks, the system shall flag every failing part in error but show only the first message raised, with no later message replacing one already set.AC-13

Open questions

  • SME-056 Can the customer identifier be changed on the account update screen, or should it be shown read-only? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-057 Please supply the complete, authoritative list of valid general-purpose phone area codes. Today it is described only as running from '201' to '989'. (Data governance team)
  • SME-063 At present, a phone number counts as 'not supplied' when the area code and exchange are blank, even if a line number was entered. Is that intended, or should a phone count as not supplied only when all three parts are blank? (Business analyst)
  • SME-064 Should the second and third parts of a social security number be validated only when the first part is valid, or always? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-038 Confirm this is deliberate: The name, city, state and country fields accept only the letters A-Z and a-z and spaces. Real names and places with apostrophes, hyphens or periods ('O'Brien', 'St. Louis') are rejected. Separately, the blank-phone check tests the area-code part twice where it should test the line-number part. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-041 Is this intended? The 'phone not supplied' test checks the area code twice and never checks that the line number is blank-spaces (third condition tests area code = spaces OR line number = low-values). Because the screen input turns blanks into low-values first, this has no visible effect today, but a number arriving with a spaces area code and prefix would be accepted as omitted even with a line number entered. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Input binding for the area code, prefix and line number of each phone: blank or '*' becomes null per part before the phone validator runs, so a phone with all three parts null counts as omitted. Stage customer phone number parts
11. Validate identity and credit detailsfinal · online · 8 requirements · 9 rules · 13 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Checks the customer's Social Security Number, date of birth and FICO score when the operator changes details. The SSN must be in three supplied, numeric, non-zero parts with an allowed first group, the birth date must be before today, and the FICO score must be between 300 and 850. Implausible identity or credit data must never be saved.

As an operator, I want the SSN, date of birth and FICO score checked when I change customer details, so that only plausible identity and credit data is saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#11

Requirements

REQ-F-095design noteWhen the operator enters a Social Security Number part as '*' or leaves it blank, the system shall treat that part as not supplied, and otherwise take the entered part as the proposed value.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-096business ruleIf the first three SSN characters are blank, not all numeric or zero, then the system shall reject them with 'SSN: First 3 chars must be supplied.', 'SSN: First 3 chars must be all numeric.' or 'SSN: First 3 chars must not be zero.' respectively, and shall not check the other two SSN parts.AC-01
REQ-F-097business ruleIf the first three SSN characters are numeric and equal 666 or fall between 900 and 999, then the system shall reject them with 'SSN: First 3 chars: should not be 000, 666, or between 900 and 999'.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-098business ruleWhen the first three SSN characters are numeric and non-zero, the system shall require the 4th-5th characters and the last 4 characters each to be supplied, all numeric and non-zero, giving 'SSN 4th & 5th chars …' or 'SSN Last 4 chars …' with 'must be supplied.', 'must be all numeric.' or 'must not be zero.'.AC-08, AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-099business ruleIf a valid calendar date of birth is today or later, then the system shall reject it, flag the day, month and year fields, and show 'Date of Birth:cannot be in the future ' if no earlier error message is already set.AC-01, AC-04
REQ-F-100business ruleIf the FICO score is entered as blank or '*', then the system shall treat it as not supplied and reject it with 'FICO Score must be supplied.'.AC-11
REQ-F-101business ruleIf the FICO score is not all three digits, then the system shall reject it with 'FICO Score must be all numeric.', and if it is zero, the system shall reject it with 'FICO Score must not be zero.'.AC-12, AC-13
REQ-F-102business ruleIf a numeric, non-zero FICO score is below 300 or above 850, then the system shall mark the FICO score in error and reject the input with 'FICO Score: should be between 300 and 850', accepting 300 and 850 themselves.AC-05

  • SME-060 Should date validation check that the month is numeric before checking that it is between 1 and 12? (Account servicing business owner)

  • DEF-037 Is this intended? A date of birth equal to today is rejected with a message saying it is in the future, which it is not. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-042 Is this intended? The IF on part 1 being valid has no END-IF, so the SSN 4th-5th and last-4 checks are skipped whenever part 1 is blank, non-numeric or zero; the 000 branch of the forbidden-value message can never be shown. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Input binding for the three SSN parts (3, 2 and 4 digits): each part that is blank or '*' becomes null; otherwise the entered part is kept as the proposed value for the SSN validator. Stage social security number parts
12. Validate account flags and EFT accountfinal · online · 4 requirements · 6 rules · 5 criteria · 1 screen

Checks the account status and primary card holder flags and the EFT account id when the operator changes account details. Both flags must be supplied as Y or N, and the EFT account id must be ten digits and not zero. A missing or malformed flag or funds-transfer account must never be saved, and the cursor goes to the field in error.

As an operator, I want the account status, primary card holder indicator and EFT account id checked, so that only valid flags and a well-formed funds transfer account are saved.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#12

Design notes

  • Input binding for Account Status and Primary Card Holder: blank or '*' becomes null (not supplied) so the Y/N validator reports it as missing rather than saving it. Stage entered account active status
  • Input binding for the EFT account id (and the name, address and city fields): blank or '*' becomes null; otherwise the value is the proposed new value passed to the 10-digit, non-zero numeric check. Stage electronic funds transfer account
13. Save confirmed account and customer changesfinal · online · 8 requirements · 7 rules · 8 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Saves an operator's confirmed changes to an account and its customer as one unit of work: the account record first, then the customer record. It must never leave the two out of step. If either record cannot be locked, or either save fails, nothing is kept and the operator is told the changes were unsuccessful.

As an operator, I want my confirmed changes saved to both the account and customer records together, so that the two records never end up out of step.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#13

Open questions

  • SME-066 When account update saves changes, the account record is written before the customer record. Must both be saved together, so that if the customer save fails the account change is rolled back? How critical is this, given it changes balances, limits and regulated customer data? (Account servicing SME / architecture team)
  • DEF-057 Is this intended? A customer lock failure is not handled in the outcome EVALUATE, so it falls to WHEN OTHER and the change is marked done ('C') with an update-success prompt although nothing was saved; likewise if a message was already set, the lock-failure flag is never set and the outcome also falls to 'C'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-074 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch that turns a committed save ('C') back into 'details shown' and clears the account and card number when there is no calling transaction, but it can never run: the main dispatch catches state 'C' first on the next interaction and resets the screen itself. The field edits also skip the 'C' state check for the same reason. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

14. Navigate the account update screenfinal · online · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 6 criteria · 1 screen

Controls how the account update screen moves between its steps: a blank search on first arrival, checking entries on each submit, and a fresh start after a save has completed or failed. It is for operators maintaining accounts. It must never act on PF5 unless validated changes are waiting for confirmation, and never on PF12 unless account details have been fetched.

As an operator, I want the account update screen to respond predictably to my keys and to start afresh when appropriate, so that I always know which step of the update I am in.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#14

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-114formattingWhen the operator arrives with no saved context, or comes from the main menu ('COMEN01C') for the first time, the system shall clear any previous update data and show an empty screen asking 'Enter or update id of account to update'.AC-01
REQ-F-115business ruleWhen the operator submits the screen with any key other than PF3 after a committed ('C') or failed ('L', 'F') save, the system shall clear the update data and account number and show an empty screen asking for a new account number.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-116business ruleWhen the operator submits the screen with any key other than PF3, and it is not a first arrival and not the interaction after a committed or failed save, the system shall read and check the entries, decide the next step from the update state, and show the screen again.AC-04
REQ-F-117business ruleThe system shall accept PF5 only while validated changes await confirmation ('N') and PF12 only once account details have been fetched, and shall treat any other key, or PF5/PF12 outside those states, as Enter.AC-05, AC-06

15. Update account details with validation and confirmationfinal · online · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 7 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Lets an operator change the details of a fetched account. Every field is checked, and the changes are saved only when the operator confirms them with PF5. Unchanged or invalid submissions must never be saved, and the operator must always see the outcome: committed, a lock failure, an update failure, or a record that someone else changed meanwhile.

As an operator, I want my changes to account details checked and then saved only when I confirm them with PF5, so that only validated changes reach the account record and I know whether the save succeeded.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#15

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-118business ruleWhile details are shown, when the operator changes one or more values, the system shall check every field and set the state to 'N' with the message 'Changes validated.Press F5 to save' if no check fails, or to 'E' (changes not OK) if any check fails.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-119business ruleWhile details are shown, when the operator submits without changing any value, the system shall keep the details shown (state 'S') and report 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.'.AC-03
REQ-F-120business ruleWhen the state is changes not OK ('E'), or validated changes ('N') are submitted without PF5, the system shall save nothing and show the details again for correction or confirmation.AC-04
REQ-F-121business ruleWhen validated changes ('N') are confirmed with PF5, the system shall save them and set the state to 'L' if the account cannot be locked, 'F' if the locked update fails, 'S' (details shown again) if someone else changed the record since it was read, or 'C' otherwise.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-122formattingWhen a save completes ('C'), the system shall show the message 'Changes committed to database'.AC-07

Open questions

  • SME-054 When saving an account update, a failure to lock the customer record is reported as a successful save. Is that intended, or should it be reported as a lock error? (Account servicing business owner)
  • SME-062 What should the account update screen do in each of these cases: exit (PF3), first entry before any details are fetched, arriving from the menu, a completed save, a failed save, cancel (PF12), details shown, and answering 'N' to confirmation (PF5)? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-074 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch that turns a committed save ('C') back into 'details shown' and clears the account and card number when there is no calling transaction, but it can never run: the main dispatch catches state 'C' first on the next interaction and resets the screen itself. The field edits also skip the 'C' state check for the same reason. (Subject-matter expert)

16. Validate and look up an account for viewingfinal · online · 14 requirements · 14 rules · 16 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Checks the account number a user enters on the Account View screen. A valid number is looked up in the card cross-reference, then the account master, then the customer master, so the right account and cardholder can be shown. Nothing may be read for a blank, non-numeric, short or all-zero number, and every failed lookup must give a clear message naming what was not found.

As a user, I want the account number I enter to be checked and the account and its customer looked up, so that I see the right account or a clear reason why it could not be shown.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#16

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-123business ruleWhen the account number entered on the Account View screen is '*' or blank, the system shall treat the account number as not supplied.AC-01
REQ-F-124business ruleIf no account number is supplied, then the system shall reject the request as an input error without reading any file, set the session account to zero, show 'No input received', and redisplay the account field as '*' in red.AC-02
REQ-F-125business ruleIf the account number supplied is not all digits (including one shorter than 11 digits) or is all zeros, then the system shall reject it as an input error without reading any file, set the session account to zero, show the account field in red and show 'Account Filter must be a non-zero 11 digit number'.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-126business ruleWhen the account number is 11 digits and not all zeros, the system shall accept it as the session account and go on to the account lookup.AC-05
REQ-F-127design noteWhen an account number passes validation, the system shall look the account up in the card cross-reference by account number (CXACAIX) and, when it is found, keep that account's customer number and card number for the rest of the session.AC-06
REQ-F-128business ruleIf the account is not in the card cross-reference, then the system shall stop the lookup, treat it as an input error, show the account number in red and show 'Account:<account number> not found in Cross ref file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>'.AC-12
REQ-F-129error handlingIf reading the card cross-reference fails for any reason other than 'not found', then the system shall stop the lookup, treat it as an input error and show 'File Error: READ on CXACAIX returned RESP <code>,RESP2 <code>'.AC-13
REQ-F-130design noteWhen the account is found in the cross-reference, the system shall read the account master (ACCTDAT) by account number and, on success, mark the account as found so that its details are displayed.AC-07
REQ-F-131error handlingIf the account is not in the account master, then the system shall treat it as an input error, show the account number in red and show 'Account:<account number> not found in Acct Master file.Resp:<code> Reas:<code>', and for any other read failure show 'File Error: READ on ACCTDAT returned RESP <code>,RESP2 <code>'.AC-14
REQ-F-132error handlingIf reading the account master does not succeed, then the system shall still go on to read the customer master, because the stop check after the account read never triggers.AC-08
REQ-F-133design noteThe system shall read the customer master (CUSTDAT) using the customer number taken from the card cross-reference and, on success, mark the customer as found so that the customer details are displayed.AC-09
REQ-F-134error handlingIf the customer is not in the customer master, then the system shall treat it as an input error and show 'CustId:<customer number> not found in customer master.Resp: <code> REAS:<code>', unless an earlier message is already set.AC-15
REQ-F-135error handlingIf reading the customer master fails for any reason other than 'not found', then the system shall treat it as an input error and show 'File Error: READ on CUSTDAT returned RESP <code>,RESP2 <code>', replacing any earlier message.AC-16
REQ-F-136business ruleWhile the program context is re-entry (1), when PF3 was not pressed, the system shall read and validate the entered account number, redisplay the screen with the error on an input error, and otherwise look up the card cross-reference, account master and customer master in turn (stopping at the first not found) and display the screen.AC-10, AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-067 When an account number is entered on the account view screen and the account is not found, or the file cannot be read, should the lookup stop at that point? (Currently it stops only on one exact message, 'Did not find this account in account master file', and the real not-found path produces a different message.) (Business analyst)
  • SME-068 On the account view screen, if the account number is left blank, which message should the operator see: 'Account number not provided' or 'No input received'? (Business analyst)
  • SME-069 On the account view screen, the error message says the account number must be 'a non-zero 11 digit number', but only 'numeric and non-zero' is checked. Should exactly 11 digits be required? Should the message keep its current double space? (Business analyst)
  • SME-070 On the account view screen, if the customer record is found but the account record is not, should the account's financial details still be shown? After a successful lookup, should the screen show a success message ('Displaying details of given Account') instead of the input prompt? (Customer service operations lead)
  • SME-071 Please confirm the priority of the account view lookup chain (card cross-reference, then account master, then customer master). Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that would be costly if it were wrong? (Account servicing subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-044 Is this intended? A blank account number first sets the message 'Account number not provided', which is then replaced at once with 'No input received', so the more specific message can never be shown. The 'only if no message yet' guard in front of it has no effect. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-045 Is this intended? When the account is missing from the account master, or the read fails, the lookup does not stop: the stop check tests a message flag that is never set, so the customer master is still read. If the customer is found, the account fields are filled from an empty account record next to the account 'not found' message. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Needs a keyed lookup from account number to its card cross-reference entry, which gives the customer number and card number (a secondary index or account-keyed query on the card-account link). Both values must be kept in the user's session for the following reads and later screens. Orchestrate account and customer retrieval
  • Needs a keyed read of the account by account number, done only after the cross-reference lookup succeeds. A successful read sets an 'account found' flag that the screen uses to decide whether to show account details. Orchestrate account and customer retrieval
  • Needs a keyed read of the customer by the customer number that came from the cross-reference, not by any value the user typed. A successful read sets a 'customer found' flag that controls display of the customer details. Orchestrate account and customer retrieval
17. Display account and customer detailsfinal · online · 7 requirements · 8 rules · 11 criteria · 1 screen

Shows an account's financial details and its cardholder's profile together on one screen for users reviewing an account. Each part is shown only when its record was actually found. As agreed, the customer's full Social Security number is shown unmasked as NNN-NN-NNNN, so that screen needs proper access control. The cursor always returns to the account number field.

As a user, I want to see an account's financial details and its customer's profile on one screen, so that I can review the account and the cardholder.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, personal_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#17

18. Navigate the account view screenfinal · online · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 8 criteria · 1 screen

Controls how a user enters and leaves the account view screen. It starts fresh on first entry, treats any unsupported key as Enter, and returns to the caller or the main menu on PF3. It must keep track of whether this is a first visit or a return visit and keep the session data between interactions. An unexpected state must end with 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' rather than guessing.

As a user, I want the account view screen to start fresh, accept my input and return me to where I came from with PF3, so that I can move through the application predictably.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#18

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-143business ruleWhen the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 (PF15 counts as PF3), such as PF7, Clear or PA1, the system shall treat it as Enter.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-144business ruleWhen the user presses PF3, the system shall transfer control, with the session data and the program context reset to first entry, to the calling program and transaction, or to the main menu ('COMEN01C', transaction 'CM00') when no caller is recorded.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-145design noteWhen the program starts with no session data, or is entered from the main menu ('COMEN01C') other than as a re-entry, the system shall start a fresh session context, discarding any passed data.AC-05
REQ-F-146business ruleWhile the program context is first entry (0), when PF3 was not pressed, the system shall show the empty account search screen and wait for input.AC-06
REQ-F-147design noteWhen the account view screen is sent, the system shall set the program context to re-entry (1) and end the task, keeping the session data, so that the next input from the user starts transaction 'CAVW'.AC-07
REQ-F-148error handlingIf the program context is neither first entry nor re-entry, then the system shall send the plain text 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' and end.AC-08

Open questions

  • SME-067 When an account number is entered on the account view screen and the account is not found, or the file cannot be read, should the lookup stop at that point? (Currently it stops only on one exact message, 'Did not find this account in account master file', and the real not-found path produces a different message.) (Business analyst)
  • SME-068 On the account view screen, if the account number is left blank, which message should the operator see: 'Account number not provided' or 'No input received'? (Business analyst)
  • SME-069 On the account view screen, the error message says the account number must be 'a non-zero 11 digit number', but only 'numeric and non-zero' is checked. Should exactly 11 digits be required? Should the message keep its current double space? (Business analyst)
  • SME-070 On the account view screen, if the customer record is found but the account record is not, should the account's financial details still be shown? After a successful lookup, should the screen show a success message ('Displaying details of given Account') instead of the input prompt? (Customer service operations lead)

Design notes

  • The screen needs a per-user conversation state with a 'first entry' marker. When there is no session, or the user arrives fresh from the main menu, the server creates new screen state and ignores any data passed in. Only a return visit to the same screen reuses its state. Screen conversation state: first entry vs re-entry
  • Each time the account view is rendered, store its session state server-side (or in a signed client token) marked as 're-entry'. The next request from the user then resumes the same account view conversation. No process stays waiting between requests: the flow is stateless request handling with persisted session state. Screen conversation state: first entry vs re-entry
19. Request a bill paymentfinal · online · 12 requirements · 12 rules · 16 criteria · 3 screens

Lets a signed-on cardholder enter an account, see the balance owed, and then confirm or decline paying it in full. It must never post a payment without an explicit 'Y' or 'y'. It must never accept a payment when the balance is zero or less, and it must never run without a signed-on session.

As a cardholder, I want to enter my account, see the balance owed and confirm or decline paying it, so that I only pay when I mean to and there is something to pay.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches money, security. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#19

Open questions

  • SME-080 What should the bill payment screen do when it is opened without any information from the screen that called it? (Business analyst)
  • SME-081 What format and length must a new bill payment transaction ID have? It is currently the last ID plus 1. (Data architect)
  • SME-082 The bill payment transaction is saved before the account balance is reduced. If the account update then fails, what should happen to the saved transaction? Should the two be one all-or-nothing step? (Business analyst / architecture team)
  • SME-083 How must the system make sure that two bill payments made at the same time never get the same transaction ID? (Architecture team)
  • SME-084 If saving the bill payment transaction fails, what message should the user see and how should the failure be handled? (Business analyst)
  • SME-085 During a bill payment, should a failed card cross-reference lookup or a failed account update stop the remaining payment steps? (Business analyst)
  • SME-086 Please confirm the full rule for checking the account ID on bill payment: it is required, it must exist, and which error message goes with each case. (Legacy application SME)
  • SME-087 If the user enters 'Y' on the first submission, the bill payment is posted straight away without first showing the balance. Should the balance always be shown before a payment can be confirmed? (Payments business owner)
  • DEF-046 Is this intended? A failed card cross-reference lookup sets an error message but does not stop the posting: the transaction is still written (with whatever card number is in the cross-reference record) and the balance is still reduced and saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-112 Is this intended? When a selected account is passed on first entry, the Enter processing already sends the screen and the first-entry logic then sends it again, so the screen is sent twice in one interaction. (Subject-matter expert)

20. Post a full-balance bill paymentfinal · online · 11 requirements · 13 rules · 15 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Posts a confirmed bill payment as a new transaction for the full current balance, clears the account balance to zero, and gives the cardholder the new transaction ID as proof. The payment is numbered one above the highest existing transaction ID. As the legacy system behaves, the balance is still cleared even when the payment transaction could not be written, so the build team must decide explicitly whether to keep that.

As a cardholder, I want my confirmed payment recorded as a transaction for the full balance and my account balance cleared, so that my account is paid off and I get a transaction ID as proof.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money, updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#20

REQ-F-160business ruleWhen the user confirms a bill payment with 'Y' or 'y' and the account has a balance to pay, the system shall look up the card linked to the account and number the new payment transaction as the highest existing transaction ID plus 1.AC-01

Open questions

  • SME-080 What should the bill payment screen do when it is opened without any information from the screen that called it? (Business analyst)
  • SME-081 What format and length must a new bill payment transaction ID have? It is currently the last ID plus 1. (Data architect)
  • SME-082 The bill payment transaction is saved before the account balance is reduced. If the account update then fails, what should happen to the saved transaction? Should the two be one all-or-nothing step? (Business analyst / architecture team)
  • SME-083 How must the system make sure that two bill payments made at the same time never get the same transaction ID? (Architecture team)
  • SME-084 If saving the bill payment transaction fails, what message should the user see and how should the failure be handled? (Business analyst)
  • SME-085 During a bill payment, should a failed card cross-reference lookup or a failed account update stop the remaining payment steps? (Business analyst)
  • SME-086 Please confirm the full rule for checking the account ID on bill payment: it is required, it must exist, and which error message goes with each case. (Legacy application SME)
  • SME-088 Online bill payments are recorded as type '02', category 2. Does that match the payment type and category in the transaction-type reference data? Should payment amounts be stored as positive or negative compared with purchases? (Payments business owner)
  • DEF-046 Is this intended? A failed card cross-reference lookup sets an error message but does not stop the posting: the transaction is still written (with whatever card number is in the cross-reference record) and the balance is still reduced and saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-058 Is this intended? The balance reduction and account rewrite are not conditional on the transaction write (or card lookup) succeeding, so a failed write leaves the account balance cleared with no payment transaction recorded. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-111 Is this intended? After each step of the payment (card cross-reference lookup, transaction browse, transaction write) the error flag is set on failure but never checked before the next step, so a failed lookup still leads to writing a transaction, and a failed transaction write still reduces and rewrites the account balance. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-115 Is this intended? Errors from the card cross-reference lookup or the transaction browse set the error flag but the payment steps continue anyway, so a transaction can be written with no card number. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-118 Is this intended? The account is rewritten even when the payment transaction write failed, and a failed account rewrite does not undo the transaction already written, so the transaction file and account balance can disagree. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Needs the highest existing transaction ID (a 'max ID' query or a descending keyed read of the last record). When there are no transactions it returns zero. Because 'highest plus 1' can race between concurrent payments, the new application should use a database sequence or an atomic ID generator, with the unique key as a safety net. Retrieve latest existing transaction
  • After the payment transaction is written, the account read for update earlier is saved with its reduced current balance. This should be an update on the same locked or version-checked account row. Ideally it runs in the same database transaction as the payment insert, so the balance and the payment record cannot disagree (subject to the decision on the non-atomic legacy behaviour). Save updated account balance
21. Set report period for transaction reportsfinal · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria · 1 screen

Lets an operator ask for a monthly or a yearly transaction report and works out the report period from today's date: the current calendar month, or January 1 to December 31 of the current year. It must never submit a period that does not match the option chosen.

As an operator, I want to pick a monthly or yearly report and have its date range set for me, so that the report job runs over the right period.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#21

REQ-F-172business ruleWhen the operator selects the monthly report option, the system shall set the report period from the first to the last day of the current month and submit the report job.AC-03

22. Reach and move around the transaction report screenfinal · online · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria · 2 screens

Handles reaching and leaving the transaction report screen for signed-on users. Without a session it sends them to sign-on, PF3 returns to the main menu, Enter processes the request, and any other key gets 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'. It must never allow report requests outside a valid signed-on session.

As a signed-on user, I want to open the transaction report screen, leave it, and be told when I press a key it does not support, so that I can ask for reports only within a valid session.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches reporting_only, security. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#22

23. Choose a report type and a valid custom periodfinal · online · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 13 criteria · 1 screen · 4 gaps

Lets a user pick a Monthly, Yearly or Custom transaction report. If more than one is marked, the first in that order wins. For Custom, every start and end date part is checked as present, numeric, in range and a real calendar date. It must never submit a report with no type selected or with an invalid custom date, and it always points the user to the first field in error.

As a user requesting a transaction report, I want to pick Monthly, Yearly or Custom and have my custom start and end dates checked, so that only a report with a clear, valid period is submitted.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#23

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-177business ruleWhen more than one report type is marked, the system shall process only the first in the order Monthly, Yearly, Custom and ignore the others.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-178business ruleIf none of Monthly, Yearly or Custom is marked, then the system shall show 'Select a report type to print report...' with the cursor on Monthly and submit nothing.AC-03
REQ-F-179business ruleIf a Custom report is requested and a start or end month, day or year is blank, then the system shall check the parts in the order start month, start day, start year, end month, end day, end year, show the message for the first blank part, put the cursor on that part and submit nothing.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-180design noteWhen all custom date parts are entered, the system shall convert each month and day to a two-digit number and each year to a four-digit number before checking them.AC-06
REQ-F-181business ruleIf a custom start or end month is above '12' or not numeric, then the system shall show 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...' or 'End Date - Not a valid Month...', put the cursor on that month and submit nothing.AC-07
REQ-F-182business ruleIf a custom start or end day is above '31' or not numeric, then the system shall show 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...' or 'End Date - Not a valid Day...', put the cursor on that day and submit nothing.AC-08
REQ-F-183business ruleIf a custom start or end year is not numeric, then the system shall show 'Start Date - Not a valid Year...' or 'End Date - Not a valid Year...', put the cursor on that year and submit nothing.AC-09
REQ-F-184business ruleIf the custom start date, checked as YYYY-MM-DD by the date utility (CSUTLDTC), is not a real calendar date, then the system shall show 'Start Date - Not a valid date...', put the cursor on the start month and submit nothing, while accepting a date the utility reports only as outside its supported range (message number '2513').AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-185business ruleIf the custom end date, checked as YYYY-MM-DD by the date utility (CSUTLDTC), is not a real calendar date, then the system shall show 'End Date - Not a valid date...', put the cursor on the end month and submit nothing, while accepting a date reported only as outside the supported range (message number '2513').AC-12
REQ-F-186business ruleWhen a Custom report's dates pass every check, the system shall use the entered start and end dates as the report period, name the report 'Custom' and go on to submit the report job.AC-13

Open questions

  • SME-151 For custom report dates: (a) the date check currently accepts some dates it flags as outside the supported range (message 2513). What does that message mean, and should those dates still be accepted? (b) Should a custom report be rejected when its start date is after its end date? (Reporting business owner)
  • SME-152 Report date entry only checks that the day is no greater than 31, and leaves month-specific limits (for example, the 31st of a 30-day month) to the later calendar check. Please confirm that the calendar check is the intended control. (Business analyst)
  • DEF-048 Is this intended? The 'not numeric' checks run after each part has already been converted to a number and moved back, so they can almost never fail (a year in particular is never rejected as non-numeric); there is no check that the start date is on or before the end date; and a date the utility reports as outside its supported range (2513) is accepted. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-078 Is this intended? If writing a line to 'JOBS' fails part-way, the lines already written stay in the queue and nothing removes them, so an incomplete job stream can be left for the internal reader. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-093 Is this intended? Marking more than one report type gives no warning; only the first (Monthly before Yearly before Custom) is run and the rest are silently ignored. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Before validating, turn the entered month and day into two-digit numbers and the year into a four-digit number (for example, '3' becomes '03'). This makes the range checks and the YYYY-MM-DD calendar check work on a consistent form. A standard date-parsing library can then do the calendar check. Normalize custom date entries numerically
24. Confirm and submit a transaction report for printingfinal · online · 8 requirements · 9 rules · 9 criteria · 1 screen

Asks the user to confirm a validated transaction report request. On 'Y' or 'y' it submits the report job to the batch queue with the start and end dates as its parameters, and tells the user in green that the report was submitted. It must never submit without an explicit 'Y' or 'y', and it must report a failure to queue the job instead of claiming success.

As a user requesting a transaction report, I want to confirm the request before it is sent to the batch job queue and be told it was submitted, so that reports are printed only when I mean them to be.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#24

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-187business ruleWhen a report request has passed its checks and the Confirm field is blank, the system shall show 'Please confirm to print the <report name> report...' (for example Monthly, Yearly or Custom), put the cursor on Confirm and submit nothing.AC-05
REQ-F-188business ruleWhen the Confirm field is 'Y' or 'y', the system shall submit the report job (TRNRPT00) to the batch job queue, clear the screen and show '<report name> report submitted for printing ...' in green.AC-06
REQ-F-189business ruleWhen the Confirm field is 'N' or 'n', the system shall clear all entry fields, submit nothing, and show the screen again with no message and the cursor on Monthly.AC-01
REQ-F-190business ruleIf the Confirm field holds any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N' or 'n', then the system shall show '"<value>" is not a valid value to confirm...', put the cursor on Confirm and submit nothing.AC-07
REQ-F-191design noteWhen the user confirms a report request with 'Y' or 'y', the system shall put the report start and end dates into the job's selection parameters (PARM-START-DATE, PARM-END-DATE) and date card (DATEPARM) as 'YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD'.AC-08
REQ-F-192side effectWhen the request is confirmed, the system shall write the job stream to the job queue 'JOBS' one 80-character line at a time, from the first line up to and including the '/*EOF' line (or a blank line), and never more than 1000 lines.AC-02
REQ-F-193error handlingIf writing a line of the report job to the job queue 'JOBS' fails, then the system shall stop writing further lines and show 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...' with the cursor on the Monthly field.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-194formattingWhen a report job has been submitted without error, the system shall clear all entry fields and show in green '<report name> report submitted for printing ...' with the cursor on the Monthly field.AC-09

  • SME-153 If writing the report job to the submission queue fails partway through, lines already written are not removed, so a partial job could still run. What should the operator see, how should partial jobs be handled, and how critical is this rule? (Batch operations lead)
  • SME-154 The 'report submitted' confirmation is shown in green. Must the new screen show success in a visually distinct way? (UX lead)
  • DEF-078 Is this intended? If writing a line to 'JOBS' fails part-way, the lines already written stay in the queue and nothing removes them, so an incomplete job stream can be left for the internal reader. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The report job needs the start and end dates as YYYY-MM-DD parameters, plus a combined 'YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD' date value. The new application should pass these as named parameters on the job submission request (for example, a message to the batch scheduler or a job-run API). It should not edit a job script text. Submit validated custom report period
25. Browse and page through the transaction listfinal · online · 25 requirements · 25 rules · 31 criteria · 2 screens · 2 gaps

Lets any signed-on user browse the transaction list ten rows at a time in transaction ID order. They can start from a transaction ID they type and page forward and backward. Paging must never skip or repeat a transaction at a page boundary. A non-numeric filter must be rejected, and the user must be told plainly when they reach the top or bottom of the list.

As a signed-on user, I want to see transactions ten at a time, start from a transaction ID I choose, and page forward and backward, so that I can find the transaction I am looking for.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#25

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-195business ruleWhen the transaction list is opened from another screen (not a re-entry), the system shall mark itself as re-entered, clear the screen, read the first page of up to 10 transactions from the start of the transaction file and display it.AC-01
REQ-F-196design noteThe system shall, at the start of every transaction list interaction, clear the message line, reset its error, end-of-file and next-page indicators, set the screen to be fully redrawn, and place the cursor on the transaction ID field.AC-02
REQ-F-197business ruleWhen the user presses a key on the redisplayed transaction list, the system shall read the screen input and then run search and selection for Enter, show the previous page for PF7, or show the next page for PF8.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-198business ruleWhen the Tran ID filter is blank and the user presses Enter, the system shall show the first page starting from the first transaction on file.AC-05
REQ-F-199business ruleWhen the Tran ID filter is numeric and the user presses Enter, the system shall start the list at that transaction ID, or at the next higher ID if it does not exist.AC-06
REQ-F-200business ruleIf the Tran ID filter is not entirely digits across all 16 positions, then the system shall show 'Tran ID must be Numeric ...', put the cursor on the filter, keep the entry, and not build a new page.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-201business ruleWhen the user presses Enter without selecting a row, the system shall reset the page number to 0, build the first page (shown as page 1 if any transaction is found), and clear the filter field when no error occurred.AC-09
REQ-F-202formattingWhen the numeric Tran ID filter is higher than every transaction ID on file, the system shall show 'You are at the top of the page...' with no rows and page number 0.AC-10
REQ-F-203business ruleWhen a page is built after Enter, PF3 (return from the transaction detail screen) or PF7, the system shall start with the transaction at the starting ID itself (or the next higher ID) without skipping it.AC-11
REQ-F-204formattingWhen a forward page is built, the system shall first blank all 10 rows, so that rows after the last transaction found stay empty.AC-12
REQ-F-205formattingWhen a transaction record has been retrieved for display on the list page, the system shall convert the transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) to the signed display amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) and derive the display date (WS-TRAN-DATE) as MM/DD/YY from the month, the day and the last two digits of the year of the origination timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS).AC-31
REQ-F-206design noteThe system shall remember the transaction ID shown in row 1 as the page's first transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), used as the starting point for the next PF7, and the ID in row 10 as the page's last transaction ID.AC-13
REQ-F-207design noteWhen a transaction is placed in the tenth row, the system shall remember its ID as the page's last transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), which the next PF8 starts from.AC-14
REQ-F-208business ruleWhen all 10 rows are filled, the system shall add 1 to the page number and read one transaction ahead, setting next page available to Y if another transaction exists and to N if not.AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-209business ruleWhen the transactions run out before 10 rows are filled, the system shall set next page available to N and add 1 to the page number only if at least one transaction was placed on the page.AC-17
REQ-F-210formattingWhen the end of the transactions is reached while filling the page or in the look-ahead read, the system shall show the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...'.AC-18
REQ-F-211error handlingIf positioning on or reading the transaction file fails for any reason other than not found or end of file, then the system shall stop filling the page and show 'Unable to lookup transaction...'.AC-19
REQ-F-212business ruleWhen the user presses PF8 and a next page is available, the system shall restart at the last transaction ID shown on the current page, skip that transaction so it is not repeated, and show up to the next 10 transactions in transaction ID order.AC-20
REQ-F-213formattingIf the user presses PF8 when no next page is available, then the system shall redisplay the current screen without erasing it and with the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'.AC-21, AC-22
REQ-F-214business ruleWhen the user presses PF7 on the transaction list and the current page number is greater than 1, the system shall start reading from the first transaction ID shown on the current page, mark a next page as available, and show the previous page.AC-23
REQ-F-215formattingWhen the user presses PF7 and the current page number is 1 or lower, the system shall redisplay the current screen without clearing it, with the message 'You are already at the top of the page...', and still mark a next page as available.AC-24, AC-25
REQ-F-216design noteWhen paging backward with PF7, the system shall first step back past the current page's first transaction, so that the previous page does not repeat it.AC-26
REQ-F-217formattingWhen paging backward, the system shall clear the ten rows and fill them from row 10 up to row 1 with the preceding transactions in descending ID order, stopping early if the start of the transaction file is reached or a read fails.AC-27
REQ-F-218business ruleWhen all ten rows have been filled while paging backward, the system shall check for one more earlier transaction and decrease the page number by 1 if one exists and the page number is above 1, otherwise set the page number to 1.AC-28, AC-29
REQ-F-219error handlingWhen the start of the transaction file is reached before all ten rows are filled while paging backward, the system shall show the message 'You have reached the top of the page...', leave the unfilled top rows blank and leave the page number unchanged.AC-30

Open questions

  • SME-164 When the operator pages back through the transaction list, the page number is reset to 1 "otherwise". Which situation triggers that reset: when the look-back read failed or the page number is already 1 or less, when no next page is flagged as available, or both? (Business analyst)
  • SME-165 The transaction list only describes how transactions are placed in rows 1 and 10. How should transactions be placed in rows 2 through 9? (Business analyst)
  • SME-166 On the transaction list, how is the next screen chosen when the operator selects a transaction, what should PF3 do, and what should happen when the list is opened without any information from a calling screen? (Application owner)
  • SME-167 When the operator presses PF8 (next page) and no last transaction ID is held, the list currently starts after the highest possible key, which probably shows an empty page. Should the new system keep this behaviour? (Business analyst)
  • SME-169 When the operator searches the transaction list for a transaction ID that does not exist, should the list start at the next higher transaction, as it does today, or should the system report 'not found'? (Product owner)
  • SME-170 When the operator pages back and fewer than 10 earlier transactions exist, should the previous page start from the beginning of the file and fill all 10 rows from the top, rather than leaving the top rows blank? (Product owner)
  • SME-171 How important is the forward paging rule on the transaction list (10 transactions per page, with a check for whether another page follows)? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or is it a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Product owner)
  • DEF-014 Is this intended? If the start of the file is reached before ten rows are filled (possible only if transactions were added or removed between screens), the page number is not reduced, the top rows stay blank and the remembered first ID is not updated, so the screen shows a partial page with the old page number. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-050 Is this intended? A filter beyond the last transaction gives a not-found browse that shows 'You are at the top of the page...' and page 0 instead of saying no transaction was found; and a short ID typed without leading zeros is rejected as non-numeric because the 16-character field keeps blanks. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Every request to the list starts from a clean state: no leftover message, no error, end-of-list or next-page flags carried over, and focus on the transaction ID filter. Page position comes only from the paging state the server keeps (or the request carries), not from previous screen contents. Show first transaction page on entry
  • Each page response must keep the transaction ID of its first row and of its last row as paging cursors. The first ID is where the next previous-page request starts. Keep them in the user's session or return them as opaque cursors. Place first row and record page start
  • The ID of the tenth row is the cursor for the next-page request. The next page is a keyed range read of transactions with ID strictly greater than this cursor, in ascending ID order, limited to 10 (plus one look-ahead to tell whether more exist). Place last row and record page end
  • The previous page is a keyed range read of transactions with ID strictly less than the current page's first ID, in descending order, limited to 10, then reversed for display. The current first transaction is never repeated. Use an index on transaction ID that supports reading in both directions from a key. Position backward browse before current page
26. Select a transaction from the list to view its detailsfinal · online · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 6 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

Lets a signed-on user mark one transaction on the list with 'S' (or 's') and open its details on the Transaction View. Only the first marked row, top to bottom, counts. Any other code is rejected with 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S'. A stale earlier selection must never open a transaction the user did not choose.

As a signed-on user, I want to mark a transaction in the list with 'S' and open its details, so that I can look at one transaction closely.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#26

27. Transaction list access and session handlingfinal · online · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria · 3 screens

Governs access to the transaction list. Only signed-on users reach it: anyone without a session goes to sign-on. PF3 returns to the main menu, and unsupported keys get 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'. Any signed-on user, regular or admin, sees transactions from every account and card. That is current behaviour and the team must confirm it deliberately rather than change it by accident.

As the business, I want the transaction list reachable only within a signed-on session, with clear key handling and return to the main menu, so that users move safely through the screens.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, security. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#27

  • SME-168 Should any signed-on user, including regular users, be able to list and open every transaction in the system, or should each user see only the transactions for their own account or cards? (Security/compliance officer)
  • DEF-177 Confirm this is deliberate: Any regular user can see all customers' transactions (card-holder data) because the list is not scoped to the user's account. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The list is a stateful interaction. Between requests the application must keep the user's session state: signed-on user, current page number, first and last transaction IDs of the page, next-page flag and any selection. This can be a server-side session keyed by an authenticated session token, or signed state round-tripped with the client. Each response then waits for the user's next action. Transaction list screen navigation and session routing
28. Look up a single transactionfinal · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria · 2 screens

Opens the Transaction View for a signed-on user. If they came from the transaction list with a transaction picked, its ID is pre-filled and looked up straight away. If the transaction ID is left empty, the screen must refuse to look anything up and say 'Tran ID can NOT be empty...'.

As a signed-on user, I want to open the transaction view, with the transaction I picked already filled in, and be told when I leave the ID empty, so that I can see the details of one transaction.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#28

REQ-F-227business ruleIf the entered transaction ID (TRNIDINI) is spaces or low-values, then the system shall flag an error, show the message 'Tran ID can NOT be empty...' and redisplay the screen with the cursor on the transaction ID field.AC-02

29. View a single transactionfinal · online · 11 requirements · 11 rules · 13 criteria · 2 screens

Lets cardholders and staff look up one transaction by its Transaction ID and see its full details: card, type, category, source, signed amount, description, timestamps and merchant. It must show the exact stored record and amount sign. A missing ID gets 'Transaction ID NOT found...', and a lookup failure gets 'Unable to lookup Transaction...'. PF3, PF4 and PF5 return, clear or go to the list.

As a cardholder or staff user, I want to look up a transaction by its Transaction ID and see its full details, so that I can review what was charged, where and when.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#29

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-228business ruleWhen the user presses Enter on the Transaction View screen, the system shall read the entered Transaction ID and look up the transaction.AC-01
REQ-F-229business ruleWhen a Transaction ID is entered and Enter is pressed, or the user arrives from the transaction list with a transaction selected, the system shall clear the previously shown details and look up the transaction record with that ID in the transaction file (TRANSACT).AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-230business ruleIf the user asks to view a transaction and the Transaction ID is blank, then the system shall not look anything up and shall redisplay the screen with the message 'Tran ID can NOT be empty...'.AC-04

REQ-F-232formattingThe system shall show the transaction amount on the Transaction View with a leading sign, 8 digits before the decimal point and 2 after (format +99999999.99).AC-13

REQ-F-237business ruleIf the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4 or PF5 on the Transaction View, then the system shall redisplay the screen with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-172 The transaction view screen only displays a transaction, but today it reads the record as if for update, which locks it. Is the lock needed, for example to guarantee a consistent read, or should the new system use a plain read with no lock? (Solution architect)
  • SME-173 On the transaction view screen, PF3 and PF5 are accepted as valid keys. What should each one do? (Business analyst)
  • SME-174 What should the transaction view screen do when it is opened without any information from a calling screen? (Business analyst)
  • SME-175 When looking up a transaction fails for a reason other than 'not found', what message should the operator see and what should happen next? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-051 Is this intended? The view-only lookup reads the transaction with UPDATE, taking an exclusive lock that is never used for a rewrite and is held until the task ends; another user updating the same record at that moment would get an error. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-160 Is this intended? The stored amount holds 9 digits before the decimal point but the display format holds only 8, so an amount of 100,000,000.00 or more would lose its leading digit on screen. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

30. Open and navigate the Add Transaction screenfinal · online · 8 requirements · 7 rules · 9 criteria · 2 screens

Gives staff the Add Transaction screen within a signed-on session. It can be pre-filled from a selected value or, with PF5, copied from the most recent transaction on file. PF3 goes back, PF4 clears the form and Enter validates and adds. Users without a session go to sign-on, and other keys get 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.

As a staff user, I want to open the Add Transaction screen, pre-filled from a selected or the most recent transaction where useful, and move between screens with function keys, so that I can enter new transactions quickly within a signed-on session.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, security. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#30

31. Identify the account and card for a new transactionfinal · online · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 13 criteria · 1 screen

Before a new transaction is checked further, finds the account and card it belongs to from either the account ID or the card number, using the card cross-reference. When an account ID is given, the card linked to it replaces any typed card number. A transaction must never be saved against an account or card that was not found, or when either field is blank or non-numeric.

As a staff user, I want the system to find the account and card for a new transaction from either the account ID or the card number, so that the transaction is recorded against the right card.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#31

Open questions

  • DEF-052 Is this intended? When an account ID is entered, the card number the operator typed is overwritten without any check that it belongs to that account. If the account has several cards, the transaction goes to whichever card the account index returns first. Also, the account (11) and card (16) input fields are not justified or zero-filled, so a shorter entry fails the all-digits check, and the NUMVAL conversion that follows can never change the value. (Subject-matter expert)

None.

32. Validate new transaction detailsfinal · online · 24 requirements · 24 rules · 30 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Checks every new transaction before it is saved. The eleven mandatory fields are checked in a fixed order, then numeric type, category and merchant codes, an amount in the form -99999999.99, and real calendar dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD. Only the first problem is reported, with its exact message and the cursor on that field. Nothing is saved until every check passes.

As a staff user, I want every new transaction's fields checked for presence, numeric codes, amount format and real dates, with one clear message for the first problem, so that only complete and well-formed transactions are recorded.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#32

REQ-F-253business ruleWhen Enter is pressed on the Add Transaction screen and the account or card number has passed its checks, the system shall check the transaction fields for blanks in this order: Type CD, Category CD, Source, Description, Amount, Orig Date, Proc Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, and report only the first blank field.AC-01
REQ-F-254business ruleIf a mandatory transaction field is blank (spaces or low-values), then the system shall show that field's message, put the cursor on that field, redisplay the screen and save nothing.AC-02

REQ-F-261business ruleIf all fields up to the origination date are entered and the processing date is blank, then the system shall show 'Proc Date can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on the processing date (TPROCDTI).AC-09
REQ-F-262business ruleIf all fields up to the processing date are entered and the merchant ID is blank, then the system shall show 'Merchant ID can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on the merchant ID (MIDI).AC-10
REQ-F-263business ruleIf all fields up to the merchant ID are entered and the merchant name is blank, then the system shall show 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on the merchant name (MNAMEI).AC-11
REQ-F-264business ruleIf all fields up to the merchant name are entered and the merchant city is blank, then the system shall show 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on the merchant city (MCITYI).AC-12
REQ-F-265business ruleIf all fields up to the merchant city are entered and the merchant zip is blank, then the system shall show 'Merchant Zip can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on the merchant zip (MZIPI).AC-13
REQ-F-266business ruleWhen all eleven mandatory transaction fields are entered, the system shall pass the blank check and go on to the numeric and format checks.AC-14
REQ-F-267business ruleIf the transaction type code is not numeric, then the system shall show 'Type CD must be Numeric...' with the cursor on the type code and save nothing.AC-15
REQ-F-268business ruleIf the type code is numeric and the category code is not numeric, then the system shall show 'Category CD must be Numeric...' with the cursor on the category code and save nothing.AC-16
REQ-F-269business ruleIf the amount entered does not start with '-' or '+', followed by eight digits, a '.', and two digits, then the system shall reject it with 'Amount should be in format -99999999.99' and save nothing.AC-17, AC-18
REQ-F-270design noteWhen the amount passes the format check, the system shall convert it to a signed number with two decimals, show it back in the form +99999999.99, and store that value as the transaction amount when the transaction is added.AC-19, AC-20
REQ-F-271business ruleIf the origination date is not in the form YYYY-MM-DD (four digits, '-', two digits, '-', two digits), then the system shall reject the entry, show 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' and save nothing.AC-21, AC-22
REQ-F-272business ruleIf the processing date is not in the form YYYY-MM-DD, then the system shall reject the entry, show 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' and save nothing.AC-23
REQ-F-273business ruleIf the origination date has the right form but the date-check service (CSUTLDTC) does not confirm it as a real calendar date (severity not '0000' and message number not '2513'), then the system shall show 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' and save nothing.AC-24, AC-25
REQ-F-274business ruleIf the origination date is accepted but the date-check service (CSUTLDTC) does not confirm the processing date as a real calendar date (severity not '0000' and message number not '2513'), then the system shall show 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' and save nothing.AC-26
REQ-F-275business ruleIf all earlier checks pass and the Merchant ID is not entirely digits across its 9 positions, then the system shall reject the entry, show 'Merchant ID must be Numeric...' and put the cursor on Merchant ID.AC-27, AC-28, AC-29
REQ-F-276business ruleThe system shall stop the Transaction Add checks at the first failed check and show only that message, so a later check is made only after every earlier check has passed.AC-30
