Open questions

  • SME-176 When adding a transaction, the system accepts dates that the date check flags with message 2513 (outside the range the date utility supports). What does 2513 mean for the business, and should those dates still be accepted? Should the processing date also have to be on or after the origination date, and should future dates be refused? (Product owner)
  • DEF-053 Confirm this is deliberate: A date for which the date service returns message number '2513' (CEEDAYS feedback X'09D1' = 2513, 'Unsupp. Range', i.e. a year outside the supported range) is accepted as valid instead of rejected. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Parse the validated amount text into an exact decimal with two places (never floating point). Echo it back to the user in the canonical form +99999999.99, and store exactly that decimal value as the transaction amount when the transaction is added. Normalize entered transaction amount
33. Record a confirmed new transactionfinal · online · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 9 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Records a validated, confirmed new transaction. It gets the next transaction number (the highest on file plus 1, as 16 zero-padded digits) and is written with the entered details and the card found for the account. The user sees 'Transaction added successfully. Your Tran ID is <number>.'. Numbers must never be duplicated or reused, and a failed write must say so and save nothing.

As a staff user, I want a confirmed, valid transaction to be numbered and written to the transaction file with a clear confirmation or error, so that the account's activity is recorded accurately.

Open questions

  • SME-177 What type and length should the transaction number have in the transaction master store, so that new transaction numbers meet that format? (Data architect)
  • SME-178 When the origination and processing dates entered as YYYY-MM-DD are stored as timestamps, what time portion and timestamp format should be used? (Data architect)
  • SME-179 New transactions are numbered 'highest existing number + 1'. Must this scheme be kept, or should a central sequence or counter be used so that numbers cannot clash with other postings made at the same time or with transactions created by batch jobs? (Solution architect)
  • DEF-015 Is this intended? The next number is taken as highest-plus-one with no lock, so two users adding at the same moment can get the same number; the second write then fails with 'Tran ID already exist...' and the user must try again. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-060 Is this intended? The type and category codes are written as entered without checking that they exist in the reference tables; they are only checked for being present and numeric. (Subject-matter expert)

None.

34. Confirm a transaction before it is addedfinal · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria · 1 screen

Makes the operator explicitly confirm a validated transaction before it is added. 'N', 'n' or blank asks 'Confirm to add this transaction...'. Any value other than Y/y, N/n or blank gets 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...'. No transaction may ever be added without an explicit 'Y' or 'y'.

As an operator entering a transaction, I want the system to ask me to confirm before adding it and to reject an invalid confirmation, so that no transaction is added without my explicit confirmation.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#34

REQ-F-285business ruleIf every field passes validation and Confirm holds any value other than 'Y', 'N', 'n' or blank, then the system shall redisplay the Transaction Add screen with 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' and the cursor on Confirm, and add nothing.AC-03

35. Validate a date against a format maskfinal · service · 13 requirements · 13 rules · 14 criteria · 2 screens · 2 gaps

A shared date check used by the report date range and Add Transaction screens. It tests a 10-character date against a 10-character format mask and returns a severity, a message number and a reason such as 'Date is valid', 'Datevalue error' or 'Invalid month'. Callers treat the date as invalid when the severity is not 0000, unless the message number is 2513. Real dates must be accepted and impossible dates rejected.

As a screen that accepts dates (report date range, transaction add), I want a date checked against its format mask with a clear result and reason, so that invalid dates are rejected with a meaningful error.

Final: signed off by Sam (acceptance), 2026-11-25 Risk low. rec/CustomerAccountSelf-Service/OnlineAccountandTransactionManagement#35

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-286design noteThe system shall pass the caller's 10-character date and 10-character format mask to the date conversion service (CEEDAYS) and record the returned severity and message number as 4-digit values in its result.AC-12
REQ-F-287design noteThe system shall return an 80-character result made of the severity, 'Mesg Code:', the message number, the result text, 'TstDate:' with the tested date and 'Mask used:' with the mask, and shall set the program return code to the severity.AC-13
REQ-F-288business ruleWhen the date conversion service returns an all-zero feedback token for the date and mask it was given, the system shall set the result text to 'Date is valid'.AC-01
REQ-F-289business ruleIf the date conversion service reports insufficient data (feedback X'000309CB59C3C5C5', message 2507), then the system shall set the result text to 'Insufficient'.AC-02
REQ-F-290business ruleIf the date conversion service reports a bad date value (feedback X'000309CC59C3C5C5', severity 3, message 2508), then the system shall set the result text to 'Datevalue error'.AC-14
REQ-F-291business ruleIf the date conversion service reports an invalid era (feedback X'000309CD59C3C5C5', message 2509), then the system shall set the result text to 'Invalid Era'.AC-03
REQ-F-292business ruleIf the date conversion service reports an unsupported date range (feedback X'000309D159C3C5C5', message 2513), then the system shall set the result text to 'Unsupp. Range'.AC-04
REQ-F-293business ruleIf the date conversion service reports an invalid month (feedback X'000309D559C3C5C5', message 2517), then the system shall set the result text to 'Invalid month'.AC-05
REQ-F-294business ruleIf the date conversion service reports a bad format mask (feedback X'000309D659C3C5C5', message 2518), then the system shall set the result text to 'Bad Pic String'.AC-06
REQ-F-295business ruleIf the date conversion service reports a year-in-era of zero (feedback X'000309D959C3C5C5', message 2521), then the system shall set the result text to 'YearInEra is 0'.AC-07
REQ-F-296business ruleIf the date conversion service reports that the date contains non-numeric characters, then the system shall return the result text 'Nonnumeric data' together with the service's severity and message code, so the caller treats the date as invalid.AC-08
REQ-F-297business ruleIf the date conversion feedback matches none of the recognised tokens, then the system shall set the result text to 'Date is invalid'.AC-09
REQ-F-298business ruleIf the returned severity is not '0000' and the message number is not '2513', then the calling screens (report date range, transaction add) shall treat the date as invalid and show their error, for example 'Start Date - Not a valid date...' or 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...'.AC-10, AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-237 The date-check service returns an all-zeros code to mean 'date is valid', but the legacy code labels that code 'invalid date'. Can you confirm the code keeps meaning success and the misleading label is dropped? (Development lead)
  • SME-238 The date-check service reports one of ten outcomes (valid, insufficient data, bad value, invalid era, unsupported range, invalid month, bad format, non-numeric, zero year, unrecognized). How should the new date-check service's own results map to these ten outcomes? (Application architect)
  • SME-239 Screens currently accept a date that the date check flags as outside the supported range. Is accepting out-of-range dates a business rule, or a workaround the new validation should drop? (Card operations business analyst)
  • DEF-055 Is this intended? The condition for the all-zero (successful) feedback token is named FC-INVALID-DATE, although it means the date is valid; the behaviour is correct but the name is misleading. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-095 Is this intended? After the call the whole date structure, including its 2-byte binary length prefix, is moved into the 10-character tested-date field, so the 'TstDate:' part of the result shows two binary bytes followed by only the first 8 characters of the date instead of the date itself. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-119 Confirm this is deliberate: The calling screens accept a date when the message number is 2513, which is this unsupported-range result, so a date that the date service cannot handle is let through as valid. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Provide a reusable date-validation function that takes a date string and a format pattern and returns a structured result: a 4-digit severity, a 4-digit message number and a reason. Implement it with the platform's standard strict date parsing, which rejects impossible dates. Map outcomes to the legacy message numbers (2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2521) where callers depend on them, for example the 2513 exception. Submit date and mask for conversion
  • Return the result as a structured value (severity, message number, result text, tested date, mask used) with severity as the outcome code. Keep a formatter that renders the legacy 80-character text ('Mesg Code:', 'TstDate:', 'Mask used:') only if a consumer still needs that exact layout. Submit date and mask for conversion

Customer Data Setup

Credit Card List Detail View and Update

1. Browse and page the card listdraft · online · 20 requirements · 22 rules · 28 criteria · 3 screens

Lets card operations staff browse every credit card seven at a time, paging forward and back, so they can find the card they want to view or update. Each row shows the card number, its account and whether it is active. It must never skip or repeat a card between pages, and it must always tell the user correctly when there are no more pages forward or back.

As a card operations user, I want to see the credit cards seven at a time and page forward and back through them, so that I can find the card I need to view or update.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001formattingWhen the card list is started from the main menu, the system shall show the first 7 cards from the beginning of the card file.AC-01
REQ-F-002design noteWhen the card list is started from another program with context 'enter' (from main menu option 3, or on return from card detail or card update), the system shall clear the saved first and last card positions, set the page to 1 and the last-page flag to 'not shown', and not read any screen input.AC-02
REQ-F-003business ruleWhen the user arrives with PF3 from another program (such as leaving card detail or card update), or the list is re-entered from another program, the system shall reset the session to page 1 as a regular user and list the cards from the beginning of the card file.AC-03
REQ-F-004business ruleWhile the card list fills a page going forward, when a card record passes the account and card-number filters, the system shall add its card number, account number and active status as the next row and, if it is the first row and the page number is 0, set the page number to 1.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-005business ruleWhen a page reaches 7 cards, the system shall stop filling the page and read one more card record ahead, without applying the filters, to decide whether a next page exists.AC-06
REQ-F-006business ruleWhen the look-ahead read after a full page finds another card record, the system shall set the next page indicator to 'Y' and remember that card as the start of the next page.AC-07, AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-007business ruleWhen a page is filled with the maximum of 7 cards and reading one card further reaches the end of the card file, the system shall record that no next page exists and, if no other message is set, show 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW'.AC-08, AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-008business ruleWhen the end of the card file is reached before the page holds 7 cards, the system shall stop reading, record that no next page exists, and show 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' if no other message is set.AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-009formattingWhen the end of the card file is reached on page 1 with no card listed, the system shall show 'NO RECORDS FOUND FOR THIS SEARCH CONDITION.' instead of 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW'.AC-12
REQ-F-010business ruleWhen there is no input error and the user presses PF8 while a next page exists ('Y'), the system shall add one to the page number and list cards starting from the card found by the look-ahead read after the last card shown.AC-13
REQ-F-011business ruleWhen there is no input error, exit, page change or valid selection (for example Enter with nothing selected, or PF8 with no next page), the system shall redisplay cards, applying any filters, starting from the first card of the page currently shown.AC-14
REQ-F-012business ruleWhen there is no input error and the user presses PF7 while on page 1, the system shall redisplay page 1 starting from its first card with the message 'NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY'.AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-013business ruleWhen there is no input error and the user presses PF7 while not on page 1, the system shall subtract one from the page number and read backward from the first card of the current page, skipping that card itself.AC-17
REQ-F-014business ruleWhile reading backward, the system shall place each card that passes the account and card-number filters into the rows from row 7 up to row 1, stop when row 1 is filled, and make the card in row 1 the new first card of the page.AC-18
REQ-F-015design noteWhen the user pages backward, the system shall set the next page indicator to 'Y' and remember the first card of the page just left as the start of the next page, so that PF8 returns to that page.AC-19
REQ-F-016design noteWhen the user presses any key other than PF8, the system shall reset the last-page flag to 'not shown'.AC-28
REQ-F-017formattingWhen the user presses PF8 on the last page for the first time, the system shall show the page again with the instruction 'TYPE S FOR DETAIL, U TO UPDATE ANY RECORD' and remember that the last page has been shown.AC-20
REQ-F-018formattingWhen the user presses PF8 again on a last page that has already been shown, the system shall redisplay that page with the message 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY'.AC-21
REQ-F-019formattingThe system shall show 'TYPE S FOR DETAIL, U TO UPDATE ANY RECORD' on the card list in every case not otherwise covered, except when the message is 'NO RECORDS FOUND FOR THIS SEARCH CONDITION.' or a filter is in error.AC-22, AC-23, AC-24
REQ-F-020business ruleWhen the user presses PF3 and the originating program is the card list, the system shall transfer control to the main menu program ('COMEN01C') with the shared context, ending the card list.AC-25, AC-26, AC-27

Open questions

  • SME-096 On the card list screen, the filter messages say the account number must be 11 digits and the card number 16 digits, but only 'numeric' is checked. Should exactly 11 and 16 digits be required? (Business analyst)
  • SME-097 On the card list screen, what should happen when the user pages forward past the last page? Should 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' appear on the first press, or is the current behaviour intended (the first PF8 shows the action prompt and only the second shows the message)? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-098 On the card list screen, what should happen when the user presses Enter with exactly one card marked 'S' (view) or 'U' (update)? (Business analyst)
  • SME-099 Please confirm this card list rule: while a page is being filled, each card record that is read successfully (a duplicate key counts as success) and passes the account and card filters adds one row showing its card number, account number and active status. (Business analyst)
  • SME-100 Please confirm the priority of the card list filter rule (by account and/or card number, both applied together). Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that would be costly if it were wrong? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-101 When paging back reaches the start of the card list before 7 rows are filled, should the screen show a partial page without an error? Today it shows 'File Error'. (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-012 Is this intended? The look-ahead read does not apply the account or card filters, so with a filter active the next page indicator can be 'Y' when no further matching card exists. PF8 then moves to an empty page. Also, the page number holds one digit, so paging forward from page 9 wraps it to 0, which the read then resets to 1. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-013 Is this intended? The backward read has no end-of-file case. If fewer than 7 matching cards come before the current page (possible with a filter, or after the page-9 wrap), the read hits the start of the file and shows a 'File Error: READ ...' message instead of a partial page. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-075 Is this intended? On PF3 return the whole shared session area is cleared and the user is set to regular user type, so the signed-on user ID and any admin type carried in the session are lost for later screens. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-092 Is this intended? A filter typed on Enter is applied from the first card of the page currently shown, not from the start of the file, so on page 2 or later earlier matching cards are missed and an empty result shows 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' instead of 'NO RECORDS FOUND FOR THIS SEARCH CONDITION.'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-099 Is this intended? The fallback branch that would leave the instruction blank can never be taken, because the screen set-up always clears the info message first, so the 'no info message' test is always true and the instruction is shown in every remaining case. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-121 Is this intended? Because this branch starts from the current page's first card, a newly typed filter is not searched from the start of the file when the user is past page 1. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Arriving at the list from the menu or back from card detail or card update starts a fresh browse: the stored first and last card positions are cleared, the page is set to 1, the 'last page shown' marker is cleared, and nothing left in the form from before is read as input. Session context reset on entry from another program
  • The browse state kept between requests must hold the first card of each page shown, so that after paging back the next-page marker is 'Y' and a forward page returns to exactly the page the user left. A keyset or cursor over card number is enough; no offset counting is needed. Backward paging and first-page guard
  • The per-user browse state carries a 'last page already shown' marker that is cleared on every action except page-forward. It is what tells the first page-forward on the last page apart from a repeated one. Reset last-page indicator unless paging down
2. Filter the card list by account and card numberdraft · online · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 10 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

Lets card operations staff narrow the card list to one account, one card number, or both. A filter left blank or all zeros is not applied. The list must show only cards that match every filter supplied, and must reject a non-numeric filter with its exact message instead of showing an unfiltered list.

As a card operations user, I want to filter the card list by account number and card number, so that I only see the cards I am looking for.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-021business ruleWhen the account filter or card filter is left blank or all zeros, the system shall treat that filter as not supplied and not filter on that field.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-022business ruleIf the card filter supplied is non-numeric and no earlier error exists, then the system shall reject it with 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER'.AC-01
REQ-F-023business ruleIf the account filter supplied is non-numeric, then the system shall reject it with 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER' and protect the selection rows.AC-02
REQ-F-024business ruleWhen a numeric account filter or card filter is submitted, the system shall accept and save that account number or card number.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-025business ruleWhen a valid account filter is entered, the system shall list only cards whose account number equals the filter.AC-04
REQ-F-026business ruleWhen a valid card number filter is entered, the system shall list only the card with that number, and when both filters are entered, the system shall list a card only if it matches both.AC-05
REQ-F-027error handlingIf an account or card filter entered is invalid, then the system shall redisplay the list screen with only the filter error message and no instruction line, re-reading the cards only when both filters are valid or blank.AC-06, AC-07, AC-08, AC-09, AC-10

Open questions

  • SME-096 On the card list screen, the filter messages say the account number must be 11 digits and the card number 16 digits, but only 'numeric' is checked. Should exactly 11 and 16 digits be required? (Business analyst)
  • SME-097 On the card list screen, what should happen when the user pages forward past the last page? Should 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' appear on the first press, or is the current behaviour intended (the first PF8 shows the action prompt and only the second shows the message)? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-098 On the card list screen, what should happen when the user presses Enter with exactly one card marked 'S' (view) or 'U' (update)? (Business analyst)
  • SME-099 Please confirm this card list rule: while a page is being filled, each card record that is read successfully (a duplicate key counts as success) and passes the account and card filters adds one row showing its card number, account number and active status. (Business analyst)
  • SME-100 Please confirm the priority of the card list filter rule (by account and/or card number, both applied together). Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that would be costly if it were wrong? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-092 Is this intended? A filter typed on Enter is applied from the first card of the page currently shown, not from the start of the file, so on page 2 or later earlier matching cards are missed and an empty result shows 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' instead of 'NO RECORDS FOUND FOR THIS SEARCH CONDITION.'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-099 Is this intended? The fallback branch that would leave the instruction blank can never be taken, because the screen set-up always clears the info message first, so the 'no info message' test is always true and the instruction is shown in every remaining case. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-124 Is this intended? On an input error the re-read is started from an empty key, so the cards shown come from the start of the file even when the user was on a later page, while the page number shown stays the same. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

3. Select a card to view or updatedraft · online · 6 requirements · 4 rules · 7 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

Lets card operations staff mark one card in the list with 'S' to view its details or 'U' to update it, and takes them straight to that screen with the card's account and card number. It must never act when more than one row is marked or when a code other than S, U or blank is entered.

As a card operations user, I want to mark one card in the list with S or U, so that I can go straight to its details or its update screen.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#3

REQ-F-029business ruleIf the filters are valid and the operator enters a code other than 'S', 'U' or blank, then the system shall reject it with 'INVALID ACTION CODE' and mark the affected rows in error.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03

REQ-F-033business ruleWhen the user types 'U' against one card row and presses Enter with no input error, the system shall transfer to card update (COCRDUPC) passing that row's account and card number, with the card list as the previous program and context 'enter'.AC-07

4. Search and view card detailsdraft · online · 20 requirements · 21 rules · 33 criteria · 2 screens

Lets card operations staff enter an account number and a 16-digit card number and see that card's embossed name, expiry month and year, and active status. The card is looked up by card number alone. It must reject missing or non-numeric input with the exact messages, and must say clearly when the card is not found or the card file cannot be read.

As a card operations user, I want to enter an account and card number and see that card's details, so that I can check the card's embossed name, expiry and status.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-034business ruleWhen the account or card number entered on the card detail screen is '*' or blank, the system shall treat that search criterion as not supplied.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-035business ruleIf the account is not supplied (blank, '*' or all zeros) after the user presses Enter, then the system shall reject the input, show 'Account number not provided' if no other message is already set, reset the saved account to 0 and redisplay the account field as '*' in red.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-036business ruleIf a supplied account is not entirely numeric, then the system shall reject the input, show the account in red with 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER' if no other message is already set, and reset the saved account to 0.AC-06
REQ-F-037business ruleWhen a supplied account is an 11-digit number that is not all zeros, the system shall accept it and keep it as the current account for the session.AC-07
REQ-F-038business ruleIf the user resubmits the card detail screen and the card number is blank, '*', spaces or all zeros, then the system shall treat it as an input error, show the field as '*' in red, show 'Card number not provided' unless an earlier message is already set, clear the saved card number to 0 and not look up a card.AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-039business ruleIf the user resubmits the card detail screen and the card number is not made up of 16 digits, then the system shall treat it as an input error, show the card field in red, show 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER' unless an earlier message is already set, and clear the saved card number to 0.AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-040business ruleWhen the card number entered is a 16-digit number other than all zeros, the system shall accept it and save it in the shared session details as the card to look up.AC-12
REQ-F-041business ruleIf the user resubmits the card detail screen with both the account number and the card number missing (blank, '*' or all zeros), then the system shall show 'No input received' in place of any other message, mark both fields with '*' in red, and not look up a card.AC-13, AC-14
REQ-F-042business ruleWhen the user presses Enter on the card detail screen and PF3 was not pressed, the system shall check the entered account and card number, redisplay the screen with the message if a check fails, and otherwise look up the card and show its details.AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-043business ruleWhen the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3 or PF15 on the card detail screen, the system shall show no error and treat the key as Enter, checking the input again and repeating the search.AC-17, AC-18
REQ-F-044business ruleWhen a card lookup is made, the system shall read the card master (CARDDAT) by the 16-digit card number only, and shall not check that the card belongs to the account entered.AC-19
REQ-F-045formattingWhen the card is found, the system shall show ' Displaying requested details' with the card's embossed name, expiry month, expiry year and active status.AC-20
REQ-F-046business ruleIf no card exists with the requested card number, then the system shall reject the search, show both the account and the card number in red, and show 'Did not find cards for this search condition'.AC-21
REQ-F-047error handlingIf reading the card master fails for any reason other than not found, then the system shall reject the search, show the account in red and show 'File Error: READ on CARDDAT returned RESP <code>,RESP2 <code>'.AC-33
REQ-F-048formattingWhen the card detail screen is shown and no information message has been set, the system shall show the information message 'Please enter Account and Card Number'.AC-22, AC-23
REQ-F-049formattingThe system shall show the current error message (if any) on the error line and the information message on the information line of the card detail screen.AC-24
REQ-F-050formattingWhen the card detail screen is shown with session details, the system shall show the saved account number and card number, leaving a field empty when its saved value is zero.AC-25, AC-26
REQ-F-051formattingWhen the card detail screen was reached from the card list (last screen COCRDLI, caller COCRDLIC), the system shall show the account and card fields as protected (not editable) in the default colour, and otherwise shall leave them editable.AC-27, AC-28
REQ-F-052formattingIf a search field fails its check, then the system shall show that field in red, and show '*' in red in a field left blank on resubmission, even if the fields are protected.AC-29, AC-30
REQ-F-053formattingThe system shall place the cursor on the account field when it is invalid or blank, otherwise on the card field when that is invalid or blank, and otherwise on the account field.AC-31, AC-32

Open questions

  • SME-103 On the card search screen, the error messages say the account number must be 11 digits and the card number 16 digits, but the rules only check that each is numeric. Should the new system require exactly 11 digits for the account number and 16 for the card number? (Business analyst)
  • SME-104 The card search finds the card by card number only and does not use the account number entered. Should the new system check that the card found belongs to the account entered? (Business analyst)
  • SME-105 On the card search screen, when both the account and card number are blank, should the message 'No input received' replace an earlier message such as 'Account number not provided', or should the first message stay? (Business analyst)
  • SME-106 When a card is found, should the operator see the message 'Displaying requested details'? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-020 Is this intended? The entered account is never compared with the card's account: the line that would use the account as part of the key is commented out, so any account (that is a valid number) plus an existing card number shows that card, despite the paragraph name and the message 'Did not find cards for this search condition'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-076 Is this intended? Clearing the whole shared context on entry from the main menu also erases the signed-on user's ID and user type, so PF3 then returns to the menu with a blank user ID and the user type forced to regular user. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-120 Is this intended? The info line is meant to be shown dark when there is no information message, but that branch can never run because the prompt has already been filled in by that point. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-122 Is this intended? An invalid (non-numeric) account or card entry is cleared from the screen because the saved value is reset to zero, so the user cannot see what they typed. On resubmission a blank field shows '*' instead. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

5. Enter and leave the card detail screendraft · online · 6 requirements · 7 rules · 8 criteria · 3 screens

Controls how users arrive at and leave the card detail screen: from the menu it opens an empty search, and from the card list it opens straight on the selected card. Leaving with PF3 returns the user to the screen they came from, or to the main menu. It must never carry stale card selections from an earlier session into a fresh entry.

As a card operations user, I want the card detail screen to open with the right card or an empty search and to return me to where I came from, so that I can move between the menu, the card list and card details without losing my place.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-054design noteWhen the card detail program (transaction CCDL) starts with no session context, or is entered from the main menu (COMEN01C) other than as a re-entry, the system shall clear the whole shared session context before going on.AC-01
REQ-F-055formattingWhen the card detail program is entered for the first time from any program other than the card list (COCRDLIC), or started with no session details, and PF3 was not pressed, the system shall show an empty search screen with 'Please enter Account and Card Number' and wait for the user's input.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-056business ruleWhen the card detail program is entered for the first time from the card list (COCRDLIC) and PF3 was not pressed, the system shall use the account and card number passed by the list as already valid, without checking them again, then look up the card and show its details.AC-04
REQ-N-001design noteThe system shall mark every card detail screen it sends as awaiting re-entry and return under transaction CCDL, so that the user's next action is treated as a re-entry.AC-05
REQ-F-057business ruleWhen the user presses PF3 (or PF15) on the card detail screen, the system shall transfer control to the program and transaction that called it (for example the card list COCRDLIC with transaction CCLI), or to the main menu COMEN01C with transaction CM00 when no caller is recorded.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-058design noteWhen control leaves the card detail screen on PF3, the system shall pass the shared session details showing COCRDSLC / CCDL as the sender, the user type as regular user ('U'), the last screen as COCRDSL / CCRDSLA, and the next program's entry as a first entry.AC-08

Open questions

  • SME-103 On the card search screen, the error messages say the account number must be 11 digits and the card number 16 digits, but the rules only check that each is numeric. Should the new system require exactly 11 digits for the account number and 16 for the card number? (Business analyst)
  • SME-104 The card search finds the card by card number only and does not use the account number entered. Should the new system check that the card found belongs to the account entered? (Business analyst)
  • SME-105 On the card search screen, when both the account and card number are blank, should the message 'No input received' replace an earlier message such as 'Account number not provided', or should the first message stay? (Business analyst)
  • SME-106 When a card is found, should the operator see the message 'Displaying requested details'? (Business analyst)
  • SME-107 When a user leaves the card detail screen, the system always resets their user type to regular user, even for an administrator. Is this intended, or should the user keep their type (admin or regular)? (Security and access-control owner)
  • DEF-076 Is this intended? Clearing the whole shared context on entry from the main menu also erases the signed-on user's ID and user type, so PF3 then returns to the menu with a blank user ID and the user type forced to regular user. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-077 Confirm this is deliberate: On PF3 the user type is always set to regular user ('U'), even if the session belonged to an administrator. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-122 Is this intended? An invalid (non-numeric) account or card entry is cleared from the screen because the saved value is reset to zero, so the user cannot see what they typed. On resubmission a blank field shows '*' instead. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the card detail screen is opened with no session state, or opened fresh from the main menu, the user's navigation and selection state (selected account and card, previous screen) is cleared before anything else happens. Card detail screen entry routing and context reset
  • The card detail screen is a stateful form: every response must keep the session state so that the user's next submit is handled as a continuation of the same screen, not a new entry. In a web app this is a normal form post back to the same route, with the session state held on the server. Card detail screen entry routing and context reset
  • On exit the shared navigation state handed to the next screen records card detail as the screen that sent the user, the user type as regular user ('U'), and that the destination should treat this as a first entry, so it starts clean and does not re-process this screen's input. Exit to the destination program
6. Detect unchanged card details on updatedraft · online · 2 requirements · 1 rules · 3 criteria · 2 screens

Spots when an operator submits the card update screen without really changing anything (differences in upper or lower case do not count) and tells them nothing changed instead of running the field checks. It must never ask for confirmation or save when nothing has changed.

As a card operations user, I want the card update to recognise when I have not changed anything, so that no needless edits are run and I am told nothing changed.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#6

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-059business ruleWhen the edited card data equals the fetched data ignoring case, the system shall set the no-change message, mark all detail fields valid and skip detailed edits.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-060business ruleWhile the update stage is validated ('N') or committed ('C'), the system shall mark all detail fields valid and skip detailed edits.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03

Business rules

RuleClassText, worked examples and evidence
Detect unchanged card details
rec/agreed:CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate/id-814f66b7d5/1		business rule
validation, medium		WHEN the edited card data equals the fetched data ignoring case, or the stage is validated ('N') or committed ('C'), THE Card Update Input Validation SHALL set the no-change message when the data is unchanged, mark all detail fields valid and skip detailed edits
  • Fetched embossed name: JOHN SMITH; Entered embossed name: john smith; Status, expiry month and year: unchanged → The change is treated as no change: message 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' is set, all detail fields are marked valid and the name, status and expiry edits are skipped.
  • Update stage: 'N' (changes validated, awaiting confirmation); Entered details: differ from fetched → All detail fields are marked valid and the detailed field edits are not run again.
  • Fetched card status: Y; Entered card status: N; Update stage: not 'N' or 'C' → A change is detected, so the name, status and expiry edits run.

7. Find and show a card for updatedraft · online · 17 requirements · 24 rules · 34 criteria · 3 screens · 3 gaps

Lets card operations staff find a card for update, either by entering an account and card number or by arriving with a card picked in the card list, and shows its stored embossed name, status and expiry. The values read at this point are kept as the card's original details, which later saves are checked against. It must reject missing or invalid keys with the exact messages and must report a card that is not found or a card file that cannot be read.

As a card operations user, I want to enter an account number and card number, or arrive with a card selected from the card list, and see that card's stored details, so that I can review the card before changing it.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#7

Open questions

  • SME-108 When a card record cannot be locked for update, the message is given as 'Could not lock record (CARDDAT) for update' in one place and 'Could not lock record for update' in another. Which text is correct, and does the outcome shown to the operator depend on the exact wording? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-109 When updating a card, where should the expiry day come from? The screen shows the original day as not changeable, yet the saved day is taken from a hidden screen field without checks. Should the saved day be the original stored day, be recalculated (for example, the last day of the month), or be the entered value? And should the new expiry date have to be in the future, or no earlier than the current expiry? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-110 When a card is updated, the saved CVV comes from an 'updated CVV' value that no rule captures or checks. Should the saved CVV always be the original stored CVV? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-111 After the operator confirms a card update, if a file error or other message is already pending, the result is reported as 'changes saved'. Is that intended? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-112 When the card update screen reaches a state it does not recognise, the old system records error code '0001' with 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. Should the new system keep this, and what should the operator see? (Business analyst / card operations)
  • SME-113 On the card update screen, entering '*' or leaving a field blank counts as 'not supplied', and the card name, status, expiry month and expiry year are then flagged as errors. Should '*' mean 'keep the existing value', or are all four fields required? (Card operations product owner)
  • SME-114 Should the new system check the expiry day entered on a card update, and if so, what range is allowed? (Card operations product owner)
  • SME-115 When checking for changes, a change only in upper or lower case in the card name is reported as 'No change detected'. Should a case-only change to the name be rejected as no change? (Card operations product owner)
  • DEF-059 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch for a completed save ('C'), which would return to details shown and clear the keys, and a catch-all that abends with '0001' 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. Neither can run: the main dispatch handles 'C', 'L' and 'F' itself before the decision step is reached. Also, once changes are validated ('N'), further edits are not re-validated before PF5 saves them. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-123 Is this intended? The stage is set to details shown even when the card read fails (not found or file error), so the screen says 'Details of selected card shown above' with empty details next to the error message. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-125 Is this intended? The lookup ignores the account number (its key move is commented out), so a card is fetched and can be updated even when the account entered does not own it. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The account number input treats '*' or blank as 'not supplied'. Any other value is used both as the account to search on and as the account carried forward with the edit. The new form should keep the two meanings separate in its model, even though one field fills both. Interpret account number entry
  • The card number input treats '*' or blank as 'not supplied'. Any other value is used both as the lookup key (a keyed lookup of the card by card number) and as the card number carried forward with the edit. Interpret card number entry
  • When the card is found, the server keeps a snapshot of the original values for the length of the edit: the embossed name in upper case, the expiry year, month and day split from the stored date (YYYY-MM-DD), the active status and the CVV code. This snapshot is the baseline for the 'no change' check and for spotting that someone else changed the card before the save (optimistic concurrency), so it must be held on the server and not trusted from the browser. Load original card details for display
8. Edit and validate card detailsdraft · online · 15 requirements · 22 rules · 33 criteria · 2 screens · 2 gaps

Lets card operations staff change a card's embossed name, active status and expiry month and year, and checks each change before it can be saved. The name may hold only letters and spaces, the status must be Y or N, the month must be 1-12 and the year 1950-2099. It must never put forward invalid details for saving, and it shows only the first failing check's message.

As a card operations user, I want to change a card's embossed name, active status and expiry date and have my changes checked, so that only valid card details are put forward for saving.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#8

REQ-F-078design noteWhen the operator submits the card update screen with the embossed name, active status, expiry month or expiry year entered as '*' or left blank, the system shall treat that value as not supplied, and otherwise shall take the entry as the new value.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03, AC-04, AC-05, AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-079design noteThe system shall always take the expiry day exactly as returned by the screen, without the '*' or blank check, as the new expiry day written back to the card record.AC-08
REQ-F-080business ruleWhen the entered card details equal the fetched details ignoring upper/lower case, the system shall skip the field checks, report 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' and leave the details shown (state 'S') without asking for confirmation.AC-09, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12
REQ-F-081business ruleWhen card details are shown and the operator submits name, status or expiry values that differ (ignoring upper/lower case) from the stored ones, the system shall run the name, status, expiry month and expiry year checks.AC-13

REQ-F-084business ruleIf the entered details differ from those fetched and the card active status is not supplied, is '0', or is anything other than uppercase 'Y' or 'N', then the system shall reject the input with 'Card Active Status must be Y or N', unless an earlier field already set a message.AC-18, AC-19, AC-20, AC-21

REQ-F-086business ruleIf the changed expiry year is missing, '*', blank or zeros, or is not between 1950 and 2099, then the system shall reject the change with 'Invalid card expiry year' and show the year in red.AC-25, AC-26, AC-27

  • expiry month: (blank); expiry year: 2027 → Month is treated as not supplied; year 2027 is taken.

Detect unchanged card data
rec/agreed:CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate/id-c89ab9678d/1		business rule
validation, medium		WHEN the new card data equals the fetched data ignoring case, or the state is awaiting confirmation ('N') or done ('C'), THE Card Update Change Detection SHALL report 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' when the data is unchanged, and stop further field editing
  • Entered card details: identical to fetched details → The screen reports 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' and no further field editing is done.
  • Fetched expiry month: 05; Entered expiry month: 05; Entered embossed name: same as fetched but in lower case → Case is ignored, so 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' is reported.
  • Fetched expiry year: 2027; Entered expiry year: 2028; Update stage: not 'N' or 'C' → A change is detected; no no-change message, and the field edits continue.
app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl:680-683,685-687,692-693, app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl:679-693
Card active status must be Y or N
rec/group:claude/RULE-106/4		business rule
validation, high		WHEN the entered card details match the fetched ones apart from upper/lower case, THE card update screen SHALL skip the status check and report 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.'.
  • Fetched status: Y; Card active status entered: y; Other fields: unchanged → Message 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.'; no status error

business, high		WHEN card details are shown and the submitted values are the same as the stored ones (ignoring case), THE card update program SHALL leave the details shown (state 'S') without asking for confirmation.

validation, high		WHEN card details are shown and the operator submits name, status or expiry values that differ (ignoring upper/lower case) from the stored ones, THE card update program SHALL run the name, status, expiry month and expiry year checks and, if any fails, keep the screen in the changes-with-errors state ('E') with 'Update card details presented above.'.
  • Card status: X → State 'E'; status error shown with 'Update card details presented above.'

validation, high		WHEN card details have been fetched and the user changes them, and the card name is missing, '*', blank or zeros, THE card update screen SHALL reject the change with 'Card name not provided' and show '*' in the name field in red.
  • Card name: (blank) → Error 'Card name not provided'; the name field shows '*'

rec/group:claude/RULE-105/3		business rule

validation, high		WHEN card details are shown, the entered details differ from those fetched, and the card active status is not supplied or is '0', THE card update screen SHALL reject the input with 'Card Active Status must be Y or N', unless an earlier field already set a message.
  • Card active status entered: 0; Embossed name: unchanged but valid; Expiry month: changed → Message 'Card Active Status must be Y or N'

rec/group:claude/RULE-106/3		business rule
validation, high		WHEN card details are shown, the entered details differ from those fetched, and the card active status is anything other than uppercase 'Y' or 'N', THE card update screen SHALL reject the input with 'Card Active Status must be Y or N' (unless an earlier message is already set), and otherwise SHALL accept the status.

yesvalid'Y' or 'N'missing, blank, zeros or not 1-12-'Card expiry month must be between 1 and 12'; month in red; state 'E'rec/group:claude/RULE-107/2
yesvalid'Y' or 'N'1-12missing, blank, zeros or not 1950-2099'Invalid card expiry year'; year in red; state 'E'rec/group:claude/RULE-107/3
yesvalid'Y' or 'N'1-121950-2099'Changes validated.Press F5 to save'; state 'N'rec/group:claude/RULE-137/5
no (differs only in case)-lowercase 'y' or 'n'--Gap: A status changed only in case is treated as no change (R41), while a lowercase status alongside another change is rejected (R40); confirm this is intended.
differs only in expiry day----Gap: The expiry day is taken as returned by the screen without checks (R10, R20) and is not named in the change comparison (R53); confirm whether a day-only change is detected and validated.

Open questions

  • SME-108 When a card record cannot be locked for update, the message is given as 'Could not lock record (CARDDAT) for update' in one place and 'Could not lock record for update' in another. Which text is correct, and does the outcome shown to the operator depend on the exact wording? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-109 When updating a card, where should the expiry day come from? The screen shows the original day as not changeable, yet the saved day is taken from a hidden screen field without checks. Should the saved day be the original stored day, be recalculated (for example, the last day of the month), or be the entered value? And should the new expiry date have to be in the future, or no earlier than the current expiry? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-110 When a card is updated, the saved CVV comes from an 'updated CVV' value that no rule captures or checks. Should the saved CVV always be the original stored CVV? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-111 After the operator confirms a card update, if a file error or other message is already pending, the result is reported as 'changes saved'. Is that intended? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-112 When the card update screen reaches a state it does not recognise, the old system records error code '0001' with 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. Should the new system keep this, and what should the operator see? (Business analyst / card operations)
  • SME-113 On the card update screen, entering '*' or leaving a field blank counts as 'not supplied', and the card name, status, expiry month and expiry year are then flagged as errors. Should '*' mean 'keep the existing value', or are all four fields required? (Card operations product owner)
  • SME-114 Should the new system check the expiry day entered on a card update, and if so, what range is allowed? (Card operations product owner)
  • SME-115 When checking for changes, a change only in upper or lower case in the card name is reported as 'No change detected'. Should a case-only change to the name be rejected as no change? (Card operations product owner)
  • DEF-059 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch for a completed save ('C'), which would return to details shown and clear the keys, and a catch-all that abends with '0001' 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. Neither can run: the main dispatch handles 'C', 'L' and 'F' itself before the decision step is reached. Also, once changes are validated ('N'), further edits are not re-validated before PF5 saves them. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-126 Is this intended? The expiry day is never checked against the new month and year, so a change such as moving to a shorter month can save an impossible date (for example 2027-06-31). (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the edit form is submitted, an embossed name, active status, expiry month or expiry year entered as '*' or left blank counts as 'not supplied', and any other entry is the proposed new value. Map this once in the form-to-model step so the checks only see a value or 'not supplied'. Interpret placeholder entries as not supplied
  • An embossed name entered as '*' or left blank is read as 'not supplied'. Any other text is the proposed new name, which the name check then validates. Interpret embossed name entry
  • An active status entered as '*' or left blank is read as 'not supplied', so the status check reports it as missing rather than as an invalid value. Interpret card active status entry
  • An expiry month or expiry year entered as '*' or left blank is read as 'not supplied'. Any other entry is the proposed new value, which the month and year range checks then validate. Interpret expiry month entry
  • The expiry day is not editable and is not given the '*' or blank treatment. The new application should carry the original expiry day through unchanged instead of reading it back from the form. Interpret placeholder entries as not supplied
  • The expiry day saved with the card is the day held for the edit, unchanged, joined with the new year and month. Take it from the server-side original snapshot, not from a hidden form field, so it cannot be altered. Stage expiry day as entered
9. Confirm and save card changesdraft · online · 7 requirements · 11 rules · 14 criteria · 2 screens

Saves validated card changes only after the operator confirms them with PF5, and lets them drop unsaved edits with PF12. Before writing, it locks the card and checks it still matches what was fetched. It must never overwrite a card that someone else changed in the meantime, and must never save without confirmation.

As a card operations user, I want to confirm validated changes with PF5 and have them saved safely, so that the card record is updated only with my confirmed changes and not over someone else's changes.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#9

10. Leave or restart card updatedraft · online · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 5 criteria · 2 screens

Takes the operator out of card update, back to the card list or the main menu, or starts a fresh search after a save has completed or failed. It must never carry the previously selected account and card into the next screen or the next search.

As a card operations user, I want to leave card update back to where I came from, or start a new search after a save, so that I can continue my work without stale card selections.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CreditCardListDetailViewandUpdate#10

Requirements

REQ-F-100business ruleWhen the operator presses PF3, or entered from the card list and the update has completed or failed and they press any key, the system shall commit its work and transfer control to the program and transaction that called it, or to the main menu (COMEN01C, transaction CM00) when no caller is recorded.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-101design noteWhen the card update program exits and the operator had come from the card list, the system shall clear the selected account and card numbers before returning.AC-03
REQ-F-102design noteWhen the card update program exits, the system shall record itself (COCRDUPC, transaction CCUP) as the calling program, mark the session user type as a regular user and flag the next program as a fresh entry.AC-04
REQ-F-103business ruleWhen a save has completed ('C') or failed ('L' or 'F') and the operator did not come from the card list, the system shall on the next interaction clear the update state and the account and card keys and show an empty search screen with 'Please enter Account and Card Number'.AC-05

Decision tables

Open questions

  • SME-108 When a card record cannot be locked for update, the message is given as 'Could not lock record (CARDDAT) for update' in one place and 'Could not lock record for update' in another. Which text is correct, and does the outcome shown to the operator depend on the exact wording? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-109 When updating a card, where should the expiry day come from? The screen shows the original day as not changeable, yet the saved day is taken from a hidden screen field without checks. Should the saved day be the original stored day, be recalculated (for example, the last day of the month), or be the entered value? And should the new expiry date have to be in the future, or no earlier than the current expiry? (Card operations subject-matter expert)
  • SME-110 When a card is updated, the saved CVV comes from an 'updated CVV' value that no rule captures or checks. Should the saved CVV always be the original stored CVV? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-111 After the operator confirms a card update, if a file error or other message is already pending, the result is reported as 'changes saved'. Is that intended? (Card operations business analyst)
  • SME-116 When a user leaves the card update screen, the system always resets their user type to regular user. Is this intended, or should the signed-on user keep their type? (Security and access-control owner)
  • DEF-059 Is this intended? The decision step has a branch for a completed save ('C'), which would return to details shown and clear the keys, and a catch-all that abends with '0001' 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'. Neither can run: the main dispatch handles 'C', 'L' and 'F' itself before the decision step is reached. Also, once changes are validated ('N'), further edits are not re-validated before PF5 saves them. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-183 Is this intended? On exit the program always sets the session user type to regular user ('U') whatever the signed-on user's type, so an admin passing through would be treated as a regular user by the menu, which uses that flag to block admin-only options. The same line appears in every card program, so it looks like copied boilerplate. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When leaving card update to go back to the card list, the selected account and card numbers are cleared from the shared navigation state, so the list does not reopen on, or reselect, the card just edited. Exit routing back to caller or main menu
  • On exit the shared navigation state records card update as the screen that sent the user, sets the user type to regular user, and tells the destination to treat this as a first entry, so it starts clean. Exit routing back to caller or main menu
11. Save card changesdraft · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria · 2 screens

Writes the confirmed embossed name, active status and expiry date to the card record, keeping its card number and account, and tells the operator whether the save worked. It must never change the card number or account, and must never report success when the write failed.

As a card operations user, I want my changes to a card's embossed name, active status and expiry date saved to the card record, so that the card holds the updated details and I know whether the save worked.

Customer Profile Branch Migration

1. Export complete customer profiles for branch migrationdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 8 rules · 10 criteria

Produces one combined branch migration file holding every customer, account, card cross-reference, transaction and card, for the operator moving complete customer profiles to a branch. Records go out in a fixed order (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards), each numbered by one running sequence and stamped with branch '0001', region 'NORTH' and a single run timestamp. It must never filter, skip or reorder records: inactive accounts and expired or inactive cards are exported as they are.

As a branch migration operator, I want every customer, account, card cross-reference, transaction and card exported into one combined migration file, so that complete customer profiles can be moved to a branch.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#1

Decision tables

None.

Open questions

  • SME-018 Does the first record in the data export get sequence number 1? (Migration team)
  • SME-019 Every exported record is stamped with branch 0001 and region NORTH. Is that right for all customers, or should branch and region come from customer or account data, or from a run setting? (Data migration lead)
  • SME-020 When the export is rerun, should it replace or add to the previous export contents, and how should a run that ended abnormally be recovered? (Batch operations)
  • SME-021 Customer SSNs and card verification codes are copied into the export unmasked. Must the new export protect or leave out these values? (Security team)
  • SME-022 If the export cannot open one of its files, should the run end abnormally? (Batch operations)
  • DEF-082 Is this intended? The job defines the export file's key at offset 28 (KEYS(4 28)), but in the record layout the 4-byte binary sequence number starts at offset 27, after the 1-byte type and the 26-byte timestamp. The program's key and the file's key do not line up, which could make the open fail (status 39) or key the records on the wrong bytes. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-088 Confirm this is deliberate: The card's CVV code and the customer's SSN and government ID go into the migration file unmasked. Storing a CVV after authorisation is not allowed under PCI DSS. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A scheduled batch job that starts from an empty migration file every run (replace, never append), keyed by sequence number with room for a 500-character record, then runs the export with no parameters against the shared customer, account, cross-reference, transaction and card data, writing its messages to the job log. Produce the card-management data export
  • One run: take the timestamp, open all five sources and the target, then stream each source in its key order — customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards — one after another; a sorted extract per source in key order, never interleaved. Sequence the full portfolio export run
  • A one-to-one mapping from each source record to an export record tagged with its type code ('C', 'A', 'X', 'T', 'D') and carrying that record's fields; the migration file is a tagged union of the five record layouts. Export each customer as type C record
  • A single counter starting at 1, incremented for each record written across all types in output order, used as the unique key of the migration file; the last value equals the total written. Global export sequence number across all record types
  • Format the run timestamp from the system clock as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.00', with the fraction fixed at '00' rather than real hundredths. Build the export run timestamp
  • Capture the timestamp once at run start and reuse that value on every record; do not read the clock per record. Export each customer as type C record
2. Carry sensitive customer and card data in the exportdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 4 criteria

The migration file carries customers' identity data and cards' security data in full so the target branch receives complete records: SSN, government ID, date of birth, EFT account and FICO score on customer records, and the full 16-digit card number and 3-digit CVV on card records. These values are copied unmasked, so the file holds highly sensitive data and the team must protect it accordingly. The values must never be truncated, masked or altered on the way out.

As a branch migration operator, I want the export to carry the customer's identity data and the card's security data, so that the target branch receives complete customer and card records.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, personal_data, security. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#2

  • DEF-173 Confirm this is deliberate: The migration export file holds full SSNs and card CVV codes in clear. Storing a CVV after authorization goes against PCI DSS, and the SSN is unprotected personal data. The field-by-field copy shows the full values were meant to be exported, but nothing shows the security risk was considered. (Subject-matter expert)

3. Report export reconciliation countsdraft · service · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Reports how many customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions and cards were exported, and the total, so the operator can reconcile the migration file against the source data. Each type's count is shown when that type finishes, and the full set is shown when the export completes. The total must always equal the last sequence number written.

As a branch migration operator, I want the export to report how many records of each type it exported and in total, so that I can reconcile the migration file against the source files.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#3

4. Stop the export on any file errordraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 6 criteria · 1 gap

Stops the export at once on any open, read or write failure, so the operator never mistakes a failed export for a complete one. It shows which file failed and its status, then 'CBEXPORT: ABENDING PROGRAM', and ends abnormally without retrying or skipping records. A failed run must never report success, and it leaves only the records already written in a partial file.

As a branch migration operator, I want the export to stop at once on any file open, read or write error, so that a failed export is never mistaken for a complete one.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-010error handlingIf opening any source file or the export file returns a status other than '00', then the system shall display 'ERROR: Cannot open <file>, Status: ' with the status and 'CBEXPORT: ABENDING PROGRAM', and abend before any record is written.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-011error handlingIf reading any source file returns a status other than '00' or '10' (end of file), or writing an export record returns a status other than '00', then the system shall display 'ERROR: Reading <file>, Status: ' or 'ERROR: Writing export record, Status: ' with the status, then 'CBEXPORT: ABENDING PROGRAM', and abend.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-012error handlingIf a read or a write fails during the export, then the system shall abend at once, without retrying or skipping the record, leaving the records already written in the partial export file.AC-06

5. Import and split the migration file into target filesdraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 9 rules · 13 criteria

Reads the combined migration file in sequence-number order and splits it back into separate customer, account, card cross-reference, transaction and card files for the target branch. Each record is routed by its type code and copied field for field, with no business validation. It must never drop, change or reject a record of a known type: the target data must match what was exported exactly.

As a branch migration operator, I want the combined migration file split back into separate customer, account, cross-reference, transaction and card files, so that the target branch receives normalized master data.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-013design noteThe system shall run the import program against the shared export file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.EXPORT.DATA) and create new cataloged customer (500-byte), account (300-byte), card cross-reference (50-byte) and transaction (350-byte) import files plus a 132-byte import error file.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-014design noteThe system shall not allocate a card import file in the import job, although the import program writes card records ('D') to one.AC-03

Open questions

  • SME-023 Imported card records go to a separate card output that is not listed among the import job's outputs. Where should imported card records be stored, and are they deleted on failure like the other import files? (Migration architecture team)
  • SME-024 After an export record with an unknown type is logged as an error, should the import carry on with the next record or stop? (Migration business analyst)
  • SME-025 If the import cannot write an entry to its error file, should the run stop? (Migration business analyst)
  • SME-026 Should the migration import apply the same checks as online maintenance (valid account status, balance within credit limit, FICO 300-850, valid dates, existing account and customer for cross-references and cards), or can the export be trusted as already valid? (Business analyst)
  • SME-027 How important is the rule that sends each import record to its target master file by record type (customer, account, cross-reference, transaction, card; anything else to the error log)? Is it core to the system, or a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Data migration lead)
  • DEF-033 Is this intended? The program header promises validation and checksum checks, but the validation step only displays 'No validation errors detected' and no data is checked. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-071 Is this intended? CEE3ABD is called with no abend code or timing arguments, so the abend code that results is not defined by the program. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-089 Is this intended? The job (CBIMPORT.jcl) has no CARDOUT DD, so opening the card output is likely to fail and abend the run before any record is read; if the runtime allocates it dynamically, the card records go to a temporary file that is not kept. Also, a failed error-file write is still counted as written, and the 9-digit export sequence number is cut to 7 digits in the error record. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-127 Is this intended? The job has no CARDOUT DD for the card output file the program opens and writes, so card records are not saved and the open may abend the run. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A scheduled import job that reads the shared migration file and creates fresh customer (500-character), account (300), cross-reference (50) and transaction (350) target files plus a 132-character error report; the outputs are kept only if the step succeeds and are removed if it fails. Split export into normalized import files
  • The legacy job sets up no card target although the program writes card records to one; the new job must provide a card target explicitly (a known gap to confirm, not behaviour to copy). Split export into normalized import files
  • Map an 'A' record field for field to an account record (number, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open/expiration/reissue dates, current-cycle credit and debit, zip, group id) and write it to the account target; any write failure stops the run. Map and write imported account record
  • Map an 'X' record to a cross-reference row linking card number, customer number and account number, and write it to the cross-reference target; any write failure stops the run. Write card cross-reference record
  • Map a 'T' record field for field to a transaction record and write it to the transaction target; any write failure stops the run. Write imported transaction record
6. Log unknown record types during importdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 3 rules · 4 criteria

Logs every migration record whose type is not 'C', 'A', 'X', 'T' or 'D' to an error report so the operator can see which records were not imported. Each entry holds the timestamp, the record type, the export sequence number and 'Unknown record type encountered', separated by '|'. An unknown record must never be imported into any target file, and a failure to write the error entry does not stop the import.

As a branch migration operator, I want export records of an unknown type logged to an error report, so that I can see which records were not imported.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#6

REQ-F-023error handlingIf the error record cannot be written, then the system shall display 'ERROR: Writing error record, Status: ' with the file status and carry on importing, still counting the error as written.AC-04

7. Report import run statisticsdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 3 rules · 5 criteria

Reports at the end of an import how many records were read, how many customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions and cards were imported, and how many error records and unknown types were found, so the operator can reconcile the targets. The legacy import then always prints 'CBIMPORT: Import validation completed' and 'CBIMPORT: No validation errors detected' without checking anything. That message must not be read as proof of reconciliation; the counts are the only real check.

As a branch migration operator, I want the import to report how many records it read, imported and rejected, so that I can reconcile the target files against the migration file.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#7

REQ-F-024side effectWhen the import completes without abending, the system shall close all files and display 'CBIMPORT: Import completed' followed by the counts of records read, customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions and cards imported, error records written and unknown record types.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-025historical artifactWhen the import has processed every record in the export file, the system shall always display 'CBIMPORT: Import validation completed' and 'CBIMPORT: No validation errors detected' without performing any checksum, record-count reconciliation or cross-file check, even when error records were written.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05

8. Abort the import on any file failuredraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 10 rules · 10 criteria · 1 gap

Stops the import on any failure to open, read or write a file, and discards the new target files so no partial migration is kept. It shows which file failed and its status, then ends abnormally without closing files or printing run statistics. A failed import must never leave behind target files that look complete.

As a branch migration operator, I want the import to stop and discard its target files on any file open, read or write failure, so that no partial migration is kept.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/CustomerProfileBranchMigration#8

REQ-F-027error handlingIf reading the export file returns any status other than success or end of file, then the system shall display 'ERROR: Reading EXPORT-INPUT, Status: ' with the status and abend the run.AC-09, AC-10

REQ-F-029error handlingWhen the import step ends abnormally, the system shall delete the new customer, account, cross-reference, transaction and error import files, so records written before the failure are not kept.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06
