  • SME-026 Should the migration import apply the same checks as online maintenance (valid account status, balance within credit limit, FICO 300-850, valid dates, existing account and customer for cross-references and cards), or can the export be trusted as already valid? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-033 Is this intended? The program header promises validation and checksum checks, but the validation step only displays 'No validation errors detected' and no data is checked. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-071 Is this intended? CEE3ABD is called with no abend code or timing arguments, so the abend code that results is not defined by the program. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-089 Is this intended? The job (CBIMPORT.jcl) has no CARDOUT DD, so opening the card output is likely to fail and abend the run before any record is read; if the runtime allocates it dynamically, the card records go to a temporary file that is not kept. Also, a failed error-file write is still counted as written, and the 9-digit export sequence number is cut to 7 digits in the error record. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-127 Is this intended? The job has no CARDOUT DD for the card output file the program opens and writes, so card records are not saved and the open may abend the run. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The account write must report failure to the job, so that a failed write stops the whole import rather than being skipped. Map and write imported account record
  • The cross-reference write must report failure to the job, so that a failed write stops the whole import. Write card cross-reference record
  • The transaction write must report failure to the job, so that a failed write stops the whole import. Write imported transaction record
  • Make the import all-or-nothing: write the targets to staging (or inside a transaction) and publish them only when the step succeeds; on an abnormal end, remove the customer, account, cross-reference, transaction and error outputs. Split export into normalized import files

Master Data File Initialization

1. Load account masterdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Rebuilds the account master from the account flat file so that the operations team starts CardDemo processing from a fresh, complete set of accounts. Each run throws away the previous account store, creates an empty one keyed on the 11-digit account ID, and loads every account record from the file. It must never lose or skip a record, keep stale accounts from before the run, or fail just because no account store existed yet.

As a CardDemo operations team member, I want to rebuild the account master from the account flat file, so that all CardDemo processing starts from a fresh, complete set of account records.

Transaction Type Reference Data Maintenance

1. Batch maintenance of transaction typesdraft · scheduled job · 12 requirements · 13 rules · 16 criteria · 1 gap

A scheduled batch job lets reference data administrators add, update and delete transaction types from an input file, one action per record ('A', 'U', 'D', or '*' for a comment). It must never let one bad record stop the run or go unnoticed: each rejected record leaves the table unchanged, is reported with its message, and makes the job end with return code 4 instead of 0. It must never delete a transaction type that still has categories referring to it.

As a reference data administrator, I want to add, update and delete transaction types from a batch input file, so that the transaction type table used to classify credit card transactions stays current.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001business ruleThe system shall read each batch input record as a one-character action code (column 1), a two-character transaction type code (columns 2-3) and a 50-character description (columns 4-53), and shall apply 'A' as add, 'U' as update and 'D' as delete.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-002business ruleWhen an input record's action code is '*', the system shall treat the line as a comment, show 'IGNORING COMMENTED LINE' and change nothing.AC-03
REQ-F-003business ruleIf an input record's action code is anything other than 'A', 'U', 'D' or '*', then the system shall show 'ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID', set the job return code to 4, leave the table unchanged and continue with the next record.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-004business ruleWhen an input record has action 'A', the system shall add a transaction type with the record's two-character code and its description, and show 'RECORD INSERTED SUCCESSFULLY' when the database accepts it.AC-11
REQ-F-005error handlingIf the database rejects an add (for example because the type code already exists, DB2 code -803), then the system shall show 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:' with the database code, set the job return code to 4 and continue with the next record.AC-12
REQ-F-006business ruleWhen an input record has action 'U' and the transaction type code exists, the system shall replace that type's description with the record's description and show 'RECORD UPDATED SUCCESSFULLY'.AC-13
REQ-F-007error handlingIf an update or a delete names a transaction type code that does not exist, then the system shall show 'No records found.', set the job return code to 4 and continue with the next record.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-008error handlingIf the database returns an error on an update, then the system shall show 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:' with the database code, set the job return code to 4 and continue with the next record.AC-14
REQ-F-009business ruleWhen an input record has action 'D' and the transaction type exists with no categories referring to it, the system shall delete the type and show 'RECORD DELETED SUCCESSFULLY'.AC-08
REQ-F-010error handlingIf a delete names a transaction type that still has transaction type categories, then the system shall refuse the delete, show 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:' with the database code, set the job return code to 4 and continue.AC-15
REQ-F-011error handlingWhen any input record is rejected (invalid action code, type not found, or database error), the system shall keep processing the remaining records and end the job with return code 4, and otherwise shall end the job with return code 0.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-N-001formattingThe system shall show 'PROCESSING' followed by the input record for each record it reads, and 'OPEN FILE OK' or 'OPEN FILE NOT OK' when it opens the input file.AC-16

Open questions

  • SME-090 In the transaction type maintenance batch, should comment records (type '*') be skipped without changing the transaction type table? (Business analyst)
  • SME-091 In the transaction type maintenance batch, what should be logged or confirmed when a new transaction type is added successfully? (Business analyst)
  • SME-092 The transaction type maintenance job is tied to database subsystem DAZ1 and application plan CARDDEMO. Should the new system keep these bindings, or treat them as deployment settings? (Platform team)
  • SME-093 When a request in the transaction type maintenance batch is rejected or the job ends abnormally, should the batch carry on and flag the problem (return code 4, earlier changes kept), or stop and roll back the whole batch? Which return code should each outcome give? (Batch operations lead)
  • SME-094 Please confirm the priority of the batch rule for adding a new transaction type. Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that would be costly if it were wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • SME-095 Should a transaction type also be protected from deletion while posted transactions still use it? Or is 'no transaction categories refer to it' the only check intended? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-168 Is this intended? If the input file fails to open, the program only shows 'OPEN FILE NOT OK' and carries on into the read loop; reads on an unopened file never reach end of file, so the job can loop instead of stopping with an error. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

2. Enter and leave the transaction type listdraft · online · 5 requirements · 8 rules · 11 criteria · 3 screens

Controls how administrators get into and out of the transaction type list. Each arrival from the admin menu or from the transaction type add/update screen starts a clean list on page 1 with no filters or selections, and leaving returns the user to where they came from, or to the admin menu. The list must never carry stale filters, selections or a pending action over from an earlier visit.

As an administrator, I want the transaction type list to start fresh when I arrive and return me to where I came from when I leave, so that I always begin from a clean, predictable view.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-012business ruleWhen the transaction type list is entered from another program (such as option 5 of the admin menu), the system shall discard any earlier filters, row selections and paging position, start at the first page and treat the request as Enter.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-013business ruleWhen the operator returns to the list from the transaction type add/update screen (transaction 'CTTU') by pressing PF3, the system shall treat the key as Enter rather than exit and show the first page afresh, discarding previous filters, selections and paging.AC-01, AC-02, AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-014design noteWhen the operator presses PF3 on the transaction type list, the system shall commit work and return to the program it was entered from, or to the admin menu (COADM01C, transaction 'CA00') when it was started directly or from itself.AC-07
REQ-F-015design noteWhen the transaction type list receives input from its own screen (caller data is present and the previous program was 'COTRTLIC'), the system shall read the screen and then check the row actions, the description filter, the type code filter and finally whether any records match the filters, in that order.AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-016design noteWhen the first row of a page is read and the page number is still 0 (a fresh start of the list), the system shall set the page number to 1.AC-10, AC-11

  • SME-182 On the transaction-type list, PF3 is described three ways: go to the destination program and end the list; restart the list on the first page when returning from the add/update screen; and clear everything and show the list from the start.   • SME-186 When counting transaction types fails, what diagnostic details should the operator see, and does the failure end the session on that screen? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-187 When one submission on the transaction-type list has several errors (an invalid action code, more than one action, or missing required text), which message should the operator see first? (Business analyst)
  • SME-188 The error message 'Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table ' ends with a space. Does that trailing space matter in the message shown to the operator? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-131 Is this intended? The EVALUATE branch for PF3 or re-entry from another program (lines 738-762) can never run: PF3 always leaves the program or is converted to Enter earlier, and no caller passes the 're-enter' context from another program. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The list keeps its filters, row selections and paging position in per-user session state. Navigating to the list from another screen (for example admin menu option 5) must reset that state and load the first page, so a fresh entry never shows an earlier visit's view. Restart list on re-entry from another program
  • Same entry behaviour as above, seen from the request side: a fresh entry is handled as a plain 'show list' request (the Enter action) with empty filters and page 1. A route or query parameter showing where the user came from is enough to tell a fresh entry from a submission of the list's own form. Start list afresh on entry from elsewhere
  • Going back from the transaction type add/update screen must land on a freshly loaded first page of the list. It is not an exit from the list, so the back action from that screen goes to the list route with its state reset. Restart list on re-entry from another program
  • The add/update screen's back/exit action, when returning to the list, is treated as a 'show list' request on page 1. The list must not take it as its own exit and pass the user on to the admin menu. Start list afresh on entry from elsewhere
  • Exit from the list commits any open unit of work and navigates back to the screen that opened it. Keep a 'return to' value in the session; when it is missing or points at the list itself, go to the admin menu. Restart list on re-entry from another program
  • When the list's own form is submitted, the server-side handler runs its checks in a fixed order: row actions first, then the description filter, then the type code filter, then whether any record matches the filters. Keep that order, because which message wins depends on it. Process screen input on self re-entry
  • Page numbers start at 1. A freshly started list has page number 0 or none; set it to 1 when the first page of rows is loaded. Number the first page on first row
3. Page through transaction typesdraft · online · 15 requirements · 16 rules · 21 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Lets administrators page forwards and backwards through transaction types seven at a time, in ascending type-code order, within any accepted filters. It must never skip or repeat a type between pages. At either end of the list it must say so ('No more pages to display', 'No previous pages to display', 'No more pages for these search conditions') rather than show a wrong page.

As an administrator, I want to page forwards and backwards through the transaction types, seven at a time, so that I can review every type in code order.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#3

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-017formattingThe system shall show at most 7 transaction types per page in ascending type-code order, limited to the type-code filter and the description pattern only when each filter has been accepted (type filter flag and description filter flag = '1').AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-018business ruleWhen a page has been filled with 7 types and another matching type follows, the system shall record that a next page exists (next-page indicator 'Y') and keep that following type code as the start of the next page.AC-03
REQ-F-019business ruleWhen the database has no more matching transaction types before 7 rows are filled, the system shall stop reading and record that no next page exists.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-020business ruleWhen the user presses F8 and a next page exists, the system shall show the page starting at the stored next type code (type code >= that code), add 1 to the page number and clear any row selections.AC-07
REQ-F-021business ruleWhen the matching transaction types run out after the operator pressed F8 and no other message is pending, the system shall show 'No more pages for these search conditions'.AC-05, AC-06, AC-08
REQ-F-022formattingWhen the operator presses PF8 and there is no further page and the last page had not already been shown, the system shall show the information message 'Type U to update, D to delete any record' and remember that the last page has now been shown.AC-09
REQ-F-023formattingWhen the user presses F8 again after the last page has already been shown, the system shall show the same page again with the message 'No more pages to display'.AC-10
REQ-F-024business ruleWhen the user presses F7 and the list is not on the first page, the system shall show the 7 matching types just before the current page's first code, in ascending order, subtract 1 from the page number, clear row selections and mark that a next page exists.AC-11
REQ-F-025formattingWhen the user presses F7 on the first page and there are no input errors, the system shall show the first page again from its first type code with the message 'No previous pages to display'.AC-12
REQ-F-026formattingWhen the operator presses PF7 and the page shown afterwards is page 1 (because page 1 was already shown, or because the list paged back from page 2), the system shall show 'No previous pages to display', unless a filter error or a completed delete or update message takes precedence.AC-13, AC-14
REQ-F-027formattingWhen the list is on page 1 and no transaction type is read, the system shall show 'No records found for this search condition.'.AC-15
REQ-F-028formattingWhen no input error, page up, page down, exit, or delete or update request applies, the system shall re-read the current page starting from its first type code and show it.AC-16, AC-17
REQ-F-029formattingWhen no delete or update outcome, filter error, delete or update prompt, or paging message applies, and either no informational message is set or another page exists, the system shall show the message 'Type U to update, D to delete any record'.AC-18, AC-19
REQ-F-030error handlingIf the database cannot open or read the forward list of transaction types, then the system shall show an empty or partly filled page and a database error message naming the failed step.AC-20
REQ-F-031error handlingIf a previous-page read stops before all 7 rows are filled, because fewer than 7 earlier types match or the database fails, then the system shall stop reading and report a database error ('Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD').AC-21

F7Yes--Gap: R49 applies only with no input errors; no rule states the page shown on F7 from the first page when an input error exists beyond R30/R31's general redisplay.

Open questions

  • SME-189 Could the transaction-type table ever need more than 9 pages (63 or more types)? When paging back gives fewer than 7 types, how should that page be shown? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-006 Is this intended? On F7, the backward read treats running out of earlier records (end of data) as a database error. The program then shows a Db2 error message and a part-filled page instead of a short first page. It does this when fewer than 7 matching types come before the current page, for example after another user deletes types. The backward read also does not check whether the list failed to open. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-132 Is this intended? The page number only becomes 1 when a first row is read, so when nothing at all is read on a fresh start the page number is still 0 and the 'No records found for this search condition.' message is not given. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-133 Is this intended? Paging back from page 2 to page 1 with PF7 succeeds but still shows 'No previous pages to display', because the page number is decremented before the message is chosen. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Read the page as a keyset query ordered by type code, from the page's start code, with the active filters, taking up to 8 rows (7 to show plus 1 to look ahead). When fewer than 8 come back, stop and record that there is no next page. Do not treat running out of rows as an error. Handle end of transaction type data
4. Filter the transaction type listdraft · online · 9 requirements · 10 rules · 12 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Lets administrators narrow the transaction type list by an exact two-digit type code and by text contained in the description. A blank or '00' code filter, or a blank description filter, means no filter. A non-numeric code filter must be rejected with 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', and changing either filter must restart paging from the first page.

As an administrator, I want to filter the transaction type list by type code and by description text, so that I can find the types I need quickly.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-032business ruleWhen the type code filter is blank, empty (low-values), zeros or '00', the system shall treat it as not supplied and list all type codes, with no error.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-033business ruleWhen a numeric type code filter is entered, the system shall list only the transaction type with that code.AC-04
REQ-F-034business ruleIf a type code filter is entered and is not numeric, then the system shall reject it with 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', show the filter in red with the cursor on it, lock the row selection fields and not re-read the list.AC-05
REQ-F-035design noteWhen the entered type code filter differs from the one last used, the system shall reset paging to the start, remember the new filter, and mark the filter as changed so that a pending F10 confirmation is treated as Enter.AC-06
REQ-F-036design noteWhen the entered type code filter equals the one last used, or both the entered and the previous filter are empty, the system shall keep the current paging and mark the filter as unchanged.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-037business ruleWhen the description filter is left blank, the system shall apply no description filter, so the list, paging and record count include every description.AC-09
REQ-F-038business ruleWhen a description filter is entered, the system shall list, page and count only transaction types whose description contains the entered text (trimmed and wrapped in '%' for a contains match).AC-12
REQ-F-039business ruleWhen the description filter entered differs from the one used for the previous screen (blank and blank count as the same), the system shall restart paging from the first page, remember the new filter and ignore any row actions entered on that screen.AC-10
REQ-F-040formattingWhen no delete or update has just completed and the type code filter or the description filter is in error, the system shall show no information message, so that only the filter error message (for example 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER' or 'No Records found for these filter conditions') is shown.AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-183 The transaction-type code filter's error message says 'MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', but the system only checks that the value is numeric. Should numbers that are not exactly 2 digits be refused? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-186 When counting transaction types fails, what diagnostic details should the operator see, and does the failure end the session on that screen? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-187 When one submission on the transaction-type list has several errors (an invalid action code, more than one action, or missing required text), which message should the operator see first? (Business analyst)
  • SME-188 The error message 'Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table ' ends with a space. Does that trailing space matter in the message shown to the operator? (Business analyst)

Design notes

  • Keep the last-used type code filter in session state. When the submitted filter differs from it, save the new value, reset paging to the first page, and set a 'filter changed' flag. With that flag set, a pending F10 confirmation is ignored and handled as a plain refresh. Restart paging when type filter changes
  • When the submitted type code filter equals the saved one, or both are empty, keep the current page position and clear the 'filter changed' flag. Restart paging when type filter changes
5. Update transaction type descriptions from the listdraft · online · 11 requirements · 11 rules · 13 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Lets administrators change a transaction type's description directly on a list row marked 'U', with checks before anything is saved. A changed description must be supplied and may hold only letters, digits and spaces. An unchanged one is reported as 'No change detected with respect to database values.'. The screen must never save, or appear to accept, a description that failed these checks.

As an administrator, I want to mark a listed transaction type for update or delete and change its description on the list screen, so that I can correct reference data online with clear validation feedback.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-041design noteWhen the operator submits the transaction type list screen, the system shall capture the type code and description filters and, for each of the 7 rows, the action code, the type code and the description.AC-01
REQ-F-042design noteWhen a row's description field holds only '*' or is blank, the system shall treat the description as not entered, and otherwise shall use the entered text with leading and trailing spaces removed.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-043business ruleWhen a transaction type row marked 'U' is submitted and the entered description matches the stored description, ignoring upper/lower case and leading or trailing spaces, the system shall show 'No change detected with respect to database values.' and skip the remaining description checks for that row.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-044business ruleWhen the entered description of a row marked 'U' differs from the stored description, the system shall treat the row as changed and check the first 50 characters of the description as a required letters-and-digits field named 'Transaction Desc'.AC-05
REQ-F-045business ruleIf a changed description is not entered (blank or '*'), then the system shall reject the input and show 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.', unless an earlier message has already been set.AC-12
REQ-F-046business ruleIf a changed description contains any character other than a letter, a digit or a space, then the system shall reject the input and show 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.', unless an earlier message has already been set.AC-06
REQ-F-047formattingIf a description entered for update fails its checks, then the system shall show that description in red with the cursor on it, and shall show a description that was not entered as '*'.AC-07
REQ-F-048formattingWhen a row is marked 'U' as the only valid action on the screen and the operator has typed a description that differs from the stored one and is not blank, the system shall show the operator's typed description on that row instead of the stored description.AC-13
REQ-F-049formattingWhen a row is not the single valid 'U' action on the screen, or it is but the typed description does not differ from the stored one, the system shall show the stored transaction type description on that row.AC-08
REQ-F-050business ruleIf the submitted screen has an input error, then the system shall show the error message and stay on the list screen rather than act on any key pressed.AC-09
REQ-F-051formattingIf the submitted screen has an input error but both the type code filter and the description filter are acceptable, then the system shall re-read the current page starting from its first type code before showing the error.AC-10, AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-183 The transaction-type code filter's error message says 'MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', but the system only checks that the value is numeric. Should numbers that are not exactly 2 digits be refused? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-186 When counting transaction types fails, what diagnostic details should the operator see, and does the failure end the session on that screen? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-187 When one submission on the transaction-type list has several errors (an invalid action code, more than one action, or missing required text), which message should the operator see first? (Business analyst)
  • SME-188 The error message 'Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table ' ends with a space. Does that trailing space matter in the message shown to the operator? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-029 Is this intended? The 'No change detected' case only sets a message and does not mark the input as an error, so the row stays ready for update; pressing F10 then still runs the database update. A change only in upper/lower case (e.g. 'Payment' to 'payment') is reported as no change but is saved on F10. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The list form posts the two filters plus seven row entries, each with an action, a type code and a description. Bind them to a request model with a fixed list of 7 rows. Map a description of '*' or all spaces to 'not entered', and trim any other description. Capture filters and row entries
  • Normalise row descriptions when reading the request: a blank value or a lone '*' becomes null (not entered), and any other value is trimmed at both ends. Validation and change detection work on the normalised value. Treat blank or asterisk description as unsupplied
6. Access to transaction type maintenancedraft · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria · 2 screens

Records how the legacy transaction type list controls who can change reference data. Started directly, it assumes the user is an administrator (user type 'A'), and it never checks the user type before allowing an update or delete. The new application must not carry that gap forward unknowingly: whether to keep or close it is a decision for security, and changes to transaction types should be restricted to authorised administrators.

As a security officer, I want to know how access to transaction type update and delete is controlled, so that only authorised users can change reference data.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security, updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#6

7. Filter the transaction type listdraft · online · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 4 criteria · 1 screen

When an administrator supplies a type code filter, a description filter or both, the list first counts the transaction types that match. If none match, it reports 'No Records found for these filter conditions' and highlights the filters. It must never show an empty list as if it were normal when the filters match nothing, and it must report a failed count as a database error rather than as 'no records'.

As an administrator, I want to filter the transaction type list by type code and description, so that I only see the transaction types I am looking for.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#7

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-052business ruleWhen neither the type filter nor the description filter holds a usable value (both blank, or the type filter is blank or not numeric with no description), the system shall skip the check that the filters match any record.AC-01
REQ-F-053business ruleWhen at least one filter holds a usable value, the system shall count the transaction types whose type code equals the type filter (if one was given) and whose description contains the description filter text (if one was given).AC-04
REQ-F-054business ruleIf no transaction type matches the supplied filters, then the system shall treat the input as an error, show 'No Records found for these filter conditions', show each supplied filter in red with the cursor on it, and lock the row selection fields.AC-02
REQ-F-055error handlingIf the database count of matching transaction types fails, then the system shall treat the input as an error and, unless another message is already set, show a database error message built from 'Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table ' and the SQL code.AC-03

8. Mark a list row for update or deletedraft · online · 9 requirements · 9 rules · 12 criteria · 1 screen · 1 gap

Lets administrators mark exactly one listed transaction type 'D' (delete) or 'U' (update) and then asks them to confirm with F10 before anything changes. It must reject any other action code ('Action code selected is invalid') and more than one marked row ('Please select only 1 action'). Marks entered while a filter is being changed are cleared rather than acted on.

As an administrator, I want to mark one transaction type on the list for update or delete and be asked to confirm, so that I can review the change before it is applied.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#8

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-056business ruleWhen the user has changed the transaction type filter or the description filter, the system shall clear every row action code and skip all row action checks for that submission.AC-01
REQ-F-057design noteWhen the filters are unchanged, the system shall count as an action every one of the 7 rows whose action code is not blank, and count separately the rows marked 'D' (delete) and 'U' (update).AC-02
REQ-F-058design noteWhen the filters are unchanged, the system shall remember the top-most row marked 'D' or 'U' as the selected row (0 if none) and note whether it differs from the row selected on the previous screen.AC-03, AC-04

REQ-F-060business ruleIf two to seven rows carry a non-blank action code, then the system shall highlight every row marked 'D' or 'U' in error, reject the input and show 'Please select only 1 action', replacing any 'Action code selected is invalid' message.AC-07, AC-08

REQ-F-064formattingWhen the user presses Enter with a row marked 'D' or 'U', the system shall show the same page again from its first type code, re-reading the list only when neither filter is in error.AC-12

Open questions

  • SME-183 The transaction-type code filter's error message says 'MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', but the system only checks that the value is numeric. Should numbers that are not exactly 2 digits be refused? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-184 Updating a transaction type is explicitly committed when it succeeds, but deleting one is not described as committed. Should a successful delete be committed in the same way? (Data owner)
  • SME-185 A transaction type cannot be deleted while it has 'dependent child records'. Which records count as dependents of a transaction type, and where are they stored? (Data owner)
  • SME-186 When counting transaction types fails, what diagnostic details should the operator see, and does the failure end the session on that screen? (Reference data product owner)
  • SME-187 When one submission on the transaction-type list has several errors (an invalid action code, more than one action, or missing required text), which message should the operator see first? (Business analyst)
  • SME-188 The error message 'Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table ' ends with a space. Does that trailing space matter in the message shown to the operator? (Business analyst)
  • SME-190 How important is the rule that the operator must confirm with F10 before a transaction type is deleted or updated? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or is it a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-065 Is this intended? The 'nothing changed' check compares only the row position and the filters, not the action letter. If the user is prompted to update a row, then changes its 'U' to 'D' and presses F10, the delete runs without the delete prompt ever being shown. The reverse (D changed to U) saves an update without the update prompt. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the filters are unchanged, go through the 7 submitted rows and count three things: rows with any non-blank action, rows marked 'D' and rows marked 'U'. The counts drive the 'only one action' and invalid-code checks. Tally row actions and route updates
  • Record the index of the top-most row marked 'D' or 'U' (0 if none) as the selected row in session state. Compare it with the selected row saved from the previous screen and set a 'selection changed' flag, which the F10 confirmation step uses. Count row actions and identify selected row
9. Confirm and apply a list update or deletedraft · online · 13 requirements · 13 rules · 15 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Carries out a pending list update or delete only when the administrator presses F10 and nothing has changed since the confirmation prompt (filters and selected row). It then reports 'HIGHLIGHTED row was updated' or 'HIGHLIGHTED row deleted.Hit Enter to continue'. It must never delete a type that other records still refer to, and must never report success when the database rejected the change.

As an administrator, I want to confirm a pending update or delete with F10, so that the transaction type table is changed only when I have reviewed the marked row.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#9

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-065business ruleWhen the user presses F10 and no delete or update is pending from the previous Enter, the system shall treat the key as Enter and just show the list again.AC-01
REQ-F-066business ruleWhen the user presses F10 while a delete or update is pending but has changed the type filter, the description filter or which row is selected since the confirmation prompt, the system shall treat the key as Enter instead of carrying out the change.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-067business ruleWhen the user presses F10 while a delete or update is pending and neither filter nor the selected row has changed, the system shall delete the marked transaction type if the row is marked 'D', or save the new description if it is marked 'U'.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-068business ruleWhen the user presses PF10 to confirm a row marked 'U', and the type filter, description filter and row selection are unchanged since the screen was shown, the system shall replace that type code's stored description with the entered description, trimmed, in the transaction type table (CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE), and commit the change.AC-07
REQ-F-069formattingWhen an update has been confirmed with PF10, the system shall re-read the list starting from the first type code on the current page and redisplay it, whether or not the update succeeded.AC-08
REQ-F-070formattingWhen the confirmed update succeeds and no deletion was confirmed in the same request, the system shall show the message 'HIGHLIGHTED row was updated'.AC-09
REQ-F-071error handlingIf the database finds no row for the type code being updated (SQLCODE +100), then the system shall show a message starting 'Record not found. Deleted by others ?' and leave the update pending for confirmation.AC-10
REQ-F-072error handlingIf the update hits a deadlock (SQLCODE -911), then the system shall show a message starting 'Deadlock. Someone else updating ?', treat the request as an input error and leave the update pending for confirmation.AC-11
REQ-F-073error handlingIf the update fails with any other negative database code, then the system shall show a message starting 'Update failed with' followed by the database error details, and leave the update pending for confirmation.AC-12
REQ-F-074business ruleWhen the operator has marked one transaction type for delete and presses F10 without changing the filters or the selection, the system shall delete that type from the transaction type table (CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE).AC-06
REQ-F-075business ruleWhen the delete succeeds, the system shall commit the change, show 'HIGHLIGHTED row deleted.Hit Enter to continue', and start the next interaction from the first page with filters cleared.AC-13
REQ-F-076error handlingIf the database refuses the delete because other records still refer to the transaction type (SQLCODE -532), then the system shall delete nothing, keep the delete request pending, and show 'Please delete associated child records first:' followed by the database error details.AC-14
REQ-F-077error handlingIf the delete fails for any other database reason, then the system shall show 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the database error details and treat the delete as not done.AC-15

Open questions

  • SME-184 Updating a transaction type is explicitly committed when it succeeds, but deleting one is not described as committed. Should a successful delete be committed in the same way? (Data owner)
  • SME-185 A transaction type cannot be deleted while it has 'dependent child records'. Which records count as dependents of a transaction type, and where are they stored? (Data owner)
  • SME-190 How important is the rule that the operator must confirm with F10 before a transaction type is deleted or updated? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or is it a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • SME-191 How important is the rule for updating a transaction type's description from the list screen? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or is it a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • SME-192 How important is the rule for deleting a transaction type from the list screen, which is blocked when dependent records exist? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or is it a rule that would be costly to get wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-064 Is this intended? The description length sent to the database is always the full 50-character field length, not the length of the trimmed text, so a shorter description is stored padded with trailing spaces. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-065 Is this intended? The 'nothing changed' check compares only the row position and the filters, not the action letter. If the user is prompted to update a row, then changes its 'U' to 'D' and presses F10, the delete runs without the delete prompt ever being shown. The reverse (D changed to U) saves an update without the update prompt. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

10. Navigate from the transaction type listdraft · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria · 3 screens

Gives administrators two ways off the transaction type list: F3 saves any work and returns to the admin menu, and F2 opens the screen for adding a transaction type. Both must keep the user's signed-on session context.

As an administrator, I want to leave the list or go to the add screen with a function key, so that I can return to the admin menu or add a new transaction type.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#10

  • SME-183 The transaction-type code filter's error message says 'MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', but the system only checks that the value is numeric. Should numbers that are not exactly 2 digits be refused? (Reference data product owner)

11. Look up a transaction type to maintaindraft · online · 11 requirements · 14 rules · 11 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

On the transaction type maintenance screen, the administrator enters a type code and it is looked up so the type can be maintained, or added when it is not on file. The code must be supplied, numeric and not zero, and is stored as two digits. When no type has that code the screen says 'No record found for this key in database' and offers 'Press F05 to add. F12 to cancel'; it must never treat a missing type as found.

As an administrator, I want to enter a transaction type code on the maintenance screen and have it looked up, so that I can maintain an existing type or add one that is not on file.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#11

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-080business ruleWhile the state is neither new-record entry ('R') nor awaiting save confirmation ('N'), when the transaction type code is blank, the system shall show 'Tran Type code must be supplied.', mark the code field '*' in red, return to asking for a code and skip all other checks.AC-08
REQ-F-081business ruleWhile the state is neither 'R' nor 'N', when the transaction type code is not numeric, the system shall show 'Tran Type code must be numeric.', highlight the code in red, return to asking for a code and skip all other checks.AC-09
REQ-F-082business ruleWhile the state is neither 'R' nor 'N', when the transaction type code is zero, the system shall show 'Tran Type code must not be zero.', highlight the code in red, return to asking for a code and skip all other checks.AC-10
REQ-F-083formattingWhen a transaction type code fails these checks, the system shall return to the 'details not fetched' state rather than keep an invalid-search-key state ('K').AC-01
REQ-F-084business ruleWhile the state is neither 'R' nor 'N', when the code is a valid non-zero number and no record has been fetched yet, the system shall store the code as two digits with a leading zero and stop editing, so that the table is searched for that code.AC-02
REQ-F-085design noteWhen the maintenance screen looks up a transaction type code, the system shall first clear the previously held original details and the information message.AC-11
REQ-F-086design noteWhen the transaction type table (CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE) returns a row for the requested code, the system shall mark the type as found and keep its code and description (to its stored length) as the original values used for display and for detecting the operator's later edits.AC-03
REQ-F-087design noteIf the looked-up transaction type is not found or the read fails, then the system shall keep no original values.AC-03
REQ-F-088business ruleIf no transaction type row exists for the entered code, then the system shall mark the code as in error, show 'No record found for this key in database' unless another message is already set, and offer to add the record with 'Press F05 to add. F12 to cancel'.AC-04
REQ-F-089business ruleWhen the entered code was not found ('X') and the operator submits the same code again without pressing F5, the system shall keep the previously captured code and description, ignore what was typed on the screen, skip all other checks, treat the code as valid and return to the 'details not fetched' state so the code is looked up again in the transaction type table.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-090historical artifactWhen F5 is pressed in the not-found state ('X'), the system shall switch straight to new-record entry.AC-07

  • DEF-135 Is this intended? The invalid-search-key state ('K') is set and immediately overwritten with the not-fetched state, so the program's separate handling of 'K' (here and in 2000-DECIDE-ACTION) never takes effect. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Before each lookup by type code, clear the saved 'original' transaction type and the info message in the screen's session state, so that a failed lookup cannot leave the previous type's values behind. Capture fetched transaction type as original
  • Look up the transaction type by its primary key (the two-digit type code). On a hit, set a 'found' flag and keep the code and description as the values on file, used for display and change detection. Find transaction type by code
  • On a successful lookup, save the stored code and description, at its full stored length, as the 'original' snapshot in session state; later edits are compared against it. When the lookup finds nothing or fails, save no snapshot. Capture fetched transaction type as original
  • In the not-found state, if the same code is submitted again without F5, keep the code and description already in session state and ignore the posted form values, including any typed description, before the code is looked up again. Skip staging for repeated not-found key
12. Show maintenance screen values and messagesdraft · online · 9 requirements · 10 rules · 12 criteria · 2 screens

Makes the maintenance screen show the right values and guidance message for each step, such as 'Enter transaction type to be maintained' or 'Update transaction type details shown.'. In states where the stored record is being reviewed or has just been deleted, it must show the values on file; in states where the administrator is editing, it must show what they entered. It must never show typed values as if they were the values on file.

As an administrator, I want the maintenance screen to show the right values and guidance message for where I am in the process, so that I know what to do next.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#12

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-091formattingWhen the maintenance screen is shown for a fresh start (on arrival from the admin menu or the transaction type list, or when a finished, failed or cancelled action restarts the screen), the system shall show the information message 'Enter transaction type to be maintained'.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-092formattingWhen the operator returns to the maintenance screen and no transaction type has been fetched yet (including after a blank or invalid type code), the system shall show the message 'Enter transaction type to be maintained'.AC-03
REQ-F-093formattingWhen the maintenance screen is showing a fetched transaction type, or a cancelled change has no original transaction type held, the system shall show the message 'Enter transaction type to be maintained'.AC-04
REQ-F-094formattingWhen the maintenance screen is redisplayed in a state that has no information message of its own and no message is already set (for example after a delete the database refused because child records exist), the system shall show the information message 'Enter transaction type to be maintained'.AC-05
REQ-F-095formattingWhen the operator's changes failed validation, or the operator cancelled a validated change while an original transaction type is still held, the system shall show the message 'Update transaction type details shown.'AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-096formattingWhen the screen is redisplayed after the first entry and the state is record shown ('S'), awaiting delete confirmation ('9'), delete failed ('6'), delete done ('7'), update cancelled ('B') or any state without its own display rule, the system shall show the code and description as stored on the table, discarding typed values and clearing description error marks.AC-12
REQ-F-097formattingWhen the screen is redisplayed after the first entry and the state is changes entered ('E', 'N', 'L' or 'F'), not found ('X'), invalid key ('K'), new record ('R') or update done ('C'), the system shall show the transaction type code and description as the operator entered them.AC-08
REQ-F-098business ruleWhen the entered details have failed validation ('E') or have passed validation and are waiting for F5 confirmation ('N'), the system shall leave the maintenance state unchanged, so the screen is shown again with the entered values and the message for that state.AC-09
REQ-F-099design noteWhen a key press is not an exit, a first entry, a delete, save or cancel step handled on its own, or a key not allowed in the current state, the system shall read the screen input, validate it, decide the next action and redisplay the screen.AC-10, AC-11

  • SME-201 If the transaction type maintenance screen finds itself in an unrecognised state, the legacy system terminates abnormally. Should the new system do the same, or recover and show the operator an error message? (Application development lead)
  • SME-202 PF5 is allowed while a transaction type delete is awaiting confirmation, but nothing says what it does then. What should PF5 do in that situation? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-204 Please confirm this rule: when the transaction type maintenance screen is opened for the first time from the administration menu or the transaction type list (or details were not fetched), and PF3 was not pressed, the system clears its working data and the account identifier, shows an empty search screen, and waits for input. (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • DEF-128 Is this intended? When the database refuses a delete because child records exist (SQLCODE -532), the program does not set the delete-failed state ('6') as it does for other delete errors. The state stays at '8', so the screen shows the generic 'Enter transaction type to be maintained' prompt instead of 'Changes unsuccessful'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-135 Is this intended? The invalid-search-key state ('K') is set and immediately overwritten with the not-fetched state, so the program's separate handling of 'K' (here and in 2000-DECIDE-ACTION) never takes effect. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The maintenance screen handler has a default path for actions without a dedicated handler (exit, first entry, delete, save, cancel, or a key not allowed in the current state): bind the posted form, validate it, work out the next state, and render the screen again. Process operator input in other cases
  • Route each request on the pair (action pressed, current screen state). Any pair without a specific handler falls through to the default: bind and validate the input, decide the next action, render again. A state machine with an explicit fallback transition is the natural way to build this. Route request by key and update state
13. Detect changes to a fetched transaction typedraft · online · 3 requirements · 4 rules · 6 criteria · 1 screen

When an administrator presses Enter on a transaction type they fetched, the maintenance screen checks whether the type code or description has actually changed. If nothing has changed, it says so and does not offer a save. The comparison must ignore upper/lower case and leading or trailing spaces, so a record that differs only in case or spacing is never treated as changed and saved again.

As an administrator, I want the maintenance screen to tell me when I have not changed anything, so that I do not save a record that is the same as the one on file.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#13

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-100business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter on a transaction type, the system shall treat it as unchanged if the type code and the description match the values fetched, ignoring upper/lower case and leading or trailing spaces, and otherwise record that a change has occurred.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-101business ruleWhen no change is found, the system shall show 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.', leave the record in the show-details state without offering a save, and skip the description checks.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-102business ruleWhile the changes are already validated and awaiting F5 confirmation (state 'N') or already committed (state 'C'), the system shall skip the description checks and keep the current state.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06

14. Cancel a pending maintenance changedraft · online · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria · 1 screen · 2 gaps

Lets an administrator back out of a pending update or delete of a transaction type with F12, so nothing is written to the reference data. Cancelling an update shows the stored values again for editing. Cancelling a delete returns to the search. A cancel must never save or delete anything, and anything typed on the screen at the time is ignored.

As an administrator, I want to cancel a pending update or delete with F12, so that nothing is changed when I decide not to go ahead.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#14

REQ-F-104business ruleWhen F12 is pressed while a delete is waiting for confirmation ('9'), the system shall ignore the screen input, show 'Delete was cancelled' and return to asking for a transaction type.AC-02
REQ-F-105historical artifactWhen F12 is pressed on a shown record ('S'), the system shall restart the screen to ask for a new transaction type.AC-03

15. Exit the maintenance screendraft · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria · 3 screens

Lets an administrator leave transaction type maintenance with F3. Any completed database work is committed, and the administrator returns to the Admin menu. When the screen was opened from the Admin menu or the Transaction Type list, F3 must always go back to the Admin menu, never to the list.

As an administrator, I want F3 to save my work and return me to the admin menu, so that I can leave transaction type maintenance safely.

16. Find a transaction type to maintaindraft · online · 9 requirements · 9 rules · 12 criteria · 3 screens

Lets an administrator enter a transaction type code and see that type's details, or learn that it is not on file and can be added. The code must be supplied, numeric and non-zero, and it is padded to two digits (for example 5 becomes 05) before the lookup. An invalid code must never trigger a lookup, and only the first error found is shown.

As an administrator, I want to enter a transaction type code and see its details, so that I can choose the transaction type I need to maintain.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#16

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-108formattingWhen the maintenance screen is entered for the first time from the Admin menu or the transaction type list, or is started with no prior context, the system shall clear any saved maintenance context and show an empty search screen asking 'Enter transaction type to be maintained'.AC-01
REQ-F-109design noteWhen the operator presses Enter on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen while not adding a new record and not awaiting confirmation of changes, the system shall check the entered transaction type code before looking it up.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-110business ruleIf the transaction type code is left blank or entered as '*', then the system shall show 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' and keep waiting for a search code without looking anything up.AC-09
REQ-F-111business ruleIf the transaction type code is supplied but is not a number, then the system shall show 'Tran Type code must be numeric.', mark the search code as invalid and not look anything up.AC-10
REQ-F-112business ruleIf the transaction type code is a number equal to zero, then the system shall show 'Tran Type code must not be zero.', mark the search code as invalid and not look anything up.AC-11
REQ-F-113business ruleWhen the transaction type code is a supplied, non-zero number, the system shall accept it, convert it to a two-digit code padded with a leading zero, and use that as the lookup key.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-114formattingIf more than one check fails on the same entry, then the system shall show only the first error message found.AC-12
REQ-F-115business ruleWhen a valid transaction type code is entered on the search screen, the system shall look it up in the transaction type table and show its details (state 'S') if found, or report it as not found (state 'X') with the prompt 'Press F05 to add. F12 to cancel'.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-116business ruleWhile the searched code was not found, when the operator re-sends the same code without pressing F5, the system shall treat it as a new search and look the code up again.AC-08

Open questions

  • SME-195 On the transaction type maintenance screen, when the operator's key and the screen's current state match none of the recognised combinations, should the system go straight to deciding the next action, or first process what the operator typed on the screen? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-196 Change outcomes 'L' and 'F' are both described as "changes failed". Is there any business difference between them, and if so, what is it? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-197 When the transaction type description is missing or contains characters other than letters and numbers, what message should the operator see? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-203 The screen treats 'entered but details not fetched' the same as a first entry. What situation leads to this, for example a previous lookup that failed or one that was never attempted? (Transaction type reference data business owner)
  • SME-204 Please confirm this rule: when the transaction type maintenance screen is opened for the first time from the administration menu or the transaction type list (or details were not fetched), and PF3 was not pressed, the system clears its working data and the account identifier, shows an empty search screen, and waits for input. (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-205 How important is the rule that a transaction type code must be a non-zero two-digit number, stored with a leading zero? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or costly only if it is wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • SME-207 Should a new transaction type go through a review or confirmation step before it is created? Or is the intended flow: search, get 'not found', enter the details, then press PF5 to save? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-030 Is this intended? The 'No input received' message for a blank search code can never be shown, because the blank check always sets 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' first. Also, the number check accepts signs and decimals, so '-5' is accepted as '05' and '.5' passes the not-zero check but is stored as '00'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-068 Is this intended? Several branches of the decision step can never run: after a save (state 'C') the program always resets to the search screen before the decision step, so its 'C -> show details' branch is dead; F12 never reaches the decision step with a validated key, so F12 never re-reads the table; the 'delete pending + F12' branch is shadowed by the earlier F12 branch; and the invalid-search-key state 'K' is overwritten by 'not fetched' immediately after it is set, so it never persists. The check for 'Invalid Key pressed. ' also tests a message nothing sets (the code that set it is commented out). (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Code validation needs to run before the lookup, as a step in the search action. It applies only when the screen is neither adding a new record nor waiting for confirmation of changes. In those two modes, an Enter press must not re-validate the search code or look it up again. Validate transaction type search key
17. Change a transaction type descriptiondraft · online · 13 requirements · 13 rules · 14 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

Lets an administrator change a transaction type's description, check it, and confirm with F5 before it is written to the transaction type table. The description must be supplied, may hold only letters, digits and spaces, and is limited to 50 characters. Nothing is saved until the administrator confirms, and a record lock must be reported as unsuccessful. The legacy screen reports other update failures as committed; the team should review that behaviour rather than copy it unknowingly.

As an administrator, I want to change a transaction type's description and confirm it before saving, so that the transaction type reference data stays correct.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#17

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-117business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter after changing the description of a displayed or new transaction type, the system shall mark the changes as not OK (state 'E') and then validate the description (up to 50 characters).AC-01
REQ-F-118design noteWhen the operator enters '*' or leaves the transaction type description blank, the system shall treat the description as not supplied, and otherwise keep the entry with leading and trailing spaces removed.AC-02
REQ-F-119business ruleIf the changed description is blank (spaces or '*'), then the system shall show 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' and keep the changes-not-OK state ('E').AC-12
REQ-F-120business ruleIf the changed description contains any character other than letters, digits and spaces, then the system shall show 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' and keep the changes-not-OK state ('E').AC-13
REQ-F-121business ruleWhen the changed description passes validation, the system shall move to changes-validated-awaiting-confirmation (state 'N') and show 'Changes validated.Press F5 to save'.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-122business ruleWhen the operator changes the shown or new details and the changes fail an edit, the system shall move to changes not OK (state 'E'), and when nothing changed, the system shall keep showing the details.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-123business ruleWhen the operator presses F5 after the changes have been validated and are awaiting confirmation (state 'N'), the system shall update that type's description in the transaction type table and then show the outcome on the screen.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-124business ruleWhen the description update succeeds, the system shall commit the change, set the outcome to committed ('C') and show 'Changes committed to database'.AC-06, AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-125business ruleIf the update cannot lock the row (SQLCODE -911), then the system shall set the outcome to lock error ('L'), show 'Changes unsuccessful' and give the error 'Could not lock record for update'.AC-06, AC-07, AC-09
REQ-F-126error handlingIf the update fails with any other negative SQLCODE, then the system shall show the error 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:…' with the database error text, yet set the outcome to committed ('C') and show 'Changes committed to database' instead of 'Changes unsuccessful'.AC-14
REQ-F-127business ruleIf the save fails for any other database reason, then the system shall end in state 'F' showing 'Changes unsuccessful'.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-128business ruleWhen F12 is pressed while validated changes await confirmation (state 'N'), the system shall discard the pending save, show 'Update was cancelled' and mark the changes as backed out (state 'B').AC-10
REQ-F-129business ruleWhile changes are backed out (state 'B') and the next input brings no new change, the system shall return to changes not OK (state 'E') so the operator can edit again, keeping states 'E' and 'N' otherwise unchanged in the decision step.AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-195 On the transaction type maintenance screen, when the operator's key and the screen's current state match none of the recognised combinations, should the system go straight to deciding the next action, or first process what the operator typed on the screen? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-196 Change outcomes 'L' and 'F' are both described as "changes failed". Is there any business difference between them, and if so, what is it? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-197 When the transaction type description is missing or contains characters other than letters and numbers, what message should the operator see? (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-198 When a transaction type description is updated successfully, does anything else need to happen (for example notifications, logging or other updates) before the screen reports the save result? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-199 The 'update failed' outcome is tied to the message 'Update of record failed', but the actual update error shows 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table'. Which situation should count as 'update failed', and which message should the operator see? (Application development lead)
  • SME-200 When a transaction type cannot be deleted because other records still use it, what state should the screen be left in, and what should the operator be told? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-201 If the transaction type maintenance screen finds itself in an unrecognised state, the legacy system terminates abnormally. Should the new system do the same, or recover and show the operator an error message? (Application development lead)
  • SME-202 PF5 is allowed while a transaction type delete is awaiting confirmation, but nothing says what it does then. What should PF5 do in that situation? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-204 Please confirm this rule: when the transaction type maintenance screen is opened for the first time from the administration menu or the transaction type list (or details were not fetched), and PF3 was not pressed, the system clears its working data and the account identifier, shows an empty search screen, and waits for input. (Business analyst (transaction type maintenance))
  • SME-206 How important is the rule that saving a transaction type updates its description, or creates the type if it does not yet exist? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or costly only if it is wrong? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • SME-207 Should a new transaction type go through a review or confirmation step before it is created? Or is the intended flow: search, get 'not found', enter the details, then press PF5 to save? (Business SME (transaction type reference data))
  • DEF-030 Is this intended? The 'No input received' message for a blank search code can never be shown, because the blank check always sets 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' first. Also, the number check accepts signs and decimals, so '-5' is accepted as '05' and '.5' passes the not-zero check but is stored as '00'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-066 Is this intended? When the update fails with an SQL error other than -911, or the insert of a new type fails, the program writes the SQL error text into the same field that holds the 'Update of record failed' flag. That flag is lost, so the program sets the outcome to committed and the screen shows 'Changes committed to database' alongside the error text. The failed outcome 'Changes unsuccessful' is never shown. In addition, the insert error message shows the update's SQLCODE (+100), not the insert's. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-068 Is this intended? Several branches of the decision step can never run: after a save (state 'C') the program always resets to the search screen before the decision step, so its 'C -> show details' branch is dead; F12 never reaches the decision step with a validated key, so F12 never re-reads the table; the 'delete pending + F12' branch is shadowed by the earlier F12 branch; and the invalid-search-key state 'K' is overwritten by 'not fetched' immediately after it is set, so it never persists. The check for 'Invalid Key pressed. ' also tests a message nothing sets (the code that set it is commented out). (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Description input needs normalising before validation and comparison. Remove leading and trailing spaces, and treat an empty value or a lone '*' as 'not supplied' (null). Validation then sees a missing description rather than a literal '*' or blanks. Treat asterisk or blank as not supplied
18. Add a new transaction typedraft · online · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria · 2 screens

Lets an administrator add a transaction type whose code is not yet on file, so new kinds of transactions can be classified. After a search finds nothing, F5 opens a new-record entry, and the confirmed save inserts the code and description into the transaction type table. The legacy screen reports a failed insert as committed; the team should review that behaviour rather than copy it unknowingly.

As an administrator, I want to add a transaction type that is not yet on file, so that new kinds of transactions can be classified.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#18

REQ-F-131business ruleWhen the save finds no row for the type (SQLCODE +100), the system shall insert the type code and description as a new row in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE, commit it and show 'Changes committed to database'.AC-02
REQ-F-132error handlingIf the insert of a new type fails, then the system shall show the error 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:…' with the database error text, yet set the outcome to committed ('C') and show 'Changes committed to database' instead of 'Changes unsuccessful'.AC-03

19. Delete a transaction typedraft · online · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 7 criteria · 1 screen

Lets an administrator delete an obsolete transaction type in two steps: F4 asks for confirmation and a second F4 deletes it. It must delete only the code originally fetched for display, never a code typed since. It must refuse the delete while other records still refer to the type. F12 cancels without deleting anything.

As an administrator, I want to delete a transaction type after confirming it, so that obsolete transaction types are removed without accidental loss.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#19

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-133business ruleWhen a transaction type's details are on screen and the operator presses F4, the system shall not delete yet but shall ask for confirmation with the message 'Delete this record ? Press F4 to confirm', with all fields protected.AC-01
REQ-F-134business ruleWhen the operator presses F4 again while the delete confirmation is pending, the system shall delete the transaction type with the code originally fetched for display (not any code typed since) from the transaction type table.AC-02
REQ-F-135business ruleWhen the confirmed delete succeeds, the system shall commit the deletion and show 'Delete successful.'.AC-03
REQ-F-136error handlingIf the confirmed delete is refused because other records still refer to the transaction type (SQLCODE -532), then the system shall not delete it and shall show an error starting 'Please delete associated child records first:' followed by the SQL code and database message.AC-06
REQ-F-137error handlingIf the confirmed delete fails for any other database reason, then the system shall mark the delete as failed, show 'Changes unsuccessful' as the information message, and show an error starting 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the SQL code and database message.AC-07
REQ-F-138business ruleWhen F12 is pressed while a delete awaits confirmation (state '9'), the system shall not delete the record, show 'Delete was cancelled' and return to the search state with details not fetched.AC-04
REQ-F-139formattingWhen the operator presses a key after a delete has succeeded or failed, the system shall start over and prompt for a new transaction type to search for.AC-05

  • SME-198 When a transaction type description is updated successfully, does anything else need to happen (for example notifications, logging or other updates) before the screen reports the save result? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-199 The 'update failed' outcome is tied to the message 'Update of record failed', but the actual update error shows 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table'. Which situation should count as 'update failed', and which message should the operator see? (Application development lead)
  • SME-200 When a transaction type cannot be deleted because other records still use it, what state should the screen be left in, and what should the operator be told? (Reference data business owner)
  • SME-201 If the transaction type maintenance screen finds itself in an unrecognised state, the legacy system terminates abnormally. Should the new system do the same, or recover and show the operator an error message? (Application development lead)
  • SME-202 PF5 is allowed while a transaction type delete is awaiting confirmation, but nothing says what it does then. What should PF5 do in that situation? (Reference data business owner)
  • DEF-067 Is this intended? On a referential-constraint refusal (SQLCODE -532), the code does not set the delete-failed state ('6'). The screen stays in state '8' (start delete), so no 'Changes unsuccessful' information message is shown and the next key press does not reset the screen the way it does after other failures. The error text also concatenates the database message (SQLERRM) twice into a 75-character field, so it is cut off. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-068 Is this intended? Several branches of the decision step can never run: after a save (state 'C') the program always resets to the search screen before the decision step, so its 'C -> show details' branch is dead; F12 never reaches the decision step with a validated key, so F12 never re-reads the table; the 'delete pending + F12' branch is shadowed by the earlier F12 branch; and the invalid-search-key state 'K' is overwritten by 'not fetched' immediately after it is set, so it never persists. The check for 'Invalid Key pressed. ' also tests a message nothing sets (the code that set it is commented out). (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

20. Control maintenance screen keys and flowdraft · online · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 7 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

Controls which keys the transaction type maintenance screen accepts at each step, so an administrator cannot save, delete or cancel out of sequence. A key that is not allowed in the current step shows 'Invalid key pressed' and does nothing else. After any finished or cancelled action, the screen starts over cleanly at the empty search screen.

As an administrator, I want the maintenance screen to accept only the keys that make sense at each step and to start over cleanly, so that I cannot trigger an action out of sequence.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#20

Requirements

REQ-F-140business ruleThe system shall accept F3 (exit) in every state, and Enter in every state except while a delete is awaiting confirmation.AC-01
REQ-F-141business ruleThe system shall accept F4 only when record details are shown or a delete is awaiting confirmation; F5 only when changes are validated, the record was not found, or a delete is in progress; and F12 only when changes are validated, details are shown, the record was not found, a delete is awaiting confirmation, or a new record is being created.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-142business ruleIf the key pressed is not allowed in the current state, then the system shall redisplay with the message 'Invalid key pressed' (when no other message is already set) and take no other action.AC-04

REQ-F-144error handlingIf the decision step meets a screen state it does not handle, then the system shall abend with code '0001' and message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'.AC-07

21. Maintain transaction types in batchdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Lets operations apply a file of transaction type add, update and delete requests to the transaction type table in one batch run, writing a log of the run. Each line holds one request: an action code ('A', 'U', 'D', or '*' for a comment), a two-digit numeric type code and a description of up to 50 characters. The job must apply each request exactly as the file states and report what it did.

As an operations user, I want to apply a file of transaction type add, update and delete requests in a batch job, so that many reference data changes can be made at once.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#21
