REQ-F-146business ruleThe system shall read the maintenance request file as one request per line, where column 1 is the action ('A' add, 'D' delete, 'U' update, '*' comment), columns 2-3 the numeric transaction type, and columns 4-53 the transaction description.AC-01

22. Set up reference data backupsdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 7 criteria

Sets up the backup history for the transaction type, transaction category and disclosure group reference data, and takes the first backup of each, so earlier versions can be recovered. At most five transaction type backups are kept, and the oldest is removed when a sixth is added. A backup must only be taken if the steps before it succeeded.

As an operations user, I want to create the backup generations for transaction type, category and disclosure group reference data, so that earlier versions of the reference data can be kept.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#22

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-147design noteThe system shall first define the transaction type backup generation group (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.BKUP), keeping at most 5 generations and deleting the oldest when a sixth is added, before any reference data is loaded.AC-01
REQ-F-148design noteWhen the step that defines the transaction type backup group ended with return code 0, the system shall copy the transaction type reference data (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.PS) into a new, cataloged first generation of the transaction type backup (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.BKUP), with fixed-length 60-byte records.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-149design noteWhen every earlier step of the setup job ended with return code 0, the system shall copy the transaction category reference data (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANCATG.PS) into a new, cataloged first generation of the transaction category backup (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANCATG.PS.BKUP), with fixed-length 60-byte records.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-150design noteWhen every earlier step of the setup job ended with return code 0, the system shall copy the disclosure group reference data (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS) into a new, cataloged first generation of the disclosure group backup (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.BKUP), with fixed-length 50-byte records.AC-06, AC-07

STEP60, which loads that group, is then skipped because of the earlier failure, so the job can leave an empty disclosure group backup group behind. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The new application needs versioned backup storage for the transaction type reference data, such as dated snapshots or object versions. It must keep at most 5 versions and remove the oldest automatically when a sixth is written. The retention policy has to exist before any backup is written. Prepare the transaction type backup
  • This is a setup step that runs only after the retention policy step succeeds. It copies the current transaction type extract (60-character records) into the first backup version and records it so later jobs can find it. Load first transaction type backup generation
  • This setup step runs only if every earlier step succeeded. It snapshots the current transaction category extract (60-character records) as the first backup version of the category data. Load first transaction category generation
  • This setup step runs only if every earlier step succeeded. It snapshots the current disclosure group extract (50-character records) as the first backup version of the disclosure group data. Load first disclosure group generation
23. Extract transaction types and categories to filesdraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 9 rules · 11 criteria · 2 gaps

Backs up the current transaction type and category files, then produces fresh copies from the database for downstream use such as the transaction report. Types are written in type code order and categories in type then category order, as fixed 60-character records. A failed unload must never leave a partial file behind.

As an operations user, I want to back up the current transaction type and category files and unload fresh copies from the database, so that downstream processing such as the transaction report has current reference data.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/CustomerDataSetup/TransactionTypeReferenceDataMaintenance#23

Open questions

  • SME-288 The transaction category unload runs if earlier steps ended with return code 4 or lower, while the other steps in the job need return code 0. Is the looser threshold intended, or should every step require return code 0? (Batch operations / application owner)
  • SME-289 The extract job removes the existing transaction type and category files between backup and rebuild. Should the modernized flow guarantee that a file is never removed unless its backup succeeded? (Batch operations / data owner)
  • SME-290 Who uses the transaction type and category extracts, and must the modernized extracts keep the exact fixed-length layout, including padding and trailing '0' characters? (Integration team)
  • DEF-136 Is this intended? Unlike every other step, the category unload runs when an earlier step ended with return code 4, so a warning in the transaction type unload still produces a category file while the earlier steps would have been skipped; the step's comment is also copied from the transaction type step. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The first step of the scheduled extract job copies the current transaction type file to a new backup version, under the retention policy set up for these backups, before any new file is produced. Back up previous transaction type file
  • This step runs only if every earlier step of the job succeeded. It copies the current transaction category file to a new backup version. The job needs step-level success tracking so this step can be skipped. Back up previous transaction category file
  • This is a sorted extract of the transaction type table in a fixed-width layout. Each record is the 2-character type code, the description padded to 50 characters, and eight '0' filler characters, 60 characters in total. Downstream readers depend on this exact layout. Unload transaction types to flat file
  • This is a sorted extract of the transaction category table in a fixed-width layout. Each record is the type code, the category code, the category description padded to 50 characters, and four '0' filler characters, 60 characters in total. Unload transaction categories to flat file
24. Load reference data into keyed filesdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria

Reloads the keyed transaction type and category lookup stores from their latest flat files, so online screens and batch programs read current reference data. Each store is emptied and rebuilt in full. Every record in the file must be loaded, with none lost and none left over from the previous load.

As an operations user, I want to reload the keyed transaction type and category files from their flat files, so that online and batch programs read current reference data.

Design notes

The store is cleared, then every 60-character record is loaded, keyed by its first 6 characters (type code plus category code). Other writers are kept out while it loads, and the source file is read without locking it. Load transaction categories into keyed store
  • A scheduled job does a full replace of the transaction type lookup store from the transaction type flat file. The store is cleared, then every 60-character record is loaded, keyed by its first 2 characters (the type code), so readers get a keyed lookup by type code. Other writers are kept out while it loads. Card Authorization and Fraud Management

1. Purge expired pending authorizationsdraft · scheduled job · 14 requirements · 12 rules · 18 criteria

A scheduled job for the card operations team that works through every account's pending authorization summary, deletes each authorization detail that has reached the expiry age, and reduces the account's approved or declined counts and totals for each deleted detail. It deletes a summary once its adjusted approved count is zero or below. It must never delete an authorization younger than the expiry days, and it must stop the run if a deletion fails instead of carrying on with the store half purged.

As a card operations team, I want pending authorizations that have reached their expiry age removed from the authorization database by a batch job, so that the pending authorization store holds only current authorizations.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001design noteThe system shall capture the current date, use the supplied expiry days when numeric or else default them to 5, and default the checkpoint frequency to 5 when it is spaces, 0 or low-values.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-N-001design noteThe system shall run the purge program (CBPAUP0C) as an IMS batch message program with program specification block PSBPAUTB, using the IMS PSB and DBD libraries.AC-04
REQ-F-002business ruleThe system shall run the expired-authorization purge job with the control values '00,00001,00001,Y', meaning authorizations 0 or more days old count as expired, a checkpoint is taken after more than 1 authorization summary is processed, every checkpoint is reported, and debug messages are on.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-003design noteThe system shall read each account's pending authorization summary in turn until the end of the database, check every authorization detail under that summary for expiry, delete each detail that qualifies, and then move on to the next summary.AC-07
REQ-F-004business ruleThe system shall work out each authorization's date as 99999 minus its stored inverted date key (Julian YYDDD), and its age as today's Julian date (YYDDD) minus that date.AC-08
REQ-F-005business ruleWhen an authorization's age is at least the expiry days, the system shall mark it as qualified for deletion.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-006business ruleWhen an authorization's age is less than the expiry days, the system shall mark it as not qualified and keep it.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-007business ruleWhen an authorization detail qualifies for deletion, the system shall delete it from the pending authorization detail segment (PAUTDTL1) and add 1 to the details-deleted count.AC-11
REQ-F-008error handlingIf deleting an authorization detail fails, then the system shall display 'AUTH DETAIL DELETE FAILED :' with the status and 'AUTH APP ID :' with the account, then display 'CBPAUP0C ABENDING ...' and end the run with return code 16.AC-12
REQ-F-009business ruleWhen an authorization detail qualifies for purge and its response code is '00' (approved), the system shall subtract 1 from the account summary's approved count and subtract the detail's approved amount from the summary's approved total.AC-13
REQ-F-010business ruleWhen an authorization detail qualifies for purge and its response code is anything other than '00', the system shall subtract 1 from the account summary's declined count and subtract the detail's transaction amount from the summary's declined total.AC-18
REQ-F-011business ruleThe system shall make the approved and declined count and total reductions in its working copy of the summary only and shall never rewrite the summary record.AC-13
REQ-F-012business ruleWhen all of an account summary's details have been checked and the adjusted approved authorization count is zero or below, the system shall delete the pending authorization summary from the summary store (DLI:PAUTSUM0).AC-14, AC-15, AC-16, AC-17
REQ-F-013business ruleIf deleting the pending authorization summary fails, then the system shall abend the run.AC-15, AC-16, AC-17

Open questions

  • SME-028 The authorization purge job receives the parameters '00,00001,00001,Y'. What does each value mean (for example expiry days or checkpoint frequency), and would '00' mean authorizations expire after zero days? (Card authorization operations)
  • SME-029 When should a pending-authorization summary be deleted: only when both the approved and declined counts are zero and no unexpired details remain under it? (Today the code checks the approved count twice.) (Card authorization business analyst)
  • DEF-004 Is this intended? The summary-delete test checks the approved count twice ('PA-APPROVED-AUTH-CNT <= 0 AND PA-APPROVED-AUTH-CNT <= 0'), so a summary is deleted when no approved authorizations remain even if declined ones do; the declined count was almost certainly meant for the second test. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-081 Is this intended? The age is a plain subtraction of YYDDD values, so across a year end it is wrong: an authorization dated 25365 checked on 26001 gets an age of 636 days and is purged after one day. Also, the shipped job passes '00' as expiry days, which is numeric, so the default of 5 is skipped and every detail is purged on every run. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-140 Is this intended? The job passes 00 expiry days, which CBPAUP0C accepts as numeric, so every authorization (including ones made today) qualifies for deletion instead of the program default of 5 days. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The job needs a parameter setup step at start-up: record today's date as the run date, take expiry days from the job parameters when numeric or else use 5, and set the checkpoint frequency to 5 when it is missing, blank or 0. Expose these as validated job configuration, not as positional text. Load run date and purge parameters
  • Run the purge as a scheduled batch job with write access to the pending authorization store (summaries and their details). The legacy IMS batch program, PSB and DBD library setup becomes the job's scheduler entry and its database credentials and permissions. Run the expired authorization purge program
  • The job needs a full pass over all pending authorization summaries, one account at a time, with each summary's child details checked and expired ones deleted before it moves to the next summary. Commit progress at the configured checkpoint frequency so the job can restart after a failure without starting over. Traverse summaries and purge expired details
2. Answer account inquiry requests from the queuedraft · online · 16 requirements · 18 rules · 20 criteria

A message service that answers account inquiry requests from other systems with the account's status, balances, limits and dates, so they never read the account file directly. Each request is answered on the account reply queue and matched to the request by its message and correlation ids. It must never answer a malformed or unknown-account request with account data, and it must never alter the stored values it reports.

As a requesting system, I want to send an account inquiry message and receive the account's details on a reply queue, so that I can see an account's status, balances and limits without direct file access.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-014design noteWhen the account inquiry transaction (CDRA) is started by an MQ trigger, the system shall read requests from the queue named in the trigger message, send replies to the queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' and send error records to the queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'.AC-01
REQ-F-015business ruleThe system shall take request messages one at a time, waiting up to 5 seconds for each, process and answer each one, and stop when no message arrives within 5 seconds, then close the queues it opened and end the task.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-N-002design noteThe system shall take each request and put its reply as one unit of work committed before the next request is taken, with the last request's unit of work committed when the task ends.AC-04
REQ-F-016design noteWhen a request is taken successfully, the system shall keep its message id and correlation id for the reply and read the first 4 characters as the function code and the next 11 digits as the account number.AC-05
REQ-F-017historical artifactThe system shall always send replies to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' and shall not use the reply-to queue named in the request.AC-06
REQ-F-018design noteWhen a reply is ready for the current request, the system shall put the reply on the account reply queue carrying the request's message and correlation identifiers.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-019design noteIf putting the reply fails, then the system shall record 'MQPUT ERR', publish the error and end the run.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-020business ruleIf the function code is not 'INQA' or the account number is zero or less, then the system shall reply 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : ' with the account number, followed by 'FUNCTION : ' with the function code, without reading the account file.AC-09
REQ-F-021business ruleWhen a request has function code 'INQA' and an account number greater than zero, the system shall read that account from the account file (ACCTDAT).AC-10
REQ-F-022formattingWhen the account is found, the system shall reply with 'ACCOUNT ID : ', 'ACCOUNT STATUS : ', 'BALANCE : ', 'CREDIT LIMIT : ', 'CASH LIMIT : ', 'OPEN DATE : ', 'EXPR DATE : ', 'REIS DATE : ', 'CREDIT BAL : ', 'DEBIT BAL : ' and 'GROUP ID : ', each followed by the stored value unchanged, the credit and debit balances being the current billing cycle's.AC-18
REQ-F-023formattingThe system shall show amounts in the reply as 12 digits with two implied decimal places, no decimal point and the sign carried in the last digit, exactly as stored.AC-19
REQ-F-024business ruleWhen the account is not on the account file, the system shall reply 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : ' followed by the 11-digit account number.AC-20
REQ-F-025error handlingIf reading the account file returns anything other than found or not found, then the system shall put an error record on 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' holding the message 'ERROR WHILE READING ACCTF' (cut to 25 characters), the file response and reason codes and the input queue name, send no reply, close the open queues and end the task, with the request just taken committed as consumed.AC-11, AC-12, AC-13
REQ-F-026error handlingIf taking a request fails for any reason other than no message being available, then the system shall put an error record with 'INP MQGET ERR:', the condition and reason codes and the input queue name on the error queue, close the open queues and end the task.AC-14
REQ-F-027error handlingIf the trigger data cannot be retrieved, or the input or reply queue cannot be opened, then the system shall put an error record ('CICS RETREIVE' with the response codes, 'INP MQOPEN ERR' or 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' respectively) on the error queue and end the task.AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-028error handlingIf the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' cannot be opened, then the system shall write 'ERR MQOPEN ERR' with the condition and reason codes to the job log and end the task.AC-17

Open questions

  • SME-048 For the account inquiry service, when should the work of reading a request and sending its reply be committed or rolled back: per request, at the end of the run, or on error? (Integration architecture team)
  • SME-049 What are the exact labels and layout for every field in the account inquiry reply? Only 'ACCOUNT ID : ' and 'BALANCE : ' are known. (Card authorization business analyst)
  • SME-050 Where do the function code and account number sit within an account inquiry request message, and how should a non-numeric account number be treated? (Integration architecture team)
  • SME-051 How should the account inquiry service handle an account file read failure other than 'not found', and failures opening or closing queues? What should the published error record contain? (Card authorization business analyst)
  • SME-052 How important is the account inquiry lookup and the content of its reply? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that is costly if it goes wrong? (Business owner (account servicing))
  • SME-053 Should account inquiry replies go to the reply queue the requester names, or always to the fixed queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT for every consumer? (Integration architect)
  • DEF-069 Is this intended? When the trigger data cannot be retrieved, the code moves the RESP2 code onto itself instead of into its display field, so the error record always shows a RESP2 of 00000000. Also, 'CICS RETREIVE' is misspelled in the error record. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-171 Is this intended? The error text 'ERROR WHILE READING ACCTFILE' (28 characters) is moved into a 25-character field, so the record says 'ERROR WHILE READING ACCTF'; the paragraph field is never filled on this path, and the request is consumed with no reply to the requester. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Run the service as a consumer started when messages arrive on the account inquiry request queue. Take the request queue from the start-up event or configuration, and send replies to the fixed queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' and error records to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'. Process inquiry requests until queue empty
  • Treat consuming one request and publishing its reply as one transaction, committed before the next request is taken. A failure then never loses a request or sends a reply twice, and the last request's transaction is committed when the consumer stops. Queue-driven request processing loop with per-message commit
  • Parse each request as fixed-position text: characters 1-4 are the function code and the next 11 digits are the account number. Keep the message id and correlation id so the reply can be matched to the request. Retrieve next inquiry request
  • Publish each reply to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' with the request's message id and correlation id, so the requester can match it. If the publish fails, record 'MQPUT ERR', send the error to the error queue and stop the consumer. Send reply to requester
3. Answer system date requests from the queuedraft · online · 11 requirements · 11 rules · 13 criteria

A message service that answers date requests from other systems with the host's current system date (mm-dd-yyyy) and time on the date reply queue. Each reply carries the request's message and correlation ids. It must never lose or double-answer a request, and it must report every queue failure to the error queue, or to the console if the error queue itself is unavailable.

As a requesting system, I want to send a date request message and receive the system date and time on a reply queue, so that I can obtain the host system's current date and time.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#3

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-029design noteWhen the date inquiry transaction (CDRD) is started by a message arriving on its request queue, the system shall read the triggering queue's name, use it as the request queue, and always use 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' as the reply queue.AC-01
REQ-F-030design noteWhen the date inquiry transaction starts, the system shall read and answer request messages one after another, committing each read-and-reply before reading the next, until no message arrives within 5 seconds, and then close its queues and end.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-031formattingWhen a date request message has been received, the system shall compose a reply reading 'SYSTEM DATE : <mm-dd-yyyy>SYSTEM TIME : <time>' from the current system clock and send it.AC-04
REQ-F-032design noteWhen a date reply has been composed, the system shall put it on 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' carrying the request's message ID and correlation ID, as a text-format message in the queue manager's code page, within the current unit of work, without using the requester's own reply-to queue.AC-05
REQ-F-033design noteWhen the date inquiry service ends, the system shall close each of the request, reply and error queues that it opened successfully, with no special close options, and then return control to CICS.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-034error handlingIf the trigger information cannot be retrieved at start-up, then the system shall send an error record with location 'CICS RETRIEVE' and the CICS response codes to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', close any open queues and end.AC-08
REQ-F-035error handlingIf reading a request fails for any reason other than no message being available, then the system shall send an error record 'INP MQGET ERR:' with the condition and reason codes and the request queue name to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', close its queues and end.AC-09
REQ-F-036error handlingIf putting the date reply fails, then the system shall send an error record with message 'MQPUT ERR', the condition and reason codes and the reply queue name to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', close its open queues and end.AC-10
REQ-F-037error handlingIf a queue operation fails, then the system shall put an error record (failing step text, condition code, reason code and queue name) as a text message on 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' within the unit of work, then close its open queues and end.AC-11
REQ-F-038error handlingIf the error queue itself cannot be opened or written to, then the system shall write the error record to the system console ('ERR MQOPEN ERR' or 'MQPUT ERR') and end.AC-12
REQ-F-039error handlingIf closing a queue fails, then the system shall record 'MQCLOSE ERR' with the condition and reason codes and run termination again, sending only a failed error-queue close to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'.AC-13

Open questions

  • SME-117 The date/time service's error messages contain old-platform texts such as 'CICS RETRIEVE' and 'MQPUT ERR'. Do downstream consumers of the error queue rely on these exact texts, or can they be replaced with neutral wording? (Operations / integration team)
  • SME-118 What exact time format must the date/time service's reply contain (separators, precision)? (Integration team)
  • SME-119 The date/time reply is built in a fixed-size buffer. Do consumers depend on a maximum reply length? (Integration team)
  • SME-120 The date/time reply service is filed under 'Card Authorization and Fraud Management'. Should it be moved to a different business function? (Business analyst)
  • SME-121 Is the content of the system date/time reply critical to the system's core purpose, or costly if wrong, so that it must be matched exactly? (Business owner)
  • SME-122 Should date/time replies go to the reply queue named by the requester instead of the fixed queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE, and should replies be matched to requests by the request's message ID instead of its correlation ID? (Integration architect)
  • SME-123 If the date/time service fails midway, should the request be put back on the queue to retry, instead of being consumed with no reply as today? (Operations / support lead)
  • SME-124 In the date/time service, is the 'reply queue open' flag (which actually tracks the input queue) only a naming quirk? And if closing a queue fails, should the transaction end without trying to close it again? (Technical lead / MQ administrator)
  • DEF-087 Is this intended? On a CICS RETRIEVE failure the second response code is moved onto itself instead of into its display field, so the error record always shows RESP2 as zero; also the requester's reply-to queue is saved but ignored, so all replies go to the fixed queue. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-166 Is this intended? A close failure re-performs termination while the open flags are still set, so it retries the same close recursively. A failed reply-queue close is labelled with the request queue name, and request/reply close failures are never sent to the error queue. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-172 Is this intended? The error-location field is set only for the trigger-retrieve failure, so for every queue failure the record's location is blank and the step can only be read from the message text. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Run the service as a consumer started when messages arrive on the date request queue. Read the request queue name from the start-up event, and always send replies to the fixed queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'. Identify request queue from trigger
  • Drain the queue: take requests one at a time, commit each read-and-reply as one transaction before taking the next, and stop once no message arrives within 5 seconds. Triggered drain-the-queue processing loop with per-message commit
  • Publish the reply as a text message to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' with the request's message id and correlation id, inside the same transaction as consuming the request. Ignore any reply-to address the request names. Send date reply to requester
  • On shutdown, release every queue connection (request, reply, error) that was opened successfully and leave the others alone, so connections are not leaked across runs. Queue open/close resource lifecycle at termination
4. Receive and prepare card authorization requestsdraft · online · 12 requirements · 12 rules · 15 criteria

The intake step for card authorization requests from the payment network. It takes each request message, parses it, and looks up the card's account, customer and pending authorization summary so a decision can be made. It must never send a reply based on a failed read of the account, customer or summary data, and it must convert the amount text exactly into the transaction amount.

As a card payment network, I want authorization request messages taken from the queue, parsed and matched to the card's account, customer and pending authorization summary, so that each request can be decided and answered.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-040design noteWhen triggered, the system shall process request messages one at a time, committing after each, and shall stop after 501 messages (the limit 500 is checked as 'more than'), leaving the rest on the queue for a later trigger.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-041design noteWhen no request message arrives within 5 seconds of a read, the system shall stop processing and end the task.AC-03
REQ-F-042design noteWhen a request message is received, the system shall split the comma-delimited request into its fields and convert the amount text into the numeric transaction amount.AC-15
REQ-F-043design noteWhen a card is found in the cross-reference, the system shall read the account master (ACCTDAT) using the account id from the cross-reference and mark the account found when it exists.AC-04
REQ-F-044error handlingWhen the account is not in the account master, the system shall mark it not found, log warning 'A002' with message 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF' and continue processing the request.AC-05
REQ-F-045error handlingIf reading the account master fails for any other reason, then the system shall log critical error 'C002' with message 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE', ending the task before a reply is sent for that request.AC-06
REQ-F-046design noteWhen a card is found in the cross-reference, the system shall read the customer master (CUSTDAT) using the customer id from the cross-reference and mark the customer found when it exists.AC-07
REQ-F-047error handlingWhen the customer is not in the customer master, the system shall mark it not found, log warning 'A003' with message 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF' and continue processing the request.AC-08
REQ-F-048error handlingIf reading the customer master fails for any other reason, then the system shall log critical error 'C003' with message 'FAILED TO READ CUST FILE', ending the task before a reply is sent for that request.AC-09
REQ-F-049design noteWhen a card is found in the cross-reference, the system shall read the pending authorization summary for the card's account and treat IMS status blank or 'FW' as found and 'GE' as not found.AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-050error handlingIf reading the pending authorization summary returns any other IMS status, then the system shall log critical error 'I002' with message 'IMS GET SUMMARY FAILED', ending the task before a reply is sent for that request.AC-12
REQ-F-051design noteWhen an authorization detail is about to be recorded, the system shall set the key date to 99999 minus the year/day value and the key time to 999999999 minus (time x 1000 + milliseconds).AC-13, AC-14

Open questions

  • SME-131 The authorization reply expiry is given as 50 with no unit. What unit and timeout should the new messaging platform use? (Integration team)
  • SME-132 In the pending authorization summary, an approval sets the cash balance to zero instead of adding to it, and the declined-amount total may not use the current request's amount. Is each of these intended, or is it a defect? (Card authorization product owner)
  • SME-133 Decline reasons 4200 (card not active), 4300 (account closed), 5100 (card fraud) and 5200 (merchant fraud) are defined, but nothing triggers them. Should these checks be implemented, and what data should drive them? (Card authorization product owner / fraud management team)
  • SME-134 The authorization summary is saved before the authorization detail is recorded, so if recording the detail fails, the totals already include it. Must the summary update and the detail record succeed or fail together? (Card authorization business owner)
  • SME-135 When a lookup during authorization logs a critical error (C001, C002, C003, I002), should the decision, reply and recording still go ahead for that request? (Card authorization business owner)
  • DEF-138 Is this intended? The summary found/not-found flag is never reset per message, so when a later request's card is not in the cross-reference (lookup skipped) the decision reuses the previous request's summary credit limit and balance and can approve an unknown card. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Each consumer run handles at most 501 messages (the limit of 500 is tested as 'more than'), committing after each message. Leave the remaining messages on the queue for the next start-up so one run cannot hold the queue indefinitely. Per-trigger processing limit and queue wait
  • Read the request queue with a 5-second wait, and end the run when no message arrives in that time. Per-trigger processing limit and queue wait
  • Provide a parser that splits the comma-delimited request into named fields and converts the amount text to an exact decimal (not floating point) transaction amount. Parse comma-delimited authorization request
  • Look up the account record by the account id taken from the card cross-reference, and return found or not found as a flag for the decision step. Look up account master record
  • Look up the customer record by the customer id taken from the card cross-reference, and return found or not found as a flag for the decision step. Look up customer master record
  • Look up the account's pending authorization summary by account id, with three outcomes: found, not found, or error. Only an error ends the task (critical 'I002'). The legacy IMS statuses blank/'FW' mean found and 'GE' means not found. Retrieve pending authorization summary
  • Authorization details must be read newest first. The legacy store did this with an inverted key: date = 99999 minus the YYDDD value, time = 999999999 minus (time x 1000 + milliseconds). The new store can use a descending index on the authorization timestamp, but any shared or migrated keys must keep this formula, because the purge works out an authorization's age from the inverted date. Compute inverted authorization timestamp key
5. Decide and reply to card authorization requestsdraft · online · 9 requirements · 7 rules · 9 criteria · 1 gap

The decision and reply step for card authorizations. It approves or declines each request against available credit (credit limit minus balance, taken from the pending summary when there is one, or else from the account) and sends the reply to the payment network in real time. It must never approve an amount strictly greater than the available credit, and a decline always carries response '05' with approved amount 0.

As a card payment network, I want each authorization request approved or declined against the account's available credit and answered on my reply queue, so that the merchant transaction can proceed or be refused in real time.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-052business ruleWhen the account has a pending-authorization summary, the system shall compute available credit as the summary credit limit minus the summary credit balance and shall decline for insufficient funds when the requested amount is strictly greater than that available credit.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-053business ruleWhen the account has no pending-authorization summary but the account record was found, the system shall compute available credit as the account credit limit minus the account current balance and shall decline for insufficient funds when the amount is strictly greater.AC-03
REQ-F-054business ruleWhen neither a pending-authorization summary nor the account record is found, the system shall decline the request without an insufficient-funds reason, the reply then carrying reason '3100' because the account is not found.AC-04
REQ-F-055business ruleWhen the authorization decision is decline ('D'), the system shall set response code '05' with approved amount 0, and default the reason to '0000'.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-056business ruleWhen the authorization decision is approve, the system shall set response code '00' with the full transaction amount as the approved amount, and default the reason to '0000'.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-057business ruleThe system shall carry the request's card number and transaction id in the authorization reply and shall use the request's authorization time as the authorization id code.AC-07
REQ-F-058formattingThe system shall format the authorization reply as comma-delimited text of card number, transaction id, authorization id, response code, reason code and approved amount (signed, two decimals), each followed by a comma.AC-09
REQ-F-059design noteWhen an authorization decision has been made, the system shall send the non-persistent reply with expiry 50 and the original correlation id through MQPUT1 to the requester's reply queue.AC-08
REQ-F-060design noteIf putting the authorization reply fails, then the system shall log critical error 'M004'.AC-08

Open questions

  • SME-131 The authorization reply expiry is given as 50 with no unit. What unit and timeout should the new messaging platform use? (Integration team)
  • SME-132 In the pending authorization summary, an approval sets the cash balance to zero instead of adding to it, and the declined-amount total may not use the current request's amount. Is each of these intended, or is it a defect? (Card authorization product owner)
  • SME-133 Decline reasons 4200 (card not active), 4300 (account closed), 5100 (card fraud) and 5200 (merchant fraud) are defined, but nothing triggers them. Should these checks be implemented, and what data should drive them? (Card authorization product owner / fraud management team)
  • SME-134 The authorization summary is saved before the authorization detail is recorded, so if recording the detail fails, the totals already include it. Must the summary update and the detail record succeed or fail together? (Card authorization business owner)
  • SME-135 When a lookup during authorization logs a critical error (C001, C002, C003, I002), should the decision, reply and recording still go ahead for that request? (Card authorization business owner)
  • DEF-001 Is this intended? The summary-found flag and the decline-reason flag are never reset between messages. When the summary read fails with an IMS error (I002), or the card is unknown, the check uses the summary flag and the limit and balance left over from the previous request in the same run. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-139 Is this intended? The STRING pointer for the reply (WS-RESP-LENGTH) starts at 1 and is never reset between messages, so from the second request in a task each reply is appended after the previous replies in the 200-byte buffer and sent with them; after about three replies the buffer overflows. The sent length is also one byte longer than the text. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Send each reply as a one-off, non-persistent message to the reply address named in the request, with the request's correlation id and a short time-to-live (expiry 50, which is 5 seconds in MQ's tenths of a second). This way stale replies expire instead of piling up. If the send fails, log critical error 'M004'. Send authorization reply message
6. Decide a card authorization requestdraft · online · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 13 criteria · 2 gaps

The rules that decide each card authorization for the card issuer: look up the card, then its account, customer and pending summary, and approve or decline with a clear reason code. Only known cards may be approved. A card, account or customer that is not found always declines with reason '3100', which takes precedence over insufficient funds ('4100'). Every request gets a reply, even when the card is unknown.

As a card issuer, I want each incoming card authorization request approved or declined against the card, account and customer records, so that only transactions for known cards are approved and every request gets a reply with a clear reason.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, card_data, money, security. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#6

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-061business ruleWhen an authorization request is processed, the system shall start from an approve decision and look up the card in the card cross-reference, and only when the card is found shall it read the account, the customer and the account's pending-authorization summary before deciding.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-062business ruleWhen the request is declined, the system shall reply with response code '05' and approved amount 0, and otherwise shall reply '00' with the full requested amount approved.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-063business ruleWhen the card is not in the card cross-reference, the system shall treat the card and its account as not found and decline the request with response '05', reason '3100' and approved amount 0.AC-05

Open questions

  • SME-131 The authorization reply expiry is given as 50 with no unit. What unit and timeout should the new messaging platform use? (Integration team)
  • SME-132 In the pending authorization summary, an approval sets the cash balance to zero instead of adding to it, and the declined-amount total may not use the current request's amount. Is each of these intended, or is it a defect? (Card authorization product owner)
  • SME-133 Decline reasons 4200 (card not active), 4300 (account closed), 5100 (card fraud) and 5200 (merchant fraud) are defined, but nothing triggers them. Should these checks be implemented, and what data should drive them? (Card authorization product owner / fraud management team)
  • SME-134 The authorization summary is saved before the authorization detail is recorded, so if recording the detail fails, the totals already include it. Must the summary update and the detail record succeed or fail together? (Card authorization business owner)
  • SME-135 When a lookup during authorization logs a critical error (C001, C002, C003, I002), should the decision, reply and recording still go ahead for that request? (Card authorization business owner)
  • DEF-001 Is this intended? The summary-found flag and the decline-reason flag are never reset between messages. When the summary read fails with an IMS error (I002), or the card is unknown, the check uses the summary flag and the limit and balance left over from the previous request in the same run. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-022 Is this intended? The summary-found flag is not reset for each message. For an unknown card, the decision uses the summary-found flag and the limit and balance left over from an earlier request in the same run of up to 500 messages, so an unknown card can be approved. A cross-reference read error (C001) also leaves the card marked as found, and processing goes on with whatever cross-reference data is in memory. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-023 Is this intended? A missing customer record does not cause a decline, but it takes precedence over the reason. A request declined for insufficient funds on an account whose customer is missing is reported as '3100' instead of '4100'. The flags are also never reset between messages. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

7. Record pending authorization summary and detaildraft · online · 9 requirements · 11 rules · 13 criteria · 2 gaps

Records every decided authorization for a known card, both in the account's pending authorization summary (counts, totals, limits, balances) and as a detail record with match status 'P' or 'D' and a blank fraud flag. These records drive later matching, review and purging. They must stay consistent: approved counts and amounts must only reflect approved authorizations, and nothing is recorded for unknown cards.

As a card issuer, I want every decided authorization for a known card recorded against the account's pending-authorization summary and as a detail record, so that approved and declined totals and balances are kept current for later matching and review.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, card_data, money, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#7

Open questions

  • SME-131 The authorization reply expiry is given as 50 with no unit. What unit and timeout should the new messaging platform use? (Integration team)
  • SME-132 In the pending authorization summary, an approval sets the cash balance to zero instead of adding to it, and the declined-amount total may not use the current request's amount. Is each of these intended, or is it a defect? (Card authorization product owner)
  • SME-133 Decline reasons 4200 (card not active), 4300 (account closed), 5100 (card fraud) and 5200 (merchant fraud) are defined, but nothing triggers them. Should these checks be implemented, and what data should drive them? (Card authorization product owner / fraud management team)
  • SME-134 The authorization summary is saved before the authorization detail is recorded, so if recording the detail fails, the totals already include it. Must the summary update and the detail record succeed or fail together? (Card authorization business owner)
  • SME-135 When a lookup during authorization logs a critical error (C001, C002, C003, I002), should the decision, reply and recording still go ahead for that request? (Card authorization business owner)
  • SME-136 If the database fails after an authorization request has been taken off the queue and answered, the request is lost. Is that acceptable, or must such authorizations be reconciled? (Card authorization operations lead)
  • DEF-002 Is this intended? The declined total adds the transaction amount from the detail segment buffer. That buffer is filled for the current request only later, in 8500-INSERT-AUTH, so it adds the previous recorded request's amount (or zero or garbage for the first one). Also, every approval resets the summary cash balance to 0. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-061 Is this intended? Summary and detail failures are only logged. The reply has already been sent, the detail insert goes ahead even after the summary update fails, and the SYNCPOINT at the end of each message commits whatever succeeded, so the summary and its details can fall out of step. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-084 Is this intended? The reply to the merchant is sent (without syncpoint) before the summary and detail are written, so when the summary save fails with I003 the merchant has already received the decision (possibly an approval) while no pending authorization summary or detail is recorded for it. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Save the pending authorization summary as an upsert keyed by account id: update it when it was found during lookup, or insert a new one when it did not exist. Report a failure as critical error 'I003' 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED'. Save pending authorization summary
  • Insert one authorization detail row as a child of the account's summary, built from the request and reply fields listed in the rule, and keyed so details are read newest first. Report a failure as critical error 'I004' 'IMS INSERT DETL FAILED'. Insert pending authorization detail record
8. Log errors and stop on critical failuresdraft · online · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Error handling for authorization processing, for operations analysts. Every error is written to the central error log. A warning lets processing continue, but a critical error releases the database and queue and ends the task. The processor must never keep going after a critical error, and requests not yet read must stay on the queue for a later run.

As an operations analyst, I want authorization processing errors logged and critical failures to stop processing safely, so that problems are traceable and unread requests are left for a later run.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#8

Requirements

REQ-F-080error handlingWhen any error is logged as critical, the system shall write the error record to the CSSL log, release the IMS database, close the request queue and end the task, leaving any unread request messages on the queue for a later trigger.AC-01
REQ-F-081error handlingWhen an error is logged as a warning, the system shall write the error record to the CSSL log and continue processing.AC-02

9. Inquire on an account's pending authorizationsdraft · online · 19 requirements · 21 rules · 24 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

The Pending authorizations screen for customer service operators. The operator enters a numeric Account ID and sees the customer's name, address, phone, credit and cash limits and pending authorization totals, with the first page of authorizations. The screen must reject blank or non-numeric Account IDs with the stated messages. It must show zero totals and no authorizations when the account has no pending summary, and it must say clearly which record (XREF, ACCT, CUST or AUTH Summary) was not found or failed to read.

As a customer service operator, I want to enter an account and see its customer, limits and pending-authorization totals, so that I can review the account's authorization activity.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#9

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-082formattingWhen the pending authorization summary is started with no session data, the system shall start a new session, mark it as re-entered and show an empty screen with the cursor on the account number field.AC-01
REQ-F-083business ruleWhen the summary screen is entered from another function for the first time, the system shall mark the session as re-entered, use the passed account number if it is numeric (otherwise treat it as not supplied), load the account details and first page of authorizations, and display the screen with a full erase.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-084business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter with the Account ID blank, the system shall flag an error, show 'Please enter Acct Id...', clear the working account, put the cursor on Account ID and load no account details or authorizations.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-085business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter with an Account ID that is not entirely numeric, the system shall show 'Acct Id must be Numeric ...', flag an error, clear the working account, put the cursor on Account ID and load no account details or authorizations.AC-06
REQ-F-086business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter with a numeric Account ID, the system shall save it as the current account for the session, process any row selection, reset to the first page, and reload the account details and the first five pending authorizations.AC-07
REQ-F-087formattingWhen the Enter processing completes, the system shall redisplay the screen with the Account ID field showing the accepted account, or blank when the entry was rejected.AC-08
REQ-F-088design noteWhen a numeric account number is present, entered with Enter or passed in from the menu, the system shall look up the account's card cross-reference, account record, customer record and pending-authorization summary, and shall load the first page of authorizations only when a summary exists for the account.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-089design noteWhen the card cross-reference for the account is found, the system shall save the customer ID and card number from it in the session for later screens.AC-11
REQ-F-090formattingThe system shall show the customer name as the first word of the first name, a space, the middle initial, a space, and the last name.AC-19
REQ-F-091formattingThe system shall show address line 1 as address lines 1 and 2 joined by a comma, and address line 2 as address line 3, the state code and the first 5 digits of the ZIP code joined by commas, cutting each address line at its first double space.AC-20
REQ-F-092formattingThe system shall show the customer ID, the first phone number, and the account's credit limit and cash credit limit from the account master as signed amounts with two decimals.AC-12
REQ-F-093formattingWhen a pending authorization summary exists for the account, the system shall show its approved count, declined count, approved amount, declined amount, credit balance and cash balance.AC-13, AC-14, AC-15
REQ-F-094formattingWhen no pending authorization summary exists for the account, the system shall show the approved and declined counts and amounts and the credit and cash balances as zero, and shall not list any authorizations.AC-14, AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-095error handlingIf reading the pending authorization summary fails for any reason other than not found, then the system shall flag an error, show ' System error while reading AUTH Summary: Code:' followed by the database status code, put the cursor on Account ID and show the totals as zero.AC-21
REQ-F-096error handlingIf no card cross-reference exists for the account, then the system shall show 'Account:<account> not found in XREF file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>', and on any other read failure of file CXACAIX shall flag an error and show 'Account:<account> System error while reading XREF file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>'.AC-22
REQ-F-097error handlingIf the account record is not on the account file, then the system shall show 'Account:<account> not found in ACCT file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>', and on any other read failure of file ACCTDAT shall flag an error and show 'Account:<account> System error while reading ACCT file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>'.AC-23
REQ-F-098error handlingIf the customer record is not on the customer file, then the system shall show 'Customer:<customer> not found in CUST file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>', and on any other read failure of file CUSTDAT shall flag an error and show 'Customer:<customer> System error while reading CUST file. Resp:<code> Reas:<code>'.AC-24
REQ-F-099business ruleWhen the user presses PF3 on the summary screen, the system shall transfer control to the main menu (COMEN01C), passing the session data.AC-17
REQ-F-100business ruleIf the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF7 or PF8, then the system shall flag an error and redisplay the screen with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' and the cursor on the account number field.AC-18

Open questions

  • SME-137 On the pending-authorizations list screen, the PF3 (exit) key is accepted but nothing says what it does. Where should PF3 take the user? (Business analyst)
  • SME-138 When an account typed on the pending-authorizations screen has no card cross-reference, account record or customer record, a 'not found' message appears but the inquiry carries on. Should a missing record stop the inquiry so no authorization list is shown, or should the screen still show whatever authorization data exists for that account ID? (Customer service operations lead)
  • SME-139 When a page of pending authorizations is full, the system reads one more record ahead. What rule should decide that there is a next page, so that forward paging (PF8) is allowed? (Business analyst)
  • SME-140 Please confirm: when the card cross-reference lookup succeeds, the account ID and customer ID it returns are the ones used to look up the account and the customer. (Business analyst)
  • DEF-005 Is this intended? When the summary read fails, the program sends the screen from inside the read paragraph and then sends it again from the main flow, so the operator gets two screen sends in one task. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-024 Is this intended? The Account ID field is 11 characters with no numeric or justify attribute. An account typed without its leading zeros (for example '1') keeps trailing blanks, fails the numeric test and gets 'Acct Id must be Numeric ...'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-025 Is this intended? When a lookup fails, the program sends the screen with the error but keeps going: it still reads the account file using the account number left over from the failed cross-reference read, then the customer file, and sends the screen again, so a later message can overwrite the first one. 'Not found' cases also do not set the error flag, while system errors do. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The screen's load endpoint does keyed lookups in order: card cross-reference by account id (an alternate index on account), account by account id, customer by the customer id from the cross-reference, then pending authorization summary by account id. It fetches the first page of authorizations only when a summary exists. Gather account and authorization details
  • Keep the customer id and card number from the cross-reference in the operator's session state, so the detail and fraud screens can use them without looking them up again. Look up card cross-reference by account
10. Page through an account's pending authorizationsdraft · online · 8 requirements · 10 rules · 13 criteria · 2 screens

Lets customer service operators page forward (PF8) and back (PF7) through an account's pending authorizations five at a time. Each row shows 'A' for approved (response '00') or 'D' for declined, with amount, date, time, transaction id, type and match status. Paging must never skip or repeat authorizations, and the operator sees the stated message at the top or bottom of the list.

As a customer service operator, I want to page forward and back through an account's pending authorizations five at a time, with each shown as approved or declined, so that I can review every authorization on the account.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money, reporting_only. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#10

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-101business ruleWhen a page of authorizations is loaded and no error is flagged, the system shall read up to 5 pending authorizations for the account into the list rows (on backward paging starting at the saved first key of that page), remember each page's first key and the last key shown, then read one more ahead to set whether a next page exists.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-102design noteWhen the user pages forward (PF8), the system shall re-read the account's authorization summary and reposition at the last authorization shown when one exists, otherwise clear the start key.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-103business ruleWhen the user presses PF8 and a next page exists, the system shall clear the five list rows, load the next page of up to 5 pending authorizations and redisplay the screen without a full erase.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-104business ruleWhen the user presses PF8 and no further page of authorizations exists, the system shall keep the current list and show 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'.AC-07
REQ-F-105business ruleWhen the operator presses PF7 and the current page number is greater than 1, the system shall step the page number back by one, reposition to the saved first authorization key of that page, and redisplay up to five authorizations starting from that key without erasing the screen.AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-106business ruleWhen the operator presses PF7 and the current page number is 1 or less, the system shall show 'You are already at the top of the page...' and leave the list unchanged.AC-10
REQ-F-107business ruleWhen an authorization is placed in the summary list, the system shall show it as approved 'A' when its response code is '00' and as declined 'D' for any other response code.AC-11, AC-12

Open questions

  • SME-137 On the pending-authorizations list screen, the PF3 (exit) key is accepted but nothing says what it does. Where should PF3 take the user? (Business analyst)
  • SME-138 When an account typed on the pending-authorizations screen has no card cross-reference, account record or customer record, a 'not found' message appears but the inquiry carries on. Should a missing record stop the inquiry so no authorization list is shown, or should the screen still show whatever authorization data exists for that account ID? (Customer service operations lead)
  • SME-139 When a page of pending authorizations is full, the system reads one more record ahead. What rule should decide that there is a next page, so that forward paging (PF8) is allowed? (Business analyst)
  • SME-140 Please confirm: when the card cross-reference lookup succeeds, the account ID and customer ID it returns are the ones used to look up the account and the customer. (Business analyst)
  • SME-141 Backward paging (PF7) seems unable to go back more than one page. Is that what happens in production? How many pages should be supported for accounts with more than 100 pending authorizations? (Customer service operations lead)
  • SME-142 An authorization shows as Approved ('A') only when its response code is '00'. Every other code shows as Declined ('D'), on both the list and the detail screens. Is this rule critical to the system's core purpose, and would getting it wrong be costly? (Card authorization product owner)
  • DEF-062 Is this intended? After PF7 has repositioned, the page-forward loop adds 1 to the page number again when it reads the first row, and it overwrites that page's saved first key with the key of the page just shown. Example: from page 2, PF7 shows page 1, but the stored page number goes back to 2. A second PF7 shows page 1 again instead of 'You are already at the top of the page...'. From page 3 or later, repeated PF7 presses keep showing the same page, so the operator can only go back one page. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Use keyset (cursor) pagination over the account's authorizations in newest-first order. For a forward page, start after the last authorization key shown, or from the beginning when there is none. Keep the cursor in session state, not as a page offset. Position forward paging start key
  • For the next page, fetch up to 5 authorizations after the cursor and replace the list rows entirely, so rows from the previous page never remain. Fetch one more to work out whether a further page exists, and keep each page's first key so backward paging works. Show next authorization page
11. Select an authorization for detaildraft · online · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 4 criteria · 2 screens · 2 gaps

Lets a customer service operator mark one listed authorization with 'S' (or 's') to open its details on the Authorization details screen. Only the first marked row from the top counts. Any other selection code shows 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S' and the list is redisplayed, never an unintended record.

As a customer service operator, I want to mark one listed authorization with 'S' to open its details, so that I can examine a specific authorization.

12. View authorization detail and mark frauddraft · online · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 6 criteria · 2 screens

The Authorization details screen for fraud analysts. It shows a selected authorization with its response ('A' in green for '00', otherwise 'D' in red) and its reason as code and description. With PF5 the analyst reports the authorization as fraud or withdraws a fraud report. A toggle must always act on a freshly re-read record: 'F' becomes 'R' (remove fraud) and anything else becomes 'F' (report fraud), and the record goes to fraud processing with its account and customer number.

As a fraud analyst, I want to see an authorization's details with its decline reason and toggle its fraud mark, so that suspected fraud can be reported or withdrawn.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#12

REQ-F-114business ruleWhen the user presses PF5 on the selected authorization, the system shall re-read the authorization and, if its fraud flag is 'F', set it to 'R' with a remove-fraud action 'R', otherwise set it to 'F' with a report-fraud action 'F', and pass the record with account and customer number to the fraud processor (COPAUS2C).AC-03, AC-04, AC-05

13. View pending authorization detailsdraft · online · 12 requirements · 14 rules · 15 criteria · 2 screens · 2 gaps

Lets a card operations user open one pending authorization from an account's list and see all of it: card, date and time, approved amount, expiry, transaction and merchant details, and fraud status. It must always show the authorization that was selected for that account, with dates, times and amounts formatted exactly. When the account or selection is invalid, or the data cannot be read, it must show blank fields instead of stale or partial data.

As a card operations user, I want to open a selected pending authorization and see its full details, so that I can review the transaction, merchant and fraud status of the authorization.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches card_data, money. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#13

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-115business ruleWhen the authorization detail screen is first opened from the pending authorization list, or the user presses Enter, the system shall read the selected authorization for the account and display its details.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-116formattingWhen a selected authorization has been read without error, the system shall show the card number, the original authorization date (stored as YYMMDD) as MM/DD/YY and the original time (stored as HHMMSS) as HH:MM:SS.AC-10
REQ-F-117formattingWhen a selected authorization has been read without error, the system shall show the approved amount right-aligned with two decimals and a leading '-' when it is negative.AC-11
REQ-F-118formattingWhen a selected authorization has been read without error, the system shall show the card expiry date (stored as four characters) as the first two characters, '/', and the last two characters.AC-12
REQ-F-119formattingWhen a selected authorization has been read without error, the system shall show the processing code, POS entry mode, message source, merchant category code, authorization type, transaction ID, match status, and the merchant name, ID, city, state and ZIP as stored.AC-13
REQ-F-120formattingWhen the authorization is shown and its fraud flag is 'F' (fraud confirmed) or 'R' (fraud removed), the system shall show the flag, '-', and the fraud report date, and otherwise shall show '-'.AC-04
REQ-F-121business ruleIf the account id passed in is not numeric or no authorization is selected (spaces or low-values), then the system shall not read the database, set the error flag and show the screen with all authorization detail fields blank and no message.AC-05, AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-122business ruleIf a database read error occurred (error flag on), then the system shall leave the authorization detail fields blank.AC-05
REQ-F-123design noteThe system shall first read the account's pending authorization summary by account id and, only when that read succeeds (status blank or 'FW'), read the authorization detail under that account whose key matches the selected key.AC-08
REQ-F-124error handlingIf the summary or the detail is not found (status 'GE') or the end of the database is reached (status 'GB'), then the system shall mark that no authorizations remain and skip any further read, without an error message.AC-09
REQ-F-125error handlingIf reading the authorization summary returns any status other than success, not found or end of database, then the system shall set the error flag and show ' System error while reading Auth Summary: Code:' followed by the status code.AC-14
REQ-F-126error handlingIf reading the authorization detail returns any status other than success, not found or end of database, then the system shall set the error flag and show ' System error while reading Auth Details: Code:' followed by the status code.AC-15

Open questions

  • SME-143 On the authorization detail screen, what should happen (a) when the screen is opened without any data from the screen that called it, and (b) when the user presses PF3 after the screen is already showing? (Authorization business analyst)
  • SME-150 Should the authorization detail screen show the approved amount (current behavior) or the requested transaction amount, especially for declined or partly approved authorizations? Is the card expiry stored as MMYY? (Customer service operations lead)
  • DEF-017 Is this intended? When the account summary or the selected authorization detail is not found, the read sets only the end-of-data flag, not the error flag, so the detail screen is filled from whatever happens to be in the record area (blank or a previous record) and no 'not found' message is shown. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-026 Is this intended? When the summary or the selected detail is not found ('GE'/'GB'), the error flag stays off, so the screen is filled from whatever detail record is in memory, with no 'not found' message; and on a read error the screen is sent once inside the read routine and again by the main flow. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Retrieval is a two-step keyed lookup: first fetch the account's pending authorization summary by account id, and only if it exists fetch the authorization detail belonging to that account whose key equals the selected authorization key. A detail must never be returned without its parent summary, and lookup by key alone (ignoring the account) is not allowed. 'Not found' at either step is a normal outcome, not an error. Read authorization summary by account
14. Navigate the authorization detail screendraft · online · 6 requirements · 8 rules · 8 criteria · 2 screens

Lets a card operations user move around the authorization detail screen: step to the next pending authorization of the same account, go back to the pending authorization list, or refresh the current one. It must stay within the same account when stepping forward and keep the current selection when there is nothing further. It must never show details from a failed read.

As a card operations user, I want to use function keys on the authorization detail screen to move to the next authorization or return to the list, so that I can work through an account's pending authorizations.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#14

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-127design noteWhen the detail program starts with no data passed from a calling screen, the system shall transfer control to the authorization summary program (COPAUS0C).AC-01
REQ-F-128business ruleWhen the user presses PF3 on the detail screen, the system shall return to the authorization summary list (COPAUS0C).AC-02
REQ-F-129business ruleWhen the user presses PF8 on the detail screen, the system shall re-read the selected authorization of the account, fetch the next authorization under the same account, make it the selected authorization and display its details.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-130business ruleWhen the user presses PF8 and there is no further authorization for the account, the system shall keep the current selection and show 'Already at the last Authorization...' without erasing the screen.AC-05

REQ-F-132business ruleWhen the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF5 or PF8, the system shall re-read and redisplay the selected authorization as for Enter, with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.AC-06, AC-07

Design notes

  • The detail view can only be reached with an account and a selected authorization supplied by the pending authorization list. If it is opened directly without that context (e.g. a deep link or a fresh session), the application must redirect the user to the pending authorization list instead of showing an empty detail page. 15. Mark or unmark an authorization as frauddraft · online · 10 requirements · 14 rules · 17 criteria · 2 screens

Lets a card operations user mark a pending authorization as fraud, or remove a fraud mark, with one action on the detail screen. The fraud register and the authorization record must change together or not at all: a partial update where one says fraud and the other does not must never be left behind. The user must be told clearly whether the authorization was marked fraud, had fraud removed, or the change was rolled back.

As a card operations user, I want to press PF5 on an authorization to report fraud or remove a fraud mark, so that suspected fraudulent authorizations are flagged consistently in the authorization record and the fraud register.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, card_data, personal_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#15

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-133business ruleWhen the user presses PF5 on the authorization detail screen and the selected authorization is marked fraud ('F'), the system shall set its fraud flag to 'R' (fraud removed) and request the fraud action 'R' (remove fraud).AC-01, AC-02, AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-134business ruleWhen the user presses PF5 on the authorization detail screen and the selected authorization is not marked fraud (blank or 'R'), the system shall set its fraud flag to 'F' (fraud confirmed) and request the fraud action 'F' (report fraud).AC-02, AC-03, AC-04, AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-135design noteThe system shall send the whole authorization record, the account number, the customer number and the fraud action to the fraud update program (COPAUS2C).AC-15
REQ-F-136business ruleThe system shall set the fraud report date on the authorization record returned by the fraud update program to today's date in MM/DD/YY form with separators, which the detail screen then saves on the pending authorization and displays.AC-16
REQ-F-137business ruleWhen the fraud update program completes normally and reports success ('S'), the system shall replace the pending authorization detail record (PAUTDTL1) with the record carrying the toggled fraud flag and the fraud report date set by the fraud update program.AC-07, AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-138business ruleWhen the replace of the authorization detail succeeds (status blank or 'FW'), the system shall commit the fraud register change and the authorization detail change together and show 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' if the flag is now 'R', otherwise 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...'.AC-07, AC-08, AC-10, AC-11
REQ-N-003error handlingIf the replace of the authorization detail returns any other status, then the system shall roll back both the fraud register change and the authorization detail change, set the error flag and show ' System error while FRAUD Tagging, ROLLBACK||' followed by the database status code.AC-17
REQ-F-139error handlingIf the fraud update program completes but reports failure, then the system shall roll back, leave the authorization detail unchanged and show the fraud program's message (for example ' SYSTEM ERROR DB2: CODE:…').AC-12
REQ-F-140error handlingIf the link to the fraud update program does not complete normally, then the system shall roll back and leave the authorization detail unchanged, without setting any message.AC-13
REQ-F-141business ruleWhen a PF5 fraud action finishes, the system shall redisplay the same authorization's details.AC-02, AC-14
