Open questions

  • SME-143 On the authorization detail screen, what should happen (a) when the screen is opened without any data from the screen that called it, and (b) when the user presses PF3 after the screen is already showing? (Authorization business analyst)
  • SME-144 When the request to mark or unmark an authorization as fraud does not complete normally, what should the operator see, and what state should the authorization be left in? (Authorization business analyst)
  • SME-145 When adding or updating a fraud record fails for any reason other than a duplicate record, what status and message should go back to the operator? (Fraud management team)
  • SME-146 The fraud update is written to the fraud store first, then to the authorization detail record. If the second write fails after the first has succeeded, nothing is rolled back. Must both updates succeed or fail together? (Architecture team)
  • SME-147 When an authorization's fraud flag is changed, which data stores must hold the new fraud flag and fraud report date: the authorization detail record, the fraud store, or both? (Data architect)
  • SME-148 If the fraud update reports success but the authorization's database status is neither blank nor 'FW', what message should the system show? (Business analyst)
  • SME-149 Please confirm: after the fraud flag is changed, the system sends a fraud update request with the updated authorization record, the account ID and the customer ID, to be recorded in the authorization fraud store (CARDDEMO.AUTHFRDS). (Business analyst)
  • DEF-056 Is this intended? If the link to the fraud program itself fails, the screen rolls back the change but sets no message, so the user sees the detail screen again with no word that the fraud action was not recorded. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Marking or unmarking fraud calls a separate fraud-recording service, passing the full authorization, account number, customer number and the requested action ('F' or 'R'). The service stamps today's date (MM/DD/YY) as the fraud report date on the authorization it returns and reports success or failure with a message. This call and the save of the authorization record must run in one transaction (or an equivalent saga with compensation) so both commit or both roll back. Submit fraud action to fraud processor
16. Record fraud action in the fraud registerdraft · online · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria · 2 screens

Keeps the fraud register for fraud analysts: each fraud report or removal is recorded against the card and the exact authorization, with the action and today's date. There must be exactly one current fraud record per card and authorization timestamp; a repeat action updates it rather than adding a second one. Failures must be returned with the database code and state, never silently ignored.

As a fraud analyst, I want each fraud report or removal to be recorded against the card and authorization in the fraud register, so that there is one current fraud record per authorization with its report date.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, card_data, personal_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#16

Design notes

  • The pending authorization stores its time in complemented form (999999999 minus the time) so newest sorts first. The fraud register needs the real timestamp, so the new application must convert back (999999999 minus the stored value) and combine it with the original authorization date. Card number plus that timestamp is the unique key of a fraud record; if the new data model stores the real time directly, the conversion goes away but the key must stay the same. Rebuild authorization timestamp from stored key
17. Unload the pending authorization databasedraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 10 rules · 10 criteria

A batch job for operations that copies the whole pending authorization database out to extract files: each account summary followed by all of its authorization details. Only summaries with a numeric account id are written, and a detail is never written without its summary. Any unexpected read or write failure must stop the run with return code 16 and a clear message, so a partly written extract is never mistaken for a complete one.

As a batch operations team member, I want to unload the pending authorization database to extract files, so that the summaries and their details can be kept or reloaded outside the online system.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#17

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-147design noteThe system shall run the IMS unload utility (DFSURGU0, parameters ULU, DFSURGU0, DBPAUTP0) reading the pending authorization database (OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDB) and its index (OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDBX) in shared mode, and write a new cataloged extract (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.IMSDATA.DBPAUTP0) of variable-length records up to 27990 bytes, deleted if the step fails.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-148design noteThe system shall read the pending authorization summaries (segment 'PAUTSUM0') one after another and, for each whose account id is numeric, write the summary to the summary unload file and then unload all of that summary's details.AC-03
REQ-F-149business ruleIf a pending authorization summary's account id is not numeric, then the system shall skip it without writing it or any of its details.AC-06
REQ-F-150design noteWhen reading summaries reaches the end of the database (status 'GB'), the system shall stop reading and finish the run.AC-04
REQ-F-151design noteWhile unloading a summary, the system shall read each detail under it (segment 'PAUTDTL1') in turn and write every detail read successfully to the detail unload file.AC-05
REQ-F-152design noteWhen reading details reaches the end of the current summary (status 'GE'), the system shall print 'CHILD SEG FLAG GE : Y', stop reading details and clear the read status so the next summary can be read.AC-07
REQ-F-153error handlingIf reading the next pending authorization summary returns any status other than blank or 'GB', then the system shall print 'AUTH SUM GN FAILED :' with the status and the key feedback, print 'DBUNLDGS ABENDING ...', set return code 16 and end, leaving the unload files partly written.AC-08
REQ-F-154error handlingIf reading the next detail of a summary returns any status other than blank or 'GE', then the system shall print 'GNP CALL FAILED :' with the status and the key feedback, set return code 16 and end.AC-09
REQ-F-155error handlingIf writing a pending authorization summary or detail to its unload file returns a non-blank status, then the system shall print 'GSAM PARENT FAIL :' with the status and key feedback, set return code 16 and end.AC-10

Open questions

  • SME-244 Who uses the pending authorization extract, and must the new extract keep the legacy unload format exactly for them? (Card authorization team)
  • SME-245 In the pending authorization unload, is the 'summary output file' the authorization root file and the 'detail output file' the authorization child file? (Card authorization data owner)
  • SME-246 In the pending authorization unload, which read results mean 'no more summaries' or 'no more details', and which other read results must stop the run as a failure? (Card authorization data owner)
  • SME-247 When the pending authorization unload fails it ends with code 16. Does the batch schedule depend on that code, so the new system must keep it? (Batch operations)
  • SME-248 Authorization summaries with a non-numeric account number are skipped silently during the unload. Should the new unload report or log them? (Card authorization data owner)
  • DEF-085 Is this intended? A failed write to the detail unload file prints 'GSAM PARENT FAIL :', the same text as a failed summary write, so an operator cannot tell which file failed. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Needs a scheduled full-database export of pending authorizations that reads the live data without locking out online users, writes a new variable-length extract (records up to 27990 bytes) under a fixed name, and removes the extract if the job fails so no partial file is left registered as complete. Unload pending authorization database to extract
  • The export walks all account summaries in storage order and, for each with a numeric account id, writes the summary and then all its details, so every detail follows its parent summary in the output. In a relational model this is an ordered scan of summaries joined to their details. Unload each pending authorization summary
  • Reaching the end of the summaries is the normal finish of the export, not an error; the job completes successfully. Unload each pending authorization summary
  • For each exported summary, every detail belonging to that account is read in turn and each successfully read detail is written to the detail export file. Unload each pending authorization detail
  • Running out of details for a summary is normal: log 'CHILD SEG FLAG GE : Y', reset the per-summary state and move on to the next summary. It must not be treated as an error or stop the job. Unload each pending authorization detail
18. Load pending authorizations into the databasedraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 9 rules · 12 criteria

A batch job for operations that fills or rebuilds the pending authorization database from a summary file and a detail file. All summaries are loaded first, then each detail is attached to the summary with the same account ID; details with a non-numeric or unknown account are skipped. An unexpected insert failure must stop the load with return code 16 so a broken load is never reported as done.

As a batch operations team member, I want to load pending authorization summaries and their details from files into the database, so that the pending authorization database can be populated or rebuilt.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#18

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-156design noteThe system shall run the load program (PAUDBLOD) as an IMS batch message program with parameter 'BMP,PAUDBLOD,PSBPAUTB', under program specification PSBPAUTB, giving it in shared mode the pending-authorization root segment file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.FILEO) and child segment file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.FILEO) to insert into the database.AC-01
REQ-F-157design noteThe system shall load every pending authorization summary record from the summary file first, and only then read the detail file and attach each detail to its summary.AC-02, AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-158business ruleIf a detail record's account ID is not numeric, then the system shall skip the record without inserting it and without any message, and read the next detail record.AC-06
REQ-F-159business ruleWhen a detail record has a numeric account ID, the system shall find the pending authorization summary with that account ID and, when found, insert the detail as a child authorization detail (PAUTDTL1) under that summary.AC-07
REQ-F-160error handlingIf no summary is found for a detail record's account ID (the lookup returns any non-blank status), then the system shall skip that detail without inserting it, without an error message and without ending the run.AC-08
REQ-F-161error handlingWhen the detail insert returns a blank status, the system shall display 'CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS'.AC-09
REQ-F-162error handlingWhen the detail insert returns 'II' (already in the database), the system shall display 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB', leave the existing detail unchanged and continue.AC-09
REQ-F-163error handlingIf the detail insert returns any status other than blank or 'II', then the system shall display 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD:' with the status and the key feedback area, display 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' and stop the load with return code 16.AC-12
REQ-F-164error handlingWhen reading the detail file returns end of file (status '10'), the system shall stop reading details.AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-165error handlingIf reading the detail file returns any non-success status other than end of file, then the system shall display 'ERROR READING CHILD SEG INFILE' and try the next read.AC-10, AC-11

  • INFILE1 (summary records): 3 records; INFILE2 (detail records): 5 records → All 3 pending authorization summary records are inserted first (each showing 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS'); only after INFILE1 reaches end of file (status '10') are the 5 detail records read and inserted under their summaries ('CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS').

Open questions

  • SME-270 When the pending-authorization reload reads a detail record that cannot be attached to a summary — because no matching summary exists or because its account key is not numeric — what should happen: skip it, reject it to an error output and report it, or stop the job? Today the record is dropped without any message. (Authorization business owner)
  • SME-271 When the pending-authorization reload tries to insert a summary or detail that already exists (duplicate key), should that be silently accepted, counted, or reported? (Authorization business owner)
  • DEF-027 Is this intended? A failed parent lookup is never reported: because the status check at line 310 sits inside the GU-success branch, a detail whose summary is not found (e.g. 'GE') is dropped with no message and no abend, and the 'ROOT GU CALL FAIL' message can never appear (the insert path already abends in 3200). Also, a detail-file read error other than '10' does not set end-of-file, so the read loop may repeat the error indefinitely. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Needs a scheduled load job that takes two input files, the summary file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.FILEO) and the detail file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.FILEO), and inserts their contents into the live pending authorization store while it stays available to other users. Load pending authorizations from root and child files
  • The load runs in two passes: the whole summary file to its end, then the whole detail file to its end. Details are never processed before all summaries are in, so each detail can find its parent. Sequence summary then detail loading
  • Same two-pass order: details are attached to their summary by account ID only after every summary has been loaded. In a relational model this is the parent table loaded before the child table, with the account ID as the foreign key. A detail record is attached to its summary by account ID and needs a numeric key
19. Load pending authorization summariesdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Loads each account's pending authorization summary from the summary file into the database for operations. A summary already held for an account must be left unchanged, never overwritten. Any other insert failure must stop the load with return code 16.

As an operations analyst, I want to load pending authorization summaries from the summary file into the pending authorization database, so that each account's pending authorization summary is available without overwriting a summary already held.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, updates_records. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#19

REQ-F-168error handlingIf a summary insert returns 'II' because that account's summary is already in the database, then the system shall display 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB', leave the existing summary unchanged and continue with the next record.AC-02
REQ-F-169error handlingIf a summary insert returns any status other than blank or 'II', then the system shall display 'ROOT INSERT FAILED :' with the status, display 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' and stop the load with return code 16.AC-03

20. Unload all pending authorizationsdraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 10 criteria

Unloads every pending authorization summary and every detail to two files for operations, with no filtering by age, expiry, response or match status. Each detail record carries its parent account id so it can be linked back. Only summaries with a numeric account id are written, and any unexpected read failure must end the run with return code 16.

As an operations analyst, I want every pending authorization summary and its details unloaded from the pending authorization database to files, so that the full set of pending authorizations is available outside the database with each detail linked to its account.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#20

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-170business ruleThe system shall unload every summary and every detail in the pending authorization database, with no filter on authorization age, expiry, response or match status.AC-01
REQ-F-171design noteWhile the end of the pending authorization database has not been reached, the system shall read the next authorization summary in database order and handle it before reading the next one.AC-02
REQ-F-172business ruleWhen a summary is read successfully and its account id is numeric, the system shall write the summary unchanged to the summary unload file and then unload every authorization detail under that summary.AC-03
REQ-F-173design noteThe system shall write each summary to the summary unload file as its 100-byte database image, unchanged.AC-04
REQ-F-174business ruleIf a summary is read successfully but its account id is not a valid number, then the system shall write neither the summary nor any of its details, give no message, and go on to the next summary.AC-05
REQ-F-175design noteWhen reading the next summary reports end of database ('GB'), the system shall stop reading summaries, close both unload files and end normally.AC-06
REQ-F-176error handlingIf reading a summary returns a status other than blank or 'GB', then the system shall display 'AUTH SUM GN FAILED :' with the status and the key feedback area, display 'IMSUNLOD ABENDING ...', and end with return code 16 without closing the files.AC-08
REQ-F-177design noteWhen a detail under the current summary is read successfully, the system shall write a 206-byte record to the detail unload file consisting of the parent account id (6-byte packed) followed by the 200-byte detail image.AC-07
REQ-F-178design noteWhen reading the next detail under the current summary reports no more details ('GE'), the system shall stop reading details for that summary, display 'CHILD SEG FLAG GE : ' with the end flag, and go on to the next summary.AC-09
REQ-F-179error handlingIf reading a detail returns a status other than blank or 'GE', then the system shall display 'GNP CALL FAILED :' with the status and 'KFB AREA IN CHILD:' with the key feedback, display 'IMSUNLOD ABENDING ...', and end with return code 16 without closing the files.AC-10

Open questions

  • SME-272 Should the pending-authorization unload be a full backup of all pending authorizations, or was it meant to exclude or purge authorizations older than a set number of expiry days? The expiry-days and checkpoint settings exist but are never read. (Authorization operations manager)
  • SME-302 When the pending-authorization unload reads the authorization details under a summary, under what conditions is each detail record written to the child (detail) unload file? (Authorization domain team)
  • SME-303 Summaries whose account number is not numeric are skipped, along with all their details, and nothing reports or counts them. Should the new unload report or reconcile the summaries it skips? (Authorization domain team)
  • SME-304 Should the new extract keep the exact fixed record layouts of the root (summary) and child (detail) unload files, so downstream consumers keep working? (Data migration team)
  • SME-305 What goes into the root (summary) unload file, and when is a summary record written to it? For example, is a summary with a non-numeric account number still written? (Authorization domain team)
  • SME-306 What condition ends the processing of a summary's authorization details? For example, which retrieval status marks the end of the details? (Authorization domain team)
  • SME-307 When reading a summary or detail returns an error status (anything other than success or end of data), should the run fail, skip the record, or report it? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-308 Are the 'second extract file' for detail records and the 'authorization child unload file' the same output? (Batch operations team)
  • SME-309 The legacy unload job runs with a fixed database batch configuration ('DLI,PAUDBUNL,PAUTBUNL,,,,,,,,,,,N'). Does any part of it have business meaning that the new unload must keep? (Platform migration team)
  • DEF-028 Is this intended? A summary whose account id is not numeric is dropped from the unload silently, together with all its details. No message is shown and nothing is counted, so the unload files can be incomplete without anyone knowing. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-086 Is this intended? File status is not checked after any WRITE to OUTFIL1 or OUTFIL2, so a failed write (for example, the file runs out of space) would not stop the job and records could be lost. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-167 Is this intended? On a database read failure the program ends with return code 16 without closing the unload files. The output files can be left partly written, and nothing undoes the work already done. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The export reads summaries one after another in storage order until there are none left, and finishes each summary (including its details) before moving to the next. A streaming or paged ordered scan is fine; loading everything into memory is not required. Retrieve next summary and process its details
  • Each summary goes to the summary export file as its full 100-byte record image, unchanged, so the file can be reloaded as it is. If the new store changes the summary layout, an explicit fixed 100-byte export format must be defined to keep compatibility. Unload output layout links each detail to its parent account
  • End of summaries is the normal finish: close both export files and end the job successfully. Stop at end of authorization summaries
  • Each detail goes to the detail export file as a 206-byte record: the parent account id (6-byte packed decimal) followed by the 200-byte detail image. The account prefix is what links each detail back to its summary on reload, so it must always be present. Extract next authorization detail record
  • Running out of details for the current summary is normal: log 'CHILD SEG FLAG GE : ' with the end flag and continue with the next summary, without treating it as an error. Traverse details of current summary
21. Run the unload jobs and manage unload filesdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 10 criteria

Defines how the pending authorization unload jobs run and what happens to their output files, so operations can rely on the outcome. Files are kept or removed according to how the job ended, and failure to open an output file stops the job with return code 16. A failure to close a file is reported but must not change the job's result.

As an operations analyst, I want the pending authorization unload jobs to run against the database and handle their output files predictably, so that unload files are opened, closed, kept or removed consistently with how the job ended.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data. rec/No domain/CardAuthorizationandFraudManagement#21

Design notes

  • Needs a scheduled batch job running the summary-and-detail unload (DBUNLDGS in the legacy) with read-only, shared access to the pending authorization data and its index, so online use is not blocked while it runs. Run authorization database batch program
  • This job writes to two existing output files, the summary file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.GSAM) and the detail file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.GSAM). No other process may write to them during the run, and they are kept whether the job succeeds or fails, so downstream steps must check the job status before using them. Run authorization database batch program
  • Needs a second scheduled export job (PAUDBUNL in the legacy) that reads the pending authorization data and its index with shared, read-only access and writes summaries to the first output file and details to the second. Unload pending authorization database in batch
  • The job creates a new summary export file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.FILEO) of fixed 100-byte records. It is published or registered only when the job succeeds and is deleted when the job fails, for example by writing to a temporary location and renaming it on success. Create the root authorization unload file
  • The job creates a new detail export file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.FILEO) of fixed 206-byte records. It is published only when the job succeeds and deleted when the job fails, the same way as the summary file. Create the child authorization unload file

1. Build screen map copybooksdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Turns each screen definition into a shared field-layout definition that the programs serving that screen use, and keeps a build listing for it. It is a developer build step, not a business function. It must always regenerate the layout from the current screen source, so a program and its screen never disagree on fields.

As a CardDemo developer, I want each screen map's symbolic map generated into the copybook library, so that programs can use the screen's field layout.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#1

2. List card master recordsdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 9 rules · 10 criteria

A read-only batch listing of every card on the card master, in card-number order. Operations staff use it to review card records. It must never change a card, must print each card exactly once with nothing after the last one, and must stop with a clear error rather than produce a partial listing when the file cannot be opened, read or closed.

As an operations user, I want a listing of every card on the card master file, so that I can review card records without changing them.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, reporting_only. rec/Unassigned-Programs#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-003design noteWhen the READCARD job runs, the system shall run the card master reader program (CBACT02C) with shared read access to the card master file AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDATA.VSAM.KSDS (CARDFILE), sending its messages and printed output to the job output listing (SYSOUT, SYSPRINT).AC-01
REQ-F-004formattingWhen the card listing job (READCARD) runs, the system shall print 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C', then each card record from the card master file once, in ascending card-number order, then 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C', opening the file for reading only so that no card is changed.AC-02, AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-005design noteWhen a read of the card master file returns status '00', the system shall treat the read as successful and print the record.AC-05
REQ-F-006design noteWhen a read of the card master file returns status '10' (end of file), the system shall stop reading, print nothing for that read and end the listing normally, so that no blank or repeated record appears after the last card.AC-06, AC-07

REQ-F-009error handlingIf closing the card master file returns any file status other than '00', then the system shall print 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE', 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the 4-digit status, and 'ABENDING PROGRAM', then abend with code 999.AC-10

Card master read outcome

Card master read file statusCard Listing actionRule
'00'Treat read as successful and print the recordrec/claude:claude/RULE-069/1

Open questions

  • SME-010 The cross-reference and customer listings print every record twice. Does anything rely on that, or should each record be printed once? (Batch operations)
  • DEF-097 Is this intended? Each record is displayed twice, once in the read paragraph and once in the main loop; CBACT02C has the same read-paragraph display commented out, suggesting the duplicate is debug output left in by mistake. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A scheduled or on-demand report job that reads the card store through a read-only connection, so it can run while online users are working. Its progress messages and the listing go to the job's log or report output. Run the card master reader
  • Each successful fetch of the next card in the ordered read is written to the report. The new application needs a sequential read of all cards, ordered by card number. Read outcome classification: success, end of file, or fatal error
  • When the cursor or stream runs out of cards, the job ends normally. End of data is the normal way to finish, not an error. Read outcome classification: success, end of file, or fatal error
  • Iterate until there are no more rows and write nothing for the empty fetch, so no blank or repeated line appears after the last card. List every card record until exhausted
3. List card cross-reference recordsdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

A read-only batch listing of every card cross-reference record, showing which card belongs to which account and customer. Operations staff use it for review. It must never change the cross-reference. The legacy job prints each record twice, which the team must either keep or consciously drop.

As an operations user, I want a listing of every card cross-reference record, so that I can review which cards link to which accounts and customers without changing the master.

5. Verify daily transaction cards and accountsdraft · service · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 11 criteria · 1 gap

A batch check of the day's transactions. For each one it looks up the card on the card cross-reference and then looks up the linked account, reporting cards and accounts that cannot be found. Operations staff use it to see bad transactions before posting. It must never quietly pass an unknown card, and it must stop the whole run at once if any file cannot be opened, read or closed.

As an operations user, I want each daily transaction's card checked against the card cross-reference and its account looked up, so that transactions with unknown cards or accounts are reported.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches card_data, personal_data. rec/Unassigned-Programs#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-015design noteThe system shall read the daily transaction file one record at a time from the start, show each record read, and verify its card, stopping when the file reports end of file (status '10').AC-01
REQ-F-016error handlingIf reading the daily transaction file returns a status other than '00' or '10', then the system shall show 'ERROR READING DAILY TRANSACTION FILE' and the file status ('FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the code), then abend with code 999.AC-06
REQ-F-017business ruleWhen a daily transaction has been read, the system shall look up the transaction's card number, by exact match, in the card cross-reference file to find the linked account and customer.AC-02
REQ-F-018formattingWhen the card number is found in the cross-reference, the system shall show 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF XREF' with the card number, account ID and customer ID, and then look up the linked account on the account master.AC-07
REQ-F-019business ruleIf the card number is not in the cross-reference, then the system shall show 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOR XREF' and 'CARD NUMBER <card> COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-<transaction ID>', and shall not look up any account for that transaction.AC-08
REQ-F-020business ruleWhile the transaction card was found in the card cross-reference, when the account lookup for the cross-referenced account id in the account store fails (not found), the system shall display 'ACCOUNT <account id> NOT FOUND'.AC-03
REQ-F-021error handlingIf any of the six files fails to open (status not '00'), then the system shall show the open error for that file ('ERROR OPENING DAILY TRANSACTION FILE', 'ERROR OPENING CUSTOMER FILE', 'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE', 'ERROR OPENING CARD FILE', 'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT FILE' or 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE') and the file status, then abend with code 999 before processing any transaction.AC-09
REQ-F-022error handlingIf any file fails to close at the end of the run (status not '00'), then the system shall show the close error for that file and its file status, then abend with code 999.AC-04
REQ-F-023historical artifactThe system shall open the customer, card and transaction files at start and close them at end even though it never reads or writes them, so that a missing customer, card or transaction file still stops the job.AC-05
REQ-F-024formattingWhen a file status is not numeric or starts with '9', the system shall show it as 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the first character and the binary value of the second character as three digits, and otherwise shall show 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN00' followed by the two-digit status.AC-10, AC-11

Open questions

  • SME-036 When a daily transaction's card number is not in the card-to-account cross-reference, the batch flags it and skips it. What else should happen to that transaction? For example, should it be rejected to a file, reported, or retried? (Business analyst)
  • SME-037 How important is the rule that every daily transaction's card must exist in the card-to-account cross-reference? Is it critical to the system's core purpose, or a rule that is costly if it goes wrong? (Business analyst / card operations owner)
  • SME-038 When a daily transaction's card is verified against the cross-reference, what processing should that transaction then receive in the card verification step? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-034 Is this intended? When the end of the daily file is reached, the loop body still runs the cross-reference lookup (and account lookup) on the last record read, so the final transaction is verified twice and any 'COULD NOT BE VERIFIED' message for it is repeated. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-072 Is this intended? The end-of-file check guards only the record display; on the final pass after end of file the card and account lookups still run on the previous record, so the last transaction is processed twice. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-181 Is this intended? If the daily transaction file fails to close, the batch shows 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' and the customer file's status instead of the daily transaction file's, so the wrong file is reported. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A batch job that streams the day's transaction feed in file order, one record at a time. It logs each record and runs card verification on it, and it finishes when the feed is used up. End of feed is the normal way to finish. Process each daily transaction card
6. Build and deploy online programsdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 7 criteria · 2 gaps

The build-and-deploy steps for online programs: compile, register the program's database access, and make the online system load the new version. Build engineers use it. It must never deploy or bind a program whose build failed, and online users must pick up the new version only after a successful build.

As a CardDemo build engineer, I want online programs compiled, bound to the database and refreshed in the online region, so that online users run the newly built code.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/Unassigned-Programs#6

Open questions

  • DEF-142 Is this intended? The bind step loads its Db2 libraries from the fixed names OEM.DB2.DAZ1.SDSNEXIT and OEMA.DB2.VERSIONA.SDSNLOAD. It ignores the SSID and SDSNLOAD settings the procedure takes, so a build against any subsystem other than DAZ1 still uses DAZ1's libraries. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-147 Is this intended? BINDPL tests only BINDPK's return code. When the link-edit fails inside the IF RC = 0 block, BINDPK is bypassed and its test is ignored, so the plan is rebound even though the build failed. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A CI/CD deploy step. When the build succeeds (warnings allowed, no errors), roll out the new version to the running online service, for example by a rolling restart or a hot reload, so new requests use the new code. Refresh the program in the online region
  • Run this only when every build step succeeded without warnings. It registers or refreshes the program's database access against the CARDDEMO schema, replacing the previous version, using read-committed isolation. In a modern stack this is usually a schema migration or a step that grants database permissions, gated on a green build. Bind the CardDemo database package
  • After the database access step succeeds (warnings allowed), refresh the application-level database binding that covers all CARDDEMO programs. Keep the existing permissions and use the same CARDDEMO schema and isolation. In a modern stack this is the deploy-time database configuration or role setup, and it must not reset grants. Rebind the application plan over packages
7. Convert date formatsdraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 7 rules · 6 criteria

A shared routine that converts dates between YYYYMMDD and YYYY-MM-DD for other batch programs, for example to write the account reissue date in the account extract. It must reject any request it cannot interpret with 'INVALID INPUT' rather than return a wrong date.

As a calling batch program, I want dates converted between YYYYMMDD and YYYY-MM-DD, so that account dates can be written in the format required.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#7

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-029business ruleIf the input type is not '1' or '2', then the system shall reject the request with the message 'INVALID INPUT' in the error message (COERMSG) and leave the output date unchanged.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-030design noteWhen the input type is '1' (YYYYMMDD) and the requested output type is not '2', the system shall return the date as YYYY-MM-DD, inserting dashes between year, month and day.AC-03
REQ-F-031business ruleIf the input type is '1' and the input date already has a dash as its fifth character or the requested output type is '2', then the system shall reject the request with the message 'INVALID INPUT'.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-032design noteWhen the input type is '2' (YYYY-MM-DD) and the requested output type is not '1', the system shall return the date as YYYYMMDD, taking the year from characters 1-4, the month from 6-7 and the day from 9-10, without checking that the input contains dashes.AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-033business ruleIf the input type is '2' and the requested output type is '1', then the system shall reject the request with the message 'INVALID INPUT'.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-034design noteWhen the account extract writes each account record, the system shall convert the account reissue date from YYYY-MM-DD to YYYYMMDD (input type '2', output type '2') using the date format conversion routine.AC-06

Design notes

  • A pure, reusable date-formatting function that takes YYYYMMDD and returns YYYY-MM-DD. Build it as a library function, not a separate service call. Route request by input date type
  • The same library function going the other way: it takes YYYY-MM-DD and returns YYYYMMDD by position (characters 1-4, 6-7 and 9-10). It does not validate the separators. Route request by input date type
  • The account extract calls the date-formatting function on the reissue date for every record it writes, so the extract carries the date as YYYYMMDD. Account date format conversion between YYYYMMDD and YYYY-MM-DD
8. Pause a batch jobdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 5 criteria

A batch utility step that pauses a job for a given time in hundredths of a second and then carries on, so that the scheduler can pace jobs. It must wait for the time asked and always end with success (return code 0).

As a batch scheduler, I want a job step that waits for a set time, so that jobs can be paced.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#8

Open questions

  • SME-089 Which batch jobs use the wait step, and how long a pause do they rely on? Should a missing or non-numeric pause value make the step fail instead of waiting for an unpredictable time? (Batch operations lead)
  • DEF-143 Is this intended? After restoring the caller's registers, the routine writes X'FF' into the caller's save area. The author's own comment questions whether this is needed, and nothing reads it. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A configurable delay step in the job scheduler or workflow. It reads an 8-digit duration in hundredths of a second (for example 00000500 = 5 seconds), sleeps for that long, and always exits successfully. In most schedulers this is a built-in wait or delay task rather than custom code. Batch job pause duration in centiseconds
  • The timer behind the delay step: suspend for the given number of hundredths of a second and then return success to the caller. A standard sleep in the job runtime covers it. Start caller-specified interval wait
9. Retain dataset generationsdraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 9 rules · 10 criteria

Keeps a limited, rolling history of the batch files: daily transactions, rejects, combined and system-generated transactions, backups and the transaction report. Old copies are removed automatically. Operators rely on it to keep the most recent runs (five, or ten for the report history set-up) and never to let old copies pile up. Re-running the set-up must be harmless.

As a CardDemo operator, I want transaction, reject, report and backup files kept as limited generation groups, so that recent history is kept and old generations are removed automatically.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#9

Open questions

  • SME-279 Two definitions of the transaction report history set different limits (10 generations vs 5). Which limit applies, and should generations that roll off be erased? (Batch operations team)
  • DEF-144 Is this intended? The step comment says it deletes the transaction master VSAM file, but the step only defines the report generation group; the comment was copied from another job. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-146 Confirm this is deliberate: After each define the job resets any return code 12 to 0, not only 'already defined', so a genuine severity-12 failure to create a generation group is hidden and the job still ends with return code 0. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Keep each run's daily rejected-transactions output as a versioned object, for example a dated file in object storage. A retention policy keeps the latest 5 and deletes older ones. Retain five generations of daily rejects
  • Version the combined transaction file (the transaction backup merged with system-generated transactions) per run. Keep the latest 5 and delete the data of older versions automatically. Retain five transaction report generations
  • Version the daily transaction input per run. Keep the latest 5 and delete older versions automatically. Retain five transaction report generations
  • Version the transaction report per run and keep the latest 5. Another set-up job defines the same report history with 10 versions (rule bc474731…), so the team must choose one limit. Retain five transaction report generations
  • A retention policy for the daily transaction report that keeps the latest 10 versions; the oldest goes when an eleventh is created. This conflicts with the 5-version definition in the main set-up (rule 1b564856…), so the team must decide which one applies. Retain ten transaction report generations
  • Take a versioned backup of the transaction category balances on each run. Keep the latest 5 and delete older ones automatically. Retain five transaction report generations
  • Take a versioned backup of the transaction master on each run. Keep the latest 5 and delete older ones automatically. Retain five transaction report generations
  • Version the system-generated transaction file per run. Keep the latest 5 and delete older ones automatically. Retain five transaction report generations
10. List the CardDemo dataset catalogdraft · scheduled job · 1 requirements · 1 rules · 2 criteria

An operator report of every CardDemo dataset that exists, with all its attributes, replacing the previous report each time it runs. It must list every CardDemo dataset and must never leave a half-written report behind when the run fails.

As a CardDemo operator, I want a report of every catalogued CardDemo dataset with its attributes, so that I can review what datasets exist.

11. Read transactions by processed timestampdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Gives batch processes a way to read transactions in the order they were processed, by keeping a secondary index on the processed timestamp of the transaction master. Many transactions may share a timestamp. The index must include every transaction on the master.

As a CardDemo batch process, I want an alternate index on the transaction master keyed on processed timestamp, so that transactions can be read by when they were processed.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#11

Design notes

1. Register online CardDemo programs and transactionsdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria · 2 screens

Registers the sign-on program and the admin menu program with the online system so that users can start them: sign-on under transaction code CC00, and the admin menu under CCAD and CCDM. This is set up by operations and is not something users see. It must never leave an entry point unregistered or attached to the wrong program, because then users cannot sign on or administrators cannot reach their menu.

As a system administrator, I want the CardDemo sign-on and admin menu programs and their transactions registered in the online system, so that users can start them by transaction code.

Open questions

  • SME-016 Two transaction codes both open the same admin menu. Should the new system keep both entry points, or is one redundant? (Application owner)
  • SME-017 Does the mainframe 'data location ANY' storage setting need an equivalent on the target platform, or can it be dropped? (Platform architecture team)
  • DEF-151 Is this intended? The job defines admin menu program COADM00C with transaction codes CCAD and CCDM, but no COADM00C exists in the source; the admin menu program is COADM01C with transaction CA00, which app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines, so these definitions point at a missing program. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-152 Is this intended? Transaction CCDM starts COADM00C, which does not exist in the source; the admin menu is COADM01C under transaction CA00, defined in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD. CCDM also differs from the CCAD code given on the program definition. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The sign-on entry point must be set up as part of deployment configuration, such as a route table or service registration. Its legacy code CC00 maps to the sign-on screen, and it must be usable from any node or region (the legacy data location ANY). Keep CC00 as an alias only if outside links or operators still use it. Register the login program with its transaction
  • Register the admin menu as a deployable entry point (a route or service) that answers to the legacy code CCAD. It must be declared in the same deployment configuration as sign-on (the CARDDEMO group), so the two are always released together. Register the admin menu program with its transaction
  • A second legacy code, CCDM, must open the same admin menu. Model it as an alias route or redirect to the admin menu entry point, not as a separate screen. No location restriction is needed (ANY). Register the admin menu transaction
2. Navigate the Admin Menudraft · online · 9 requirements · 10 rules · 15 criteria · 6 screens · 2 gaps

The Admin Menu lets administrators pick a numbered option, 1 to 6, to reach the user-security screens (list, add, update and delete users) and the transaction-type maintenance screens. It must check every entry, reject keys and option numbers it does not support with the exact messages, and pass the session on to the chosen screen. Today the menu does not check that the user is an administrator, so the new application must decide on purpose where that admin-only check sits.

As an administrator, I want to pick a numbered option from the Admin Menu, so that I am taken to the administration function I need.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/UserAccessControl/SystemOperationsandMaintenance#2

Open questions

  • SME-073 What should happen when the administration menu is opened without any information from the screen that called it (for example, return to sign-on)? (Application product owner)
  • SME-074 On the administration menu, where should pressing PF3 take the user? (Application product owner)
  • SME-075 Should the new administration menu keep a way to configure an option as 'not installed'? With today's setup no option uses it. (Application product owner)
  • SME-076 The administration menu has 6 options, but the option field takes 2 digits. Should the new system allow more than 6 (or more than 9) administrative options? (Application product owner)
  • SME-077 Today only sign-on checks that a user is an administrator before they reach the Admin Menu. Should the new system check for an administrator user on every admin function? (Security officer)
  • DEF-019 Confirm this is deliberate: The Admin Menu performs no user-type check of its own; access control depends entirely on sign-on routing admins to it. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-098 Confirm this is deliberate: The 'DUMMY' placeholder check is kept in code although no option in the table is a DUMMY entry, so the not-installed message after it can only appear via PGMIDERR. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Before validating, normalise the option field to a two-digit number: trim trailing spaces, right-align the value and left-pad it with zeros, so ' 3' or '3' becomes '03'. Show the normalised value back in the option field. In a modern form, parsing the trimmed input as an integer and showing it padded to two digits gives the same result; text that is not a number must still fail the option-number check. Normalize entered option number
3. Navigate the Main Menu with access controldraft · online · 14 requirements · 16 rules · 23 criteria · 2 screens · 1 gap

The Main Menu is the home screen for signed-on users. It lists 11 numbered options and takes the user to the chosen function, and PF3 returns them to sign-on. It must never show a menu without an active session, never let a regular user into an admin-only option, and never route an invalid choice anywhere. Its messages must be exact, including the 'not installed' message for the Pending Authorization View when that view is not available.

As a signed-on user, I want to pick a numbered option from the Main Menu, so that I reach the functions I am allowed to use and am kept out of admin-only ones.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/UserAccessControl/SystemOperationsandMaintenance#3

Open questions

  • SME-128 In the main menu, the 'not installed' and 'coming soon' messages cut off the option name differently and differ in spacing. Should these differences be kept or made consistent? (Product owner)
  • SME-129 When the main menu passes control to a selected function, what session information must be passed (for example, the signed-on user's ID and user type)? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-130 Is the rule that menus require an active session, and otherwise send the user back to sign-on, critical to the system's core purpose or costly if wrong? (Business owner)
  • DEF-047 Is this intended? After an invalid option is flagged, the program still runs the admin-only check using the invalid number as a table index (0 or above 11), reading outside the 11 filled entries; it is harmless today only because the error flag already stops navigation. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-164 Is this intended? With no session data the program puts 'COSGN00C' into the origin field instead of the destination field; it still reaches sign-on only because the transfer routine defaults a blank destination to COSGN00C. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The menu needs a 'first display' state and a 'handle input' state held in the user's session. The first request after sign-on, or after returning from a function, shows the menu. Later submits from the menu are read and acted on. A web app does this naturally with GET to show the menu and POST to submit it, inside an authenticated session. Menus require an active session or the user is sent back to sign-on
  • When the menu is reached by navigation, not by submitting the menu form, render a clean menu with no message and no input processing. Then record in the session that the next request from this screen is a submit, which replaces the legacy re-enter flag (context = 1). Menu first display versus re-entry state
  • On submit, act on the action taken. Enter (the submit action) processes the chosen option. PF3 (a Back or Sign out action) returns to sign-on. Any other action shows the menu again with 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'. In a modern UI, map function keys to explicit buttons and reject any unknown action value sent to the server. Menu first display versus re-entry state
  • Normalise the typed option before validating: trim trailing spaces, right-align it into two digits and pad it with leading zeros (for example '7' becomes '07'). Show the normalised number back in the field. Text that is not a number must still fail the option check. Normalise entered option number
  • The menu keeps no server-side process waiting between interactions. After each response, the session (user, user type, origin screen) must persist so that the next submit arrives back at the Main Menu (legacy transaction CM00) with the same session data. Use a stateless request handler with session storage. Menu first display versus re-entry state
4. Send the CardDemo test file by FTPdraft · scheduled job · 2 requirements · 2 rules · 2 criteria

Operations sends the CardDemo test file to a remote FTP folder to prove the outbound file-transfer path works: it signs on as 'carddemousr' and delivers the file as text named 'welcome.txt' into '/ftpfolder'. It must deliver the file under the right name and in text mode, and must never leave the transfer session open. The sign-on details should come from managed secrets, not be written into the job.

As an operations administrator, I want the CardDemo test dataset sent to the remote FTP folder, so that the file transfer path can be exercised.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/UserAccessControl/SystemOperationsandMaintenance#4

5. Back up and distribute the FTP test filedraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Operations backs up the FTP test file to its backup copy, then starts a follow-on job that copies the backup on to a second copy. This keeps spare copies of the test file. Every record must be copied in full, and the follow-on copy must only start after the backup step.

As an operations administrator, I want the FTP test file backed up and the backup copied on by a follow-on job, so that copies of the test file are kept.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/UserAccessControl/SystemOperationsandMaintenance#5

Design notes

  • A batch step that copies every record of the FTP test file into its existing backup file (or object), replacing what is there. It must not stop other readers using either file while it runs, for example by copying to a temporary file and then renaming it, or by copying object to object in storage. Back up the FTP test file
  • Once the backup step finishes, the job must trigger the follow-on job (INTRDRJ2) using its stored job definition, unchanged. In the new application this is a dependency in the scheduler or workflow (backup, then distribute), or an event or message that starts the follow-on job, not a submission of job text. Submit the follow-on job definition
  • The follow-on job copies every record of the backup file into the existing second copy (the legacy '.INTRDR' copy). Like the first step, it must not lock out other jobs reading or writing these files while it runs. Copy FTP test backup to internal-reader dataset
6. Authorize online transaction under the card security profiledraft · scheduled job · 1 requirements · 1 rules · 1 criterion

Security administration adds transaction CT02 to the CARD access profile, so only users allowed under that profile can run it. The result of the change must be recorded in the job output for audit. The change must never miss CT02, never put it in the wrong profile, and never go unrecorded.

As a security administrator, I want transaction CT02 added to the CARD transaction profile, so that access to it is controlled by the card security profile.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, security. rec/UserAccessControl/SystemOperationsandMaintenance#6

User Security Profile Management

1. Sign on to CardDemodraft · online · 15 requirements · 17 rules · 19 criteria · 2 screens

Lets any CardDemo user sign on with a User ID and Password. Both are checked against the user security file without regard to case, and the user is then sent to the menu for their user type. It must never send anyone other than a type 'A' user to the administrator menu, and it must give a clear message for a blank field, an unknown user, a wrong password or a lookup failure. As in the legacy system, failed attempts are not limited or recorded.

As a CardDemo user, I want to sign on with my User ID and Password, so that I reach the menu that matches my user type.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, security. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001formattingWhen the sign-on transaction (CC00) starts with no data passed in from a previous screen, the system shall clear the error state and message and show a blank sign-on screen with the cursor on the User ID field.AC-01
REQ-F-002business ruleWhen the user presses Enter on the sign-on screen, the system shall check the entered User ID and Password and try to sign the user on.AC-02
REQ-F-003business ruleWhen Enter is pressed and the User ID is blank, the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with 'Please enter User ID ...' and the cursor on the User ID field, without reading the user security file.AC-03
REQ-F-004business ruleWhen Enter is pressed with a User ID but a blank Password, the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with 'Please enter Password ...' and the cursor on the Password field, without reading the user security file.AC-04
REQ-F-005business ruleWhen both User ID and Password are entered, the system shall convert both to upper case, keep the User ID for the session, and look the user up in the user security file (USRSEC) by that User ID.AC-19
REQ-F-006business ruleIf no user security record exists for the entered User ID, then the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with 'User not found. Try again ...' and the cursor on the User ID field.AC-05
REQ-F-007error handlingIf reading the user security file fails for any reason other than the user not being found, then the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with 'Unable to verify the User ...' and the cursor on the User ID field.AC-06
REQ-F-008business ruleIf the user is found but the stored password differs from the upper-cased entered password, then the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with 'Wrong Password. Try again ...' and the cursor on the Password field.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-N-001business ruleIf a user enters a wrong password, then the system shall allow another attempt, with no limit on the number of failed attempts, no account lockout and no record of the failure.AC-08
REQ-F-009business ruleWhen the user is found and the stored password equals the upper-cased entered password, the system shall record the session context for the next program: coming from transaction 'CC00' and program 'COSGN00C', the user ID in upper case, the user's type from the user security file, and a program context of 0 (first entry).AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-010business ruleWhen sign-on succeeds and the user's type is 'A' (administrator), the system shall transfer control to the administrator menu (COADM01C), passing the session context.AC-09, AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-011business ruleWhen sign-on succeeds and the user's type is anything other than 'A', the system shall transfer control to the regular user main menu (COMEN01C), not the admin menu, passing the session context.AC-09, AC-10, AC-12, AC-13, AC-14, AC-15
REQ-F-012business ruleWhen the user presses PF3 on the sign-on screen, the system shall clear the terminal, show the plain-text message 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...' and end without starting the sign-on transaction again.AC-16
REQ-F-013business ruleWhen the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 on the sign-on screen, the system shall redisplay the sign-on screen with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.AC-17
REQ-F-014design noteWhen the sign-on screen is shown (first entry, an input error or an invalid key), the system shall wait for the user's next key under the sign-on transaction CC00, passing the CardDemo session data forward.AC-18

Open questions

  • SME-156 The rule for the sign-on program covers only PF3 when the screen is already showing. First entry, the Enter key and other keys are handled under other rules. Which requirements group owns those behaviors, and should any of them also end the session? (Security business analyst)
  • SME-157 The thank-you message on exit has trailing spaces. Should the new system keep the exact padded text, or only the visible wording? (UX / product owner)
  • SME-158 After the user signs off, what should they see: should the session end, should they go back to the sign-on screen, or something else? (Security architect)
  • SME-159 PF3 is accepted on the sign-on screen. What should it do, for example exit the sign-on function? (Business analyst, user security)
  • SME-160 What must happen when a user signs on with the correct password, including any routing based on the user's role? (Business analyst, user security)
  • SME-161 The sign-on flow mentions reporting a 'verification failure', for example an unexpected error reading the user security store, but no rule says when this happens or what message is shown. Should this outcome be specified, and how? (Business analyst, user security)
  • SME-162 Passwords are converted to upper case before they are compared, so matching ignores case. Should the new system keep this? (Security team)
  • SME-163 There is no limit on failed sign-on attempts. Does an outside control (for example RACF or CICS sign-on) already lock accounts out, or should the new system add a failed-attempt limit and a single generic failure message? (Security officer)
  • SME-219 When adding a user, should User Type be limited to specific values, such as 'A' (Admin) and 'U' (Regular)? Today only its presence is checked; is any further check made by the screen itself? (Security officer)
  • DEF-021 Is this intended? Because only the entered password is upper-cased, a password stored with lower-case letters can never match, so such a user can never sign on. The wrong-password branch also leaves the error flag unset, unlike the other failure branches, though nothing reads the flag afterwards. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-163 Is this intended? User Type is not checked against the 'A'/'U' values the screen offers, so an invalid type such as 'X' is stored and later treated as a regular user. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-165 Is this intended? Any user type other than 'A' (including blank or an unknown code) is routed to the regular user menu rather than being rejected. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-176 Is this intended? There is no limit on failed sign-on attempts and no lockout or audit of failures, which allows unlimited password guessing. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • After a successful sign-on, create a server-side session that holds the upper-cased user ID, the user type read from the user security record, the origin (sign-on, transaction 'CC00' / program 'COSGN00C') and a first-entry flag (context 0). Every later screen reads this session to identify the user and decide what they may do. Role-based routing and session context set-up after successful sign-on
  • Whenever the sign-on page is shown again (first visit, an input error or an unsupported action), keep the user on the sign-on step and carry any existing session data forward to the next request. No separate state is needed beyond the normal web request/response cycle. Sign-on screen session lifecycle and key handling
2. Browse the user listdraft · online · 19 requirements · 20 rules · 25 criteria · 5 screens · 1 gap

Gives administrators a list of CardDemo users, ten per page in User ID order. The list can start from a chosen User ID and be paged forward and backward. It must keep the page boundaries and the top and bottom messages correct, so that no user is skipped or shown twice between pages, and it must send anyone without a session back to sign-on.

As an administrator, I want to page through CardDemo users ten at a time from a chosen User ID, so that I can find the user profile I need to manage.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-015business ruleWhen the User List program is started without any session data, the system shall transfer the operator to the sign-on program (COSGN00C).AC-01
REQ-F-016formattingWhen the User List program is entered for the first time in a session, the system shall mark the session as re-entered, clear the screen fields and show the first page of up to ten users from the start of the user file.AC-02
REQ-F-017business ruleWhen the operator presses a key on the User List screen, the system shall process the selection or filter on Enter, return to the Admin menu (COADM01C) on PF3, show the previous page on PF7 and the next page on PF8.AC-03
REQ-F-018business ruleWhen the operator presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF7 or PF8, the system shall redisplay the User List screen with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' and the cursor on the user ID entry field.AC-04
REQ-F-019formattingWhen the selection step completes without transferring control, the system shall start the list at the entered user ID (or from the beginning when none was entered), reset the page number to 0, build the page forward, and clear the user ID entry when no error occurred.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-020formattingWhen a user record is read into a row of the user list page (rows 1 to 10), the system shall show that user's ID, first name, last name and user type in that row.AC-07
REQ-F-021design noteWhen a user is placed in row 1 of the page, the system shall remember that user ID as the page's first user, which PF7 uses as the starting point to page backward.AC-08
REQ-F-022design noteWhen a user is placed in row 10 of the page, the system shall remember that user ID as the page's last user, which PF8 uses as the starting point to page forward.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-023business ruleWhen the operator presses PF8 and a next page is marked, the system shall start from the last user shown on the current page (row 10), skip that user, clear the rows, and show up to the next ten users in user ID order.AC-11
REQ-F-024business ruleIf the operator presses PF8 while no next page is marked, then the system shall show the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' and redisplay the current screen without clearing it.AC-12, AC-13, AC-14
REQ-F-025business ruleWhen a forward page fills all ten rows, the system shall add 1 to the page number and read one user ahead, marking a next page ('Y') if another user exists and no next page ('N') if not.AC-15, AC-16
REQ-F-026business ruleWhen a forward page reaches the end of the user file before ten rows are filled, the system shall mark no next page, add 1 to the page number only if at least one user was shown, and show 'You have reached the bottom of the page...'.AC-17
REQ-F-027error handlingIf the user file cannot be read during forward paging (any response other than normal or end of file), then the system shall show 'Unable to lookup User...' and stop filling rows.AC-18
REQ-F-028business ruleWhen the operator presses PF7 and the page number is greater than 1, the system shall start from the first user shown on the current page, skip that user, and fill the rows from row 10 upward to row 1 with the up to ten users that come before it in user ID order, after clearing all rows.AC-19
REQ-F-029business ruleIf the operator presses PF7 and the list is on page 1 or lower, then the system shall show the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' and redisplay the current screen without clearing it.AC-20
REQ-F-030design noteWhen the operator presses PF7, the system shall mark that a next page exists (next-page flag set to 'Y'), even when PF7 is refused at the top of the list.AC-21
REQ-F-031business ruleWhen a PF7 backward page has filled all ten rows, the system shall look one user further back and lower the page number by 1 if such a user exists and the page is above 1, otherwise set the page number to 1 and show 'You have reached the top of the page...', leaving the page number unchanged if fewer than ten earlier users were found.AC-22, AC-23
REQ-F-032error handlingIf the user file cannot be read during backward paging (any response other than normal or end of file), then the system shall show 'Unable to lookup User...' and stop filling rows.AC-24
REQ-F-033design noteWhen the User List program finishes a screen interaction without transferring elsewhere, the system shall wait for the operator's next key under transaction CU00, keeping the session data including the page number, first and last user shown and next-page flag.AC-25

ForwardAll tenYesAdd 1 to page number; mark next page 'Y'rec/group:claude/RULE-033/3
ForwardAll tenNoAdd 1 to page number; mark next page 'N'rec/group:claude/RULE-033/3
ForwardFewer than ten (end of file)NoMark no next page; add 1 only if at least one user shown; show 'You have reached the bottom of the page...'rec/group:claude/RULE-033/4
BackwardAll tenYes (and page above 1)Lower page number by 1rec/group:claude/RULE-032/3
BackwardAll tenNoSet page number to 1 and show 'You have reached the top of the page...'rec/group:claude/RULE-032/3
BackwardFewer than ten-Page number left unchangedrec/group:claude/RULE-032/3
BackwardFewer than ten-Gap: No rule says what message is shown or what rows are displayed when fewer than ten earlier users are found on a backward page.

Open questions

  • SME-209 On the user list, selecting 'U' (update) or 'D' (delete) against a row currently goes to the same place. Which function should handle update requests, and which should handle delete requests? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-210 After paging back through the user list, what page number should be shown? Should it reset to 1 when there is no next page, or only when it cannot go back any further? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-211 What should happen when the operator presses PF3 on the user list? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-212 What should happen when the user list is opened directly, without coming from another screen? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-213 When searching the user list by user ID, should the list start at the first user ID equal to or after what was typed (a partial match), or show only an exact match? (Business analyst)
  • SME-214 When paging back from a page that has fewer than 10 users before it, should the list go to the true first page (users 1–10) rather than show a partly blank page? (Product owner)
  • DEF-016 Is this intended? PF7 sets the next-page flag to 'Y' before checking whether paging back is allowed, so on a single short page (fewer than 11 users, flag 'N') PF7 followed by PF8 pages forward past the last user, clears the rows and shows an empty list still numbered page 1. Also, if the backward fill reaches the start of the file before ten rows, the page number is not lowered. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Keep the User ID of the first row on the current page as the backward paging cursor. 'Previous page' reads the users whose keys come before this ID, in descending key order. Fill first row and record page start
  • Keep the User ID of the tenth row on the current page as the forward paging cursor. 'Next page' reads users with keys after this ID, in ascending order (keyset pagination on User ID). Fill tenth row and record page end
  • Set the 'next page available' flag to true every time the user pages backward, including when the request is refused at the top of the list, so that 'Next page' is always allowed after a 'Previous page' request. Page backward from first user
  • Keep the list's paging state between requests: page number, first and last User ID shown, and the next-page flag. Store it in the session or as a cursor token passed with each request, so the next action continues from the same position. User list session entry and key routing
3. Select a user to update or deletedraft · online · 5 requirements · 6 rules · 8 criteria · 5 screens · 1 gap

Lets an administrator mark a user on the list with 'U' to open the update screen or 'D' to open the delete screen for that user. Lower case is also accepted. Only the first marked row counts. Any other code is rejected with a message and opens no screen.

As an administrator, I want to mark a user on the list with an action code, so that I am taken to the update or delete screen for that user.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#3

Requirements

REQ-F-034business ruleWhen the operator presses Enter on the user list and one or more of the 10 rows has a selection code entered, the system shall take only the first marked row from the top, saving its selection code and user ID as the pending selection, and ignore marks on later rows.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-035design noteWhen the operator presses Enter and no row has a selection code entered, the system shall clear the pending selection code and selected user ID to blanks so that no update or delete screen is opened, and shall just refresh the list.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-036business ruleWhen the pending selection code is 'U' or 'u' and a user ID was selected, the system shall transfer to the Update User program (COUSR02C), passing the selected user ID with from-transaction 'CU00', from-program 'COUSR00C' and context 0.AC-05
REQ-F-037business ruleWhen the pending selection code is 'D' or 'd' and a user ID was selected, the system shall transfer to the Delete User program (COUSR03C), passing the selected user ID with from-transaction 'CU00', from-program 'COUSR00C' and context 0.AC-06
REQ-F-038business ruleIf a row with a user ID is selected with an action code other than 'U', 'u', 'D' or 'd', then the system shall not open any user screen, shall show the message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D', and shall place the cursor on the user ID search field.AC-07, AC-08

Open questions

  • SME-209 On the user list, selecting 'U' (update) or 'D' (delete) against a row currently goes to the same place. Which function should handle update requests, and which should handle delete requests? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-210 After paging back through the user list, what page number should be shown? Should it reset to 1 when there is no next page, or only when it cannot go back any further? (Business analyst (user security))
  • SME-211 What should happen when the operator presses PF3 on the user list? (Business analyst (user security))

  • SME-215 Should the rule that a row selection on the user list routes to update or delete user be treated as top priority (P0)? (Product owner)
  • DEF-155 Is this intended? A selection code typed on an empty row (no user ID) is silently ignored, with no message. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the list is submitted with no row marked, clear any pending selected action and user held in the session and simply reload the list, so that a stale selection can never open the update or delete screen. Clear selection when no row marked
  • Reset the pending selection (action code and selected User ID) to empty on every submit that has no marked row, before the routing decision is made. Row selection action routes to update or delete user
4. Add a new userdraft · online · 13 requirements · 13 rules · 13 criteria · 4 screens

Lets an administrator add a user with first name, last name, User ID, password and user type, so the person can sign on. It must require all five fields and report the first blank one, refuse a User ID that already exists, and never overwrite an existing user. As in the legacy system, the password is stored as typed (up to 8 characters) and any non-blank user type is accepted.

As an administrator, I want to add a user with first name, last name, User ID, password and user type, so that the person can sign on to CardDemo.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#4

Open questions

  • SME-216 What should PF3 and PF4 each do on the add-user screen? (Business analyst)
  • SME-217 When saving a new user fails for a reason other than a duplicate user ID, what should the operator be told, and how should it be handled? (Business analyst)
  • SME-218 Passwords are stored exactly as the operator enters them. Must the new system hash or otherwise protect passwords before storing them? (Security team)
  • SME-219 When adding a user, should User Type be limited to specific values, such as 'A' (Admin) and 'U' (Regular)? Today only its presence is checked; is any further check made by the screen itself? (Security officer)
