  • DEF-178 Confirm this is deliberate: Passwords are stored in plaintext in the USRSEC file, so anyone who can read the file sees every user's password. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Build one user record from the five validated fields and insert it keyed on User ID, with a uniqueness constraint on that key. The insert must fail, not overwrite, when the key already exists, so that the 'User ID already exist...' path can be detected. Assemble new user record
5. Look up and update a userdraft · online · 3 requirements · 4 rules · 4 criteria · 4 screens · 4 gaps

Lets an administrator look up an existing user by User ID on the update screen and save changes to it. A blank User ID must be refused before any lookup, and an unknown User ID must be reported. As in the legacy system, a save against an unknown User ID ends with 'Unable to Update User...'.

As an administrator, I want to look up an existing user by User ID and save changes to it, so that the user's profile stays correct.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-051business ruleIf the administrator asks to look up a user (presses Enter) with User ID blank, then the system shall show 'User ID can NOT be empty...' with the cursor on User ID and not look the user up.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-052design noteWhen a lookup is made with a non-blank User ID, the system shall clear the name, password and type fields and read that user from the user security file (USRSEC), holding it for update.AC-03
REQ-F-053error handlingIf the administrator saves and the entered User ID does not exist, then the system shall report 'User ID NOT found...' with the cursor on User ID but still try to save, so the last message shown is 'Unable to Update User...'.AC-04

Design notes

6. Open the User Update screen and look up a userdraft · online · 10 requirements · 11 rules · 10 criteria · 4 screens · 1 gap

Opens the User Update screen for an administrator. If a user was picked on the user list, that user is looked up straight away; otherwise the screen opens empty for a User ID to be entered. It must send anyone without a session to sign-on, show the stored details or a clear not-found or lookup-failure message, and let the administrator clear the screen or leave without saving.

As an administrator, I want to open the User Update screen and look up a user by User ID, so that I can see that user's stored details before changing them.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#6

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-054business ruleWhen the Update User program is started without any session data, the system shall transfer to the sign-on program (COSGN00C).AC-01
REQ-F-055business ruleWhen the Update User screen is entered for the first time from another screen and a user was selected there (such as the user list), the system shall clear the message, pre-fill User ID with the selected user, look that user up straight away and show its details.AC-02
REQ-F-056formattingWhen the Update User screen is entered for the first time and no user was selected, the system shall show an empty screen with the cursor on User ID.AC-03
REQ-F-057business ruleWhen the administrator presses Enter on the Update User screen, the system shall look up the entered User ID and show its details.AC-04
REQ-F-058formattingWhen the user is found, the system shall show the stored First Name, Last Name, Password and User Type and the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' in neutral colour.AC-05
REQ-F-059business ruleIf no user exists for the entered User ID, then the system shall show 'User ID NOT found...' with the cursor on User ID and leave the detail fields blank.AC-06
REQ-F-060error handlingIf reading the user fails for any reason other than not found, then the system shall show 'Unable to lookup User...' and log the response codes.AC-07
REQ-F-061formattingWhen the administrator presses PF4 on the Update User screen, the system shall clear User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type and the message, and put the cursor on User ID.AC-08
REQ-F-062business ruleWhen the administrator presses PF12 on the Update User screen, the system shall go to the Admin menu (COADM01C) without saving.AC-09
REQ-F-063business ruleIf the administrator presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5 or PF12 on the Update User screen, then the system shall redisplay the screen with the message 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.AC-10

7. Save changes to a user profiledraft · online · 12 requirements · 12 rules · 13 criteria · 4 screens · 1 gap

Lets an administrator save changes to a user's first name, last name, password and user type, either staying on the screen or saving and leaving. It must require every field and report only the first blank one. It must write the record only when at least one field actually changed, and say plainly whether the save happened.

As an administrator, I want to save changes to a user's name, password and user type, so that the user's security profile stays correct.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#7

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-064business ruleWhen the administrator presses PF5, the system shall validate and save the changes and stay on the Update User screen.AC-01
REQ-F-065business ruleWhen the administrator presses PF3, the system shall attempt the same validation and save as PF5 and then always return to the program that called it, or to the Admin menu (COADM01C) if no caller is recorded.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-066business ruleIf a save is requested (PF5, or PF3 save-and-exit) and the User ID is blank, then the system shall not save, show 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and place the cursor on User ID.AC-04
REQ-F-067business ruleIf a save is requested with a User ID but a blank First Name, then the system shall not save, show 'First Name can NOT be empty...' and place the cursor on First Name.AC-05
REQ-F-068business ruleIf a save is requested with User ID and First Name filled but a blank Last Name, then the system shall not save, show 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' and place the cursor on Last Name.AC-06
REQ-F-069business ruleIf a save is requested with User ID and both names filled but a blank Password, then the system shall not save, show 'Password can NOT be empty...' and place the cursor on Password.AC-07
REQ-F-070business ruleIf a save is requested with all other fields filled but a blank User Type, then the system shall not save, show 'User Type can NOT be empty...' and place the cursor on User Type.AC-08
REQ-F-071business ruleIf several fields are blank when a save is requested, then the system shall report only the first in the order User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type.AC-09
REQ-F-072error handlingIf PF3 is pressed with a blank required field, then the system shall skip the save but still return to the calling screen (or the admin menu), so the validation message is not left on view.AC-10
REQ-F-073business ruleWhen the administrator saves (PF5 or PF3) and User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password and User Type are all filled in, the system shall re-read the stored user, replace each of First Name, Last Name, Password and User Type that differs from the screen, and save the user record only if at least one of them changed.AC-11
REQ-F-074business ruleIf the administrator saves and none of First Name, Last Name, Password or User Type differs from the stored user, then the system shall not save anything and shall show 'Please modify to update ...' in red.AC-12
REQ-F-075formattingWhen the changed user record is saved successfully, the system shall show 'User <user ID> has been updated ...' in green.AC-13

Open questions

  • SME-220 What should PF12 do on the update-user screen? (Business analyst (user security profile management))
  • SME-221 What should happen when the update-user screen is opened directly, without coming from another screen? (Business analyst (user security profile management))
  • SME-222 While an operator is editing a user's details, before pressing PF5 to save, should the new system lock the record, or check for conflicting changes when the operator saves? (Architecture team)
  • SME-223 The update-user screen displays the user's stored password. Should the new system keep showing stored passwords? (Security team)
  • SME-224 When a user record is not found during a save, the error flag is not set, unlike when it is not found during a lookup. Is this difference intended? (Business analyst (user security profile management))
  • SME-225 Please confirm this rule: when a user lookup is requested with a user ID entered and no error flagged, the system blanks the first name, last name, password and user type fields, then retrieves the user record by that user ID. (Business analyst (user security profile management))
  • SME-227 Should the rule that saving a user writes the record only when at least one field actually changed be treated as top priority (P0)? (Product owner)
  • DEF-054 Is this intended? On PF3 (save and exit) a failed validation still returns to the previous screen, so the error message sent is immediately replaced and the user is not told the update was not saved. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-079 Is this intended? The save does not check the result of re-reading the user: if the User ID is not found or the read fails, it still compares fields and tries to rewrite a record it never read for update, so the 'User ID NOT found...' message is replaced by whatever the rewrite returns. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-094 Is this intended? PF3 returns to the caller even when the save fails validation, finds no change or fails to write, so the admin never sees the error message and may think the change was saved. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

8. Delete a userdraft · online · 15 requirements · 15 rules · 16 criteria · 4 screens · 2 gaps

Lets an administrator look up a user and delete them from the user security file, so that they can no longer sign on. Delete acts at once on the User ID in the field, with no separate confirmation and no prior lookup needed, so the screen must show the user's details before delete is offered and must report the outcome clearly. As in the legacy system, the program itself does not check that the signed-on user is an administrator.

As an administrator, I want to look up a user and delete them from the user security file, so that people who should no longer use CardDemo lose their access.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#8

REQ-F-076business ruleWhen the User Delete transaction (CU03) is started with no session data, the system shall send the user to the sign-on program (COSGN00C).AC-01
REQ-F-077business ruleWhile session data is present, the system shall allow lookup and deletion without checking that the signed-on user is an administrator (type 'A'), relying on the program being offered only from the admin menu and user list.AC-02

REQ-F-081business ruleIf the administrator presses Enter with the user ID blank, then the system shall show 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and not look up any user.AC-04

REQ-F-086business ruleIf the administrator presses PF5 with the user ID blank, then the system shall show 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and not delete any user.AC-07

  • SME-228 What should happen when the delete-user screen is opened directly, without coming from another screen? (Business analyst)
  • SME-229 What should PF3 and PF12 each do on the delete-user screen? (Business analyst)
  • SME-230 On the delete-user screen, what should the messages say when a deletion fails and when an invalid key is pressed, and when should each appear? (Business analyst)
  • SME-231 The add-user and delete-user functions do not check the user's role themselves. Is admin-only access enforced elsewhere, such as by system transaction security or the admin menu? And must the new system explicitly check for the Admin role on these operations? (Security officer)
  • SME-232 Should user deletion be treated as top priority (P0) because pressing PF5 permanently removes the user's sign-on record with no soft delete, no copy of the record before deletion, and no audit trail? Should the rule's priority rationale be restated on that basis? (Security officer)
  • DEF-158 Is this intended? On PF5, the delete is attempted even when the read for update found no record (the error flag is not checked between the two steps), so the screen is sent twice and the 'User ID NOT found...' message is likely overwritten by 'Unable to Update User...'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-179 Confirm this is deliberate: The delete program does not itself verify the caller is an administrator; any session with a communication area that reaches CU03 can delete users. (Subject-matter expert)

9. Seed and load the user security filedraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 7 rules · 9 criteria

Builds the user security store from a fixed seed list, so that a fresh CardDemo installation has accounts to sign on with: administrators ADMIN001-ADMIN005 (type 'A') and regular users USER0001-USER0005 (type 'U'), all with password 'PASSWORD'. It must replace any earlier store completely rather than merge into it, and it must not leave a half-built staging set behind after a failure.

As a system operator, I want to build the user security file from a staged seed list of users, so that CardDemo has administrator and regular user accounts to sign on with.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/UserAccessControl/UserSecurityProfileManagement#9

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-091business ruleThe system shall create the staging file AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS of fixed 80-byte records holding administrators ADMIN001-ADMIN005 (user type 'A') and regular users USER0001-USER0005 (user type 'U'), each with first and last name and the password 'PASSWORD'.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-092design noteThe system shall delete any earlier user security staging file first, catalogue the new one when the copy succeeds and delete it when the copy fails.AC-03

Open questions

  • SME-256 When the user security master is loaded from the seed list, what should happen to users that already exist: replace, merge, or fail? What happens on a re-run? (Security administration)
  • SME-257 The seeded users have fixed, shared starting passwords (PASSWORDA, PASSWORDU) stored as plain text. Should the new system keep them, store them protected, and/or force a password change at first sign-on? (Security)
  • SME-258 The rules name two different user security stores as the target of the credentials load (the RRDS file and the ESDS file). Which one, or both, should receive the staged credentials? (Application data owner)
  • SME-259 The user credentials load runs even if building the staging file failed. Should it be skipped in that case, and what should the user security store look like then? (Batch operations)
  • SME-260 When staged credentials are loaded into the existing user security file, should its previous contents be replaced, added to, or required to be empty, and how are duplicate user IDs handled on a re-run? (Application data owner)
  • DEF-156 Confirm this is deliberate: Ten user credentials, including five administrators, are hard-coded in clear text in the job with the same default password 'PASSWORD'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-157 Confirm this is deliberate: Every seeded user, administrators included, gets the same plain-text password 'PASSWORD', and it is stored unencrypted in the job and the security file. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The seed step should be idempotent: remove any earlier seed data before staging, keep the new staging set only if staging completes, and discard it if staging fails. A transaction or a write-then-rename of the seed file gives this. Build user security staging file from seed list
  • Provide a setup or migration job that drops and recreates the user table keyed on an 8-character User ID, then bulk-loads every staged seed record into it. It runs on demand at environment setup, not as part of normal operation. Load user security master from staging file
  • The legacy job also copies the staged records into an entry-sequenced copy of the user file, without regard to whether earlier steps succeeded. The new application needs this only if some consumer reads users in load order. Otherwise one keyed user table covers it, and the copy should be confirmed as unneeded rather than rebuilt. Load staged credentials into user security file
  • The legacy job also copies the staged records into a relative-record (record-number addressed) copy of the user file, without regard to whether earlier steps succeeded. Rebuild this only if some consumer looks users up by position. Otherwise the keyed user table is enough. Load staged credentials into the user security file
